title: Two for One: Privileged Learning for Resource-Constrained Screening
summary: Machine learning systems are often developed under data-rich conditions but deployed when only incomplete information is available. A natural example arises in colour fundus photography (CFP), where both eyes are commonly imaged because they can provide complementary information for ocular disease assessment. Prior approaches that exploit bilateral information either fuse both eyes in a single model or use knowledge distillation to compress a dual-eye teacher into a lightweight student that still requires both images at test time. However, bilateral acquisition may not always be feasible. We thus propose a privileged learning framework in which a teacher model has access to bilateral CFP images during training and learns representations informed by information from both eyes, while the student is trained to transfer this knowledge from the bilateral teacher using only a single-eye image as input. At inference, the student operates exclusively on this single-eye input and does not require the contralateral image. Experimental results show consistent improvements in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve over conventional monocular training, with the largest gains observed for left-eye images for the detection of age-related macular degeneration (0.931 vs. 0.966) and diabetic retinopathy (0.789 vs. 0.836).%, while requiring only a single-eye image at inference. By enabling models to benefit from bilateral information during training while requiring only a single-eye image at inference, our approach may support more reliable deployment in resource-constrained clinical and screening environments.

title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
summary: Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts. We apply a dynamic intervention to steering directions obtained by three different methods: difference-in-means vectors from labeled rollouts, gradient optimization-based vectors, and vectors extracted when models reference an anti-reward-hacking model spec. This dynamic intervention perturbs model representations less than uniform steering vector addition to the residual stream, allowing for more precise edits. We find that we are able to cheaply and significantly reduce reward hacking without correspondingly significant costs to model coherence or capability, and that steering vectors originally extracted from coding environments also generalize to reducing reward hacking in other domains. Our results pave the way towards latent space monitoring and control over realistic production systems.

title: NormTune: Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Reasoning-Intensive Tasks
summary: Full fine-tuning has achieved remarkable success on reasoning-intensive tasks, but it often requires substantial GPU resource consumption. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) provides a promising alternative for reducing this cost, yet we observe a substantial performance gap on reasoning-intensive tasks. In this paper, we present three key observations showing that this gap is closely associated with norm-related under-adaptation, where PEFT produces markedly smaller weight-update norms than full fine-tuning. Based on these observations, we propose Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (NormTune), a simple yet effective strategy that adaptively strengthens insufficiently updated layers according to their weight-update norms. Extensive experiments show that NormTune consistently enhances multiple PEFT methods across challenging reasoning benchmarks. Specifically, when trained on S1K-1.1, integrating NormTune into rank-8 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA yields substantial average accuracy improvements of 24.24\%, 11.33\%, and 16.21\% , respectively, across AIME 2024, MATH 500, GPQA, and AIME 2025. Moreover, NormTune-enhanced rank-256 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA achieve performance comparable to S1 full fine-tuning, with respective average gains of 2.17\%, 0.93\%, and 3.00\% over this baseline.

title: LaVGuard: Selective Decoding for Contextual Value Drift
summary: A content-safe response can still promote priorities that conflict with its task: an assistant may demand compliance when asked to preserve autonomy. We study contextual value drift as a task-relative decoding problem with an explicit allowance for change. LaVGuard separates an authorized ten-dimensional profile from a frozen estimate of the values expressed in the visible prefix. A profile-relative density gate selects when to evaluate candidate continuations; their signed progress determines a logit tilt constrained by both changed-position and cumulative-KL budgets. We establish local surrogate improvement, pathwise budget feasibility, and a bound on response-distribution change. Profile conditioning raises boundary TPR at 5% FPR from .58 to .72. At the same .12 mean intervention ratio, the selection study reports risk-safety scores of .88 for LaVGuard and .72 for position-matched edits. The resulting interface makes task priorities actionable while keeping the extent of intervention explicit and bounded.

title: GRAFT: Restoring the Missing Sampling Interface in Continuous Diffusion Language Models
summary: Continuous diffusion language models generate a whole sequence in parallel, never drawing a single word at any intermediate step; only the final step turns embeddings into text. Models such as ELF now report autoregressive-level quality at a fraction of the sampling steps of discrete-token diffusion models, and this design principle -- no step-wise discretization -- is what their own ablations credit for the gain. We show that this same principle carries a hidden cost: a collapse of the lexical long tail. Measured against held-out human text, ELF's output matches the human rate on common words almost exactly, yet its rarest words appear at only 0.30x the human rate, a gap that does not close from 105M to 652M parameters and that no sampler setting these models expose can reach. A same-size GPT-2, in contrast, spans zero to above the human rate by its decoding rule alone. We trace the difference to what continuous diffusion models lack: with no step that ever draws a discrete word, every step is instead driven by an average over the candidates still in play, and averaging a rare candidate together with the common word competing for its slot lands on the common word. An autoregressive model avoids this because its decoding rule samples one candidate rather than averaging over all of them. We propose GRAFT, a training-free method that grafts this missing choice back onto a frozen model: while the model is still undecided, GRAFT commits the rare words the average would otherwise discard, then regenerates the sequence from scratch with those commitments held in place. Across three ELF scales and on LangFlow, an independent continuous dLLM, GRAFT restores the rare-word share of generated text from 0.42-0.77x the human rate to 0.82-1.10x, a relative gain of 34-109%, and moves the entire word-frequency profile closer to human on every model tested, by 2.7x on ELF-B and 12x on LangFlow.

title: Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction
summary: Multimodal click-through rate (CTR) prediction is central to search systems, where ranking depends on item content, query relevance, and user preference. Existing approaches incorporate content through dense embeddings or coarse discrete IDs, yet effectively integrating fine-grained heterogeneous content with ID-based predictors remains challenging. We propose FineSID, a progressive learning framework that unifies content tokenization, query--item semantic pretraining, and personalized post-training via a shared fine-grained discrete representation. Each stage optimizes an explicit objective while preserving token-level access to content. First, a pretrained multi-scale visual tokenizer and text tokenizers convert heterogeneous content into fine-grained Semantic IDs (SIDs), explicitly aligning them with the ID features. Second, full-parameter semantic pretraining under query--item relevance supervision establishes a robust matching prior, jointly optimizing the interactions of multimodal SIDs and conventional fields within a shared predictor. Third, this initialized predictor is directly fine-tuned with user click supervision to capture implicit personalized preferences. Extensive offline and online evaluations demonstrate substantial gains in both standard CTR prediction and core business metrics. Furthermore, FineSID improves within-product creative discrimination, demonstrating its semantic generalization beyond conventional ID memorization.

title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
summary: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.

title: From AI-Free Gates to AI-First Work: How Engineering Students in India Navigate University Education and Campus Placements Without AI Guidelines
summary: Engineering graduates in India enter a technology sector that is being reshaped by generative AI, yet the route into that sector runs through examinations and campus placement screens that largely exclude AI. Institutions in India have an approved intake of nearly 2.9 million seats in engineering and technology for 2026-2027, but HCI research on how students prepare for AI-mediated work has drawn mostly on Western and East Asian settings. We interviewed 23 students and recent graduates of Indian engineering and computing programmes about how they used generative AI across coursework, examinations and placements, and how they judged their own readiness for work. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we report five themes, covering AI-first workplaces and AI-free placement screens, how participants prepared for placement, how they used AI in coursework, the role of faculty authority and enforcement, and participants' concerns about their readiness for work. Drawing on signaling theory, we discuss what grades and screen scores certify once AI can help produce them, and we offer recommendations for employers, institutions and AI tool designers.

title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
summary: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).

title: State-Dependent Objective Coordination for End-to-End Balance and Navigation
summary: Traditional robotic navigation systems separate mapping, planning, and low-level control through cascaded modules, introducing computational overhead and accumulated latency. End-to-end reinforcement learning offers a compact unified policy that maps onboard observations directly to control actions. However, on inherently unstable platforms such as two-wheeled inverted-pendulum robots, navigation progress and obstacle avoidance can conflict with attitude stabilization in a strongly state-dependent manner. We propose a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for integrated navigation and control. A pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient $β(s)\in[0,1]$ adjusts the relative contributions of balance stabilization and navigation objectives during training, without extra control hierarchies or auxiliary attitude-stabilization controllers, such as proportional-integral-derivative (PID) or linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) controllers. To support zero-shot deployment, simulation training models execution delay, action hold, asynchronous and noisy observations, and dynamics uncertainty. Gradient analysis reveals persistent directional interference and state-dependent variation in the objectives' relative scales. Comparisons with alternative reward-weighting, constraint, training, and control-structure strategies show that PPO+$β(s)$, where PPO denotes proximal policy optimization, achieves 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on the fixed obstacle map and the randomly generated high-obstacle-density map, respectively. Zero-shot hardware experiments further demonstrate bounded attitude behavior and consistent obstacle avoidance using only onboard observations. Training and evaluation code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

title: VeeReview: Measuring Build-Verify Pairs in Agent-Authored Pull Requests from a V-Model Perspective
comments: 47 pages, 9 figures, 11 tables. Under review at Empirical Software Engineering. Replication package: https://zenodo.org/records/22884519
summary: Context: Reviewing a pull request requires verification evidence that addresses the proposed change. Coding agent benchmarks and studies of pull request outcomes do not directly assess this relationship. Objective: We test whether the V-Model's build and verify pairs can measure verification evidence in pull requests and support comparisons between agent-authored and human-authored changes. Method: VeeReview classifies four build and verify pairs using repository signals and a language-model judge. Three pairs use model judgements constrained by deterministic signals, and a rule over the diff and repository tree decides Module Design-Unit Test. We evaluated VeeReview against a 25-pull request reference set labelled by two raters and applied it to 1,454 matched pairs of agent and human pull requests from 741 repositories. Results: VeeReview assigned lower build-only rates to agent-authored pull requests on all four pairs, contrary to the preregistered hypothesis (mixed-effects odds ratios 0.52 to 0.86). Architecture-Integration was not significant. Standardization for linked issues, shipped tests and size reduced matched-rate differences by 34% to 60%, and the rule-decided pair's standardized interval included zero. The instrument did not meet its preregistered calibration criterion: agreement with adjudicated labels was 4% to 60% against a required 80%, and inter-rater agreement was weak (kappa = 0.154). Conclusions: The rule-decided pair shows that a process measure judged by a language model partly reflects how a pull request is presented rather than the verification work behind it. We report the cohort differences as observations made with this instrument, and we argue that such measures need a mechanically decided component and a validated human reference before they can support comparisons of verification practice.

title: From Linear Exact Repair to Mixed-Alphabet Codes: The Bandwidth-Subpacketization Tradeoff of MDS Array Codes
summary:
MDS array codes achieve optimal storage efficiency in distributed storage systems, but their repair bandwidth depends critically on the sub-packetization level. While the theoretically optimal repair bandwidth (i.e., cut-set bound) of a high-rate exact-repair MDS array code is attainable with sufficiently large sub-packetization, the fundamental limits for fixed sub-packetization remain poorly understood. We study this problem for centralized linear exact repair of $h$ failures from $d$ helper nodes over a fixed finite field.
  We show that the rank profile of any linear repair scheme is constrained by two auxiliary mixed-alphabet codes. The first code is formed from the kernels of the helper projections and exists for all repair degrees; the second is formed from their row spaces and applies in the full-helper regime when $d\ge r$. These codes have complementary alphabet profiles, and their size and minimum-distance requirements are forced solely by the MDS property and repair correctness. This gives a unified route from classical coding-theoretic upper bounds to repair-bandwidth lower bounds. As a consequence, we obtain several explicit lower bounds via Singleton, Hamming, Plotkin, and Griesmer arguments, including known bounds as corollaries. We further formulate a Delsarte-type support-enumerator LP for mixed-alphabet codes and give an exact type-compressed implementation. For fixed sub-packetization \(\ell\), this yields a polynomial-time procedure for evaluating the resulting finite-parameter lower bound.

title: VERDICT: Multi-Agent Parallel Modular Verification
summary:
Deductive verification scales to large software systems through modular reasoning, where formal contracts summarize the behavior of individual functions and enable their independent verification. Its central bottleneck is specification synthesis: constructing the contracts required for modular verification. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled automated specification synthesis at unprecedented scale. However, existing approaches remain fundamentally bottom-up, requiring callees to be verified before their callers. This dependency limits parallelism and provides no principled mechanism for resolving interprocedural inconsistencies that propagate across call chains.
  We present VERDICT, a multi-agent framework for parallelizing modular deductive verification of large-scale programs. VERDICT is built on two key principles. First, assumption-based parallel specification synthesis assigns an agent to each function and allows it to proceed immediately using assumed contracts for its callees, enabling verification to proceed in parallel across the program. Second, bidirectional interprocedural conflict reconciliation resolves the inconsistencies introduced by these assumptions: when a synthesized contract contradicts an assumption, agents propagate the necessary revisions both up and down the call graph until the contracts converge. Experimental results on real-world C programs show that VERDICT synthesizes higher-quality specifications than existing approaches while substantially reducing verification time. In particular, VERDICT is the first approach that scales to the complete 20,000-line X.509 parser, ruling out nearly all the potential runtime errors within hours, whereas prior tools like PREGUSS fall far short even after days of execution.

title: SAFTER: Safety-Aware Filtering Through Explicit Recoverability for Robust Reinforcement Learning under Distribution Shift
summary: Learning safe policies that generalize to unseen environments is difficult under bounded actuation, where an unsafe decision may become unrecoverable. Conventional control barrier function (CBF) filters enforce only instantaneous safety and ignore future recoverability. We propose SAFTER (Safety-Aware Filtering Through Explicit Recoverability), which embeds a differentiable, closed-form backup-CBF filter into Soft Actor-Critic training. SAFTER unifies current safety, finite-horizon backup safety, terminal recoverability, and input admissibility into a single differentiable certificate. Its CBF condition yields an exact minimum-intervention projection without iterative online optimization. In quadruped navigation, SAFTER reaches 90% training success with 30.6% fewer transitions than Vanilla SAC and 34.1-35.1% fewer than current-state CBF-filtered SAC baselines. Across unseen simulated environments, SAFTER improves success by up to 42.4 and 61.4 percentage points over the state-of-the-art methods CBF-RL and SEA-Nav, respectively, and achieves 73.3% and 76.7% success on two real-world navigation maps. Ablations identify accurate differentiation through the safety filter as a key contributor to robustness, in which replacing the projection Jacobian with the identity approximation reduces success rate in a High-Shift environment from 61.4% to 6.2%. These results show that recoverability-aware filtering serves as both a runtime safety mechanism and a learning mechanism for sample-efficient, robust policies.

title: Where Does Timbre Hide? Localizing Speaker Information in Speech Signals
summary: Timbre similarity is a key evaluation target for generative speech systems, including voice conversion, speaker-cloning text-to-speech, and zero-shot speech models. When the generated voice does not match the target speaker, the problem often reflects imperfect separation of speaker-related timbre from content, making it important to identify where timbre information resides and which representations still carry it. Using speaker identity as a measurable proxy, we probe frequency bands, phase/magnitude structure, WORLD source/filter decomposition, voiced/unvoiced regions, self-supervised learning (SSL) layers, EnCodec/HuBERT tokens, and a 45-listener test across Mandarin, English, and Japanese speech/singing data. Speaker information is distributed: 1--8 kHz magnitude and vocal-tract spectral-envelope structure dominate perception, above-8 kHz bands remain machine-discriminative, shallow SSL layers expose compact speaker information, and token leakage depends on tokenizer/layer choice. These findings indicate where generation systems should condition on or transform speaker information, and where content, codec, and token pipelines should audit residual speaker leakage.

title: From Augmentation to Synthetic Evidence: Evaluating Generated Chest Radiographs at Dataset Intake
summary: A generated chest radiograph can be useful as declared augmentation, but the same image becomes unsupported evidence when submitted as the record of a real examination. We study this problem by separating three questions: whether an image passes an automated quality check, whether an origin classifier flags it as generated, and whether a trusted record supports the claimed acquisition. In our experiments, Qwen selects up to 20 images from pools of 1,000 existing Cheff-identified or SynthCheX candidates. A receiver evaluates quality with MedGemma and predicted origin with a classifier on frozen DINOv3 features. Quality-based selection raises quality passes from 12 to 19 of 20 for Cheff-identified images and from 8 to 17 for SynthCheX. We find no evidence that selection improves passage through both checks: no selected Cheff-identified image passes both, while uniform, quality, and quality-constrained surrogate selection produce 2, 1, and 2 SynthCheX passes. On unprocessed test images, the origin classifier flags 4,677 of 5,000 SynthCheX images, but it also misclassify 110 of 2,297 NIH (real) images and 568 of 957 genuine images from another collection as fake. Our results further show that JPEG compression reduces SynthCheX-versus-NIH AUROC from 0.987 to 0.841. Even without processing, 152 SynthCheX images pass both pixel checks. These checks can filter submissions, but they cannot verify an acquisition claim. We strongly advocate that source and intended use must be recorded and checked separately for admission of chest radiographs in medical datasets.

title: Cycle structure of best-response dynamics in random bimatrix games
summary: We study the best-response dynamics in games with random payoffs. We consider two-player bimatrix games, with $n$ strategies each. We assume that payoffs come from a continuous distribution, and study the best-response dynamics of these games, after imposing some structure on their payoff matrices. In particular, we focus on symmetric games, antisymmetric games, common-interest games, zero-sum games, and games with independent payoffs. When two players take turns in playing the best response to the opponent's action, they eventually end up cycling through the same sequence of actions. The main focus of the paper is the cycle structure of large random games. In particular, we study the number of cycles, the number of cycles of a certain length, the length of the longest cycle, and related quantities. We show that the structure of the game has an important impact on the typical cycle structure. Our arguments are based on a representation of the best-response dynamics of these games as directed bipartite graphs, and on the cycle structure that arises in them.

title: 5uGUE: Agentic Hardware-in-the-Loop Fuzzing for 5G Devices and beyond
summary: In this paper, we present 5uGUE, a large language model (LLM)-driven hardware-in-the-loop agent, which enables the wireless fuzzing of 5G-enabled devices (such as mobile phones). 5uGUE combines multi-step reasoning with tool-assisted interaction and integrates into the fuzzing pipeline by leveraging specialized tools for internet search, 5G protocol analysis, memory management, and test-case execution. The agent iteratively generates test cases, executes them on targets, collects runtime feedback, and adaptively refines the fuzzing strategy. We evaluate 5uGUE on five commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) 5G devices across six LLMs. The best performing runs for 5uGUE trigger 167 crashes in total (141 novel and 31 unique) within 60 interaction turns (49 to 133 minutes total runtime). In contrast, the best runs for the state-of-the-art baseline (5GHOUL) discovers only 13 crashes in total (10 novel and 6 unique) within 150 minutes. Overall, by integrating LLM-driven agents, 5uGUE demonstrates significantly better crash discovery performance (12.8x total, 5.2x unique improvement). Notably, among the crashes discovered by 5uGUE, MediaTek has confirmed two new high-severity vulnerabilities, with one CVE assigned (CVE-2026-20525), while UNISOC confirmed seven crashes. Finally, to demonstrate that 5uGUE is agnostic to wireless protocols, we also extend it to Bluetooth Classic with only minimal code changes. In our evaluations, 5uGUE finds an average of 6.4 novel crashes and 1.6 unique crashes. In a nutshell, 5uGUE highlights that LLM agents are capable to operate effectively beyond software-in-the-loop settings, extending autonomous vulnerability discovery to the proprietary, hardware-bound systems that affect billions of end-user devices across multiple wireless protocols.

title: SICAF: Time-Varying Focus Bottleneck for Self-Supervised Event-Based Optical Flow with Spiking Neural Network
summary: Event-based optical flow estimation achieves high temporal resolution and dynamic range by exploiting asynchronous events, while self-supervised learning provides an effective solution to the absence of ground-truth labels. Spiking neural networks (SNNs), as brain-inspired models, process information through asynchronous spikes, naturally aligning with optical flow events. However, the temporal irregularity across event streams hinders the compact extraction of spatiotemporal features, while the absence of explicit labels leads to spurious correlations, thereby increasing redundancy within latent representations. In this paper, we propose a novel 'Compactly Compress, Time-varying Focus' training strategy. We present SICAF (Spikes Information Compression And Focus) framework that formulates the learning process as a constrained optimization with temporal modulation. It encourages self-supervised SNNs to extract compact latent representations while preventing over-compression that would discard temporal saliency. To better enable feature selectivity across time steps, we design an estimator with learnable temporal attention, achieving context awareness with cross-time dependencies. Experimental results on several datasets demonstrate that SICAF achieves state-of-the-art performance in self-supervised SNNs, with a 8.14% improvement in AEE on the MVSEC dataset and a 13.49% increase in robustness under white-box adversarial attacks.

title: RiO-DETRv2: Geometry-Aware Uncertainty Modeling Meets Real-Time Oriented Object Detection Transformer
summary: RiO-DETR is the first real-time end-to-end transformer for oriented object detection, yet further localization gains require a more expressive box representation. Although distributional regression has succeeded in horizontal DETRs, extending it to oriented detection introduces geometry-misaligned boundary modeling and topology-inconsistent orientation refinement. We present RiO-DETRv2, a geometry-aware uncertainty modeling framework for real-time oriented object detection. To resolve the geometry mismatch, Object-Aligned Boundary Distribution Refinement represents box boundaries as probability distributions in an object-aligned coordinate system and progressively refines them across decoder layers. For better orientation topology consistency, we introduce Circular-to-Local Angular Residual Refinement that transitions from global periodic search to local fine-grained estimation. Unified OBB Quality-Aligned Learning further aligns classification, boundary and angular refinement with complete-OBB localization quality. Together, these designs improve localization without compromising efficiency, achieving a better balance between speed and accuracy. Specifically, RiO-DETRv2-l/x achieves 53.7/54.1 mAP50-95 on DOTA, outperforming RiO-DETR-l/x by 1.2/1.5 points with nearly unchanged computational cost. Code is available at https://github.com/RicePasteM/RiO-DETRv2.

title: AI-Based End-to-End Automotive Design and Software Development for SDVs
summary: This paper explores the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enable end-to-end automotive design and software development for Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs). The approach emphasizes traceability, consistency, and compliance with safety-critical automotive development requirements. Validation is performed on a centralized vehicle computing platform supporting adaptive cruise control and emergency braking, tested in Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) and Software-in-the-Loop (SiL) environments. We discuss current capabilities, practical limitations, and future directions toward increasingly automated, reliable, and quality-assured automotive software development with minimal human intervention.

title: SimPT: An Automated Simulation Framework for Intervention-Based VLA Post-Training
summary: Human-in-the-loop (HIL) post-training improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies through expert corrections, but costly human supervision and repeated real-robot evaluation limit algorithm exploration and development. We introduce SimPT (Simulation-based Post-Training), a simulation framework that automates intervention-based VLA post-training by integrating policy rollouts, corrective data collection, policy training, and standalone evaluation. To automatically determine intervention timing and recovery strategies, we develop an Agent-Compiled Progress Graph that tracks task progress using privileged simulator state and retains stable snapshots during policy execution. After a rollout fails, a CuRobo-based expert attempts recovery from these snapshots, starting at more advanced task stages and falling back to earlier ones as needed to generate corrective trajectories. We implement and compare four post-training methods, RECAP, HG-DAgger, DPO+SFT, and FlowPRO, across seven RoboTwin manipulation tasks. Relative to a fixed-interval snapshot baseline, the Progress Graph reduces recovery attempts by 75.0% and increases recovery success from 93.4% to 98.9%. Using SimPT, we develop RECAP-CF-LPF, a refinement of RECAP that combines cross-fitting and low-pass filtering of value predictions. This refinement increases the overall success rate from 76.50% to 79.36% in held-out simulation trials. In real-robot HIL post-training, it increases the success rate from 72% to 96% across 25 scenarios of an Ethernet cable-insertion task. These results demonstrate the utility of SimPT for exploring and developing VLA post-training algorithms.

title: Why is AI-generated language so hard to understand?
summary: There is a widespread sense that AI-generated text has recently become harder to understand. In this study, we investigate a set of psycholinguistic features that are known to correlate with human processing difficulty (e.g., object relative clauses, long syntactic dependencies, low-frequency n-grams). Using a novel corpus of AI-generated text across diverse domains, we find that AI models use these difficult features more often than paraphrases generated by round-trip translation. Compared with human writing, all nine frontier and near-frontier models use more inanimate subjects with animate verbs and more low-frequency n-grams, and most also use longer dependencies, more stacked nouns, and more reduced object relatives in conversation; we also demonstrate substantial variation across model families. We propose and test a hypothesis as to why: while human language is optimized for successful communication, AI-generated text is increasingly optimized for other goals like math, code, and reasoning, in which there is a pressure for \textit{information density} rather than successful communication. We provide a proof-of-concept for this hypothesis by fine-tuning a language model under a length penalty, which leads to a divergence from human-like linguistic behavior. Our findings highlight the axes of misalignment between linguistic processing demands in humans and LLMs, and point toward possible remedies.

title: Carving Radiology Reports at Their Evidential Joints: Anatomical Region Sets as Generation Units
summary: Organizing radiology reports into independently generated units offers a way to generate fine-grained clinical content and bind it to visual evidence. However, existing methods typically adopt generation-unit structures not directly specified in natural reports or their annotations, introducing additional modeling compromises. We propose RadCarve, which instead defines generation units directly from the anatomical region sets in existing statement-region correspondences, unifying unit formation with visual evidence selection. RadCarve's planner uses composition-specialized query banks to jointly predict unit existence and region composition from the image, iteratively refining both with regional evidence aggregated according to current membership predictions. The generator independently produces each unit's text conditioned on the joint visual evidence of its predicted region set. Compared with strong baselines, RadCarve improves CXRFEScore by 9.4% in unit generation given region sets and achieves 2.4 times the end-to-end binding F1. It also achieves leading report-generation results on Chest ImaGenome and PadChest-GR, using fewer than one-sixth as many parameters as large-scale baselines.

title: TeachBack: Learning to Teach via Bidirectional Preference Optimization for On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables a language model to learn from a Teacher instantiated from the same model but given access to privileged information, such as a reference solution. We find that access to sufficient privileged information allows the Teacher to generate highly accurate trajectories; however, accuracy alone does not guarantee that these trajectories are suitable for Student learning. Direct access to a complete solution may encourage shortened, reference-conditioned derivations that omit the exploration, verification, and self-correction required to solve problems without privileged information. We introduce TeachBack, a bidirectional preference-learning framework for on-policy self-distillation that learns not only from the Teacher but also how the Teacher should teach. TeachBack shapes the Teacher's generation behavior by controlling the length of the reference-reasoning suffix injected into the prompt and by varying the prompt style. While maintaining comparable Teacher accuracy, it encourages the Teacher to explore and re-solve problems, thereby reducing its reliance on the reference solution. At each rollout refresh, the shared policy generates both a privileged Teacher trajectory and a problem-only Student trajectory. A pairwise preference objective uses privileged Teacher trajectories to improve Student learning, while the reversed preference uses the Student's behavior to shape future Teacher supervision under the privileged condition. Experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning tasks show that TeachBack consistently improves Student performance over existing OPSD methods and related baselines.

title: How Representational Priors Shape Generalization in World Action Models
summary: World action models (WAMs) are shown to substantially diverge under generalization performance based on their generative backbones. We investigate this gap through the representational geometry that WAMs inherit from their backbones and how policy training reorganizes it. Our central hypothesis is that a useful representational prior would structure geometry that separates nuisance information from the in-distribution manifold in advance of training as a policy. We quantify this with nuisance orthogonality; orthogonality of the feature under visual variation outside the empirical in-distribution manifold. Across various image and video backbones, we show that a higher orthogonality from the representational prior is associated with stronger robustness to visual variations after WAM training, enabling policy generalization measurable prospectively for world models. In addition, analyzing the resulting robust WAMs reveals nuisance suppression; relative suppression of feature displacement caused by such variations and robust action generation of the policy. Together, these findings provide a geometric perspective on how the representational prior of the world model shapes the generalization performance of WAMs.

title: SMR: Learning streaming motion retargeting for humanoids from human semantic
summary: Retargeting human motion to humanoids requires preserving motion semantics while accounting for the robot's physical constraints. Kinematic pipelines prescribe a robot trajectory through geometric matching, without establishing whether it can be executed under the robot's dynamics. Prior physics-supervised neural methods train bidirectional full-sequence models on physics-refined kinematic trajectories, remaining tied to prescribed kinematic solutions and requiring noncausal context. We propose SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts. We convert human motion into robot-aware task-space targets for body landmark positions, orientations, and velocities. Physics experts track these targets directly in simulation under contact, dynamics, and actuator constraints. We train a single strictly causal Transformer on their executed state trajectories that complete the motion and pass semantic and physical validity checks. At each incoming frame, the student uses only current and past human observations to generate a robot motion reference for a downstream whole-body controller. Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.

title: TrainBridge: Agentic NPU Training Optimization Guided by GPU Compilation Evidence
summary: We study how to improve training efficiency on Ascend NPUs. In the NPU training programs we study, framework-level compilation optimizations such as operator fusion are only partially applied, leaving fragmented computation and avoidable execution overheads. Profiling-guided tuning can address these inefficiencies, but it often requires costly trial and error. To make training on NPUs more efficient, we propose TrainBridge, an agentic approach for transferring GPU optimization guidance to NPU training. TrainBridge uses the highly optimized execution produced by mature GPU compilation stacks as a task-specific reference for NPU tuning. It extracts optimization intents from the GPU training execution to guide NPU program rewrites and further refines the rewritten program through iterative profiling. Our GPU-to-NPU migration experiments show that TrainBridge achieves an average 1.7x speedup across four workloads covering LLM pretraining, image classification, and vision-language training, and an average speedup of nearly 2.0x across 27 Modded-NanoGPT speedrun records with highly optimized GPU implementations.

title: Conditional Flow Models Convert Epistemic Uncertainty into Apparent Aleatoric Variance
summary:
Conditional Flow Models (CFMs) are increasingly being used in place of deterministic predictors across machine learning, including for tasks that were classically formulated as regression. Given their success in such tasks, we ask the question: what useful information do the conditional distributions produced by CFMs carry beyond what a point predictor would provide?
  We identify a systematic phenomenon: in many natural regimes, CFM samples routinely have larger variance than the true conditional distribution, even in nearly deterministic regression problems. This effect is most pronounced where the model has not resolved the dependence on the conditioning variable, and thus the additional variance can be viewed as converting epistemic uncertainty in fitting the ground truth conditional distribution into apparent aleatoric variance in the generated samples. Through controlled synthetic and real-data experiments, and comparisons with explicit smoothing estimators, we show that the induced variance tracks model underfitting of complex or hard-to-fit targets, and decreases with additional training or data. We provide a theoretical account of the phenomenon in a simplified setting and demonstrate a consequent practical use-case of conditional flow-matching: designing high-coverage predictive sets that cover the ground-truth regression target.

title: LocalAgent: Collaborative Agentic Verification for Fine-Grained Instance-Level Consistency
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general visual understanding, yet they still struggle with fine-grained instance-level consistency verification, where the goal is to determine whether two images depict the exact same physical object under varying viewpoints, illumination, and backgrounds. This task requires both global semantic perception and precise examination of subtle local evidence, since semantically similar objects may differ only in small suspicious regions. To address this challenge, we propose LocalAgent, a collaborative agentic framework that integrates the complementary strengths of a generalist MLLM and lightweight specialist verifiers. The MLLM first reasons globally to identify suspicious local regions, which are then delegated to a Local Evidence Verifier (LEV) toolkit for fine-grained appearance and geometric matching. LEV comprises Local Appearance Consistency (LAC), which estimates appearance similarity under illumination and color changes, and Local Geometric Correspondence (LGC), which estimates spatial correspondence under viewpoint changes. LEV returns structured scalar evidence that the MLLM integrates for the final decision. We further introduce an auxiliary-capped reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) strategy, in which answer correctness dominates auxiliary tool-use and format signals, enabling the policy to learn when verification is necessary. Experiments show that LocalAgent improves mean accuracy by 4.9% over the strongest CoT-RFT baseline while invoking a verifier on only 12.13% of samples and preserving the general multimodal capabilities of the underlying MLLM. The open-source repository is available at https://github.com/Firefly-zoo/LocalAgent-main.

title: Regular Syndrome Decoding Is Easier Than Previously Estimated
summary:
The Regular Syndrome Decoding (RSD) problem is a structured variant of classical Syndrome Decoding and underlies a growing number of efficient cryptographic constructions, including zero knowledge protocols, pseudorandom correlation generators, and MPC in the Head signatures. Although RSD is generally believed to be computationally hard, recent works have shown that algebraic attacks can outperform information set decoding on important RSD parameter regimes.
  Building on this line of work, we revisit the concrete hardness of RSD and show that many widely used parameter sets are substantially easier to solve than previously estimated. This improvement stems from a refined hybrid algebraic attack that exposes and removes a previously overlooked source of concrete complexity: the joint blockwise placement of zero coordinate guesses and syndrome based variable eliminations. Rather than treating the two guessing stages and linear elimination as largely separate choices, our method coordinates them across all regular blocks so that the guessing penalty is balanced while sufficient equations are retained for linearization. This gives a systematic block balancing principle for the entire guess reduce solve pipeline.
  We reassess several RSD based applications, including Ferret, Wolverine, and committed VOLE. Our estimates place at least one parameter set per application below its 128 bit target, with losses approaching 67 bits. On PCG benchmarks, we improve previous best attack costs by up to 29.77 and 25.91 bits over non binary and binary fields, respectively. Moreover, for the revised 128 bit PCG parameter sets of Liu et al. evaluated here, estimated attack costs are all below $2^{111}$ field operations. These results substantially revise the concrete security landscape of RSD and indicate that several existing parameter choices overestimate the hardness of their underlying RSD instances.

AI.title_translation: 正则伴随式译码比以往估计的更容易
AI.tldr: 本文提出改进的混合代数攻击，发现正则伴随式译码（RSD）硬度被严重高估，导致Ferret和Wolverine等协议的安全强度大幅跌破128比特目标（最高降级达67比特）。
AI.motivation: 重新评估广泛应用于高效密码协议中的正则伴随式译码（RSD）问题的实际计算硬度，解决此前评估中因忽视分块猜测与消元协同布局而高估安全性这一问题。
AI.method: 提出一种改进的混合代数攻击方法，建立了贯穿“猜测-约简-求解”全流程的系统性分块平衡原则（block balancing principle）。该方法协同优化所有正则分块中的零坐标猜测与伴随式变量消元，使得在平衡猜测代价的同时，为后续线性化阶段保留足够的有效方程。
AI.result: 对Ferret、Wolverine和committed VOLE等应用进行重新评估后，发现每个应用至少有一套参数实际安全强度低于128比特预设目标，最大安全性降级接近67比特；在PCG基准测试中，分别将非二元域和二元域上的最佳攻击代价降低了最多29.77比特和25.91比特；对Liu等人修正的128比特PCG参数集的攻击代价均低于$2^{111}$次域运算。
AI.conclusion: 本文从根本上修正了RSD的具体安全评估现状，表明当前多种实际密码学应用中的参数设计严重高估了底层RSD问题的计算硬度。
AI.translation: 正则伴随式译码（RSD）问题是经典伴随式译码的一种结构化变体，是零知识证明、伪随机关联生成器以及MPC-in-the-Head签名等日益增多的高效密码构造的基石。尽管人们普遍认为RSD在计算上是困难的，但近期的研究表明，在重要的RSD参数区间内，代数攻击的表现可以超越信息集译码。在这一系列工作的基础上，我们重新评估了RSD的具体硬度，并证明许多广泛使用的参数集其实际求解难度显著低于此前的估计。这一改进源于一种更精细的混合代数攻击，它发现并消除了一个以往被忽视的具体复杂度来源：零坐标猜测与基于伴随式的变量消元在各分块上的联合布局。我们的方法并没有将两阶段猜测与线性消元视为基本独立的选择，而是在所有正则分块中统筹协调它们，从而在保留足够方程以供线性化的同时平衡猜测惩罚。这为整个“猜测-约简-求解”流水线提供了一种系统性的分块平衡原则。我们对多种基于RSD的应用（包括Ferret、Wolverine和committed VOLE）进行了重新评估。我们的估算显示，每个应用中均至少有一套参数低于其128比特的安全目标，安全性损失接近67比特。在PCG基准测试中，针对非二元域和二元域，我们分别将此前最优的攻击代价降低了最多29.77比特和25.91比特。此外，对于本研究所评估的Liu等人修订的128比特PCG参数集，估计的攻击代价均低于2^111次域操作。这些结果实质性地改写了RSD的具体安全图景，并表明现有的若干参数选取高估了其底层RSD实例的硬度。
AI.summary: 本文针对密码学中重要的正则伴随式译码（RSD）问题展开深入研究，提出了一种改进的混合代数攻击。该方法通过全局协调零坐标猜测与变量消元，提出了系统性分块平衡原则。评估表明，Ferret、Wolverine等主流应用的实际安全强度远低于此前估计，部分参数集的安全强度下降多达近67比特，全面修正了RSD的实际安全格局。
AI.keywords: 正则伴随式译码 (RSD), 混合代数攻击, 分块平衡原则, 伪随机关联生成器 (PCG), 具体安全评估
AI.comments: 创新性：提出了系统性的分块平衡原则，首次将零坐标猜测与基于伴随式的线性消元进行全局协同布局，突破了以往分析中孤立处理两阶段的局限。重要性：该工作对多个主流密码学协议（如Ferret、Wolverine和PCG）的安全参数构成了严重挑战，揭示其安全性损失最高可达近67比特，对未来基于RSD的密码学方案参数设定具有重要指导意义。局限性：摘要中仅展示了具体的攻击复杂度估算结果，未说明是否有大规模完全实现的实验验证。

title: Multi-Scale Latent Temporal Compression Attention and Video-Text Cross Attention Fusion for Video Action Detection
comments: This paper has been accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 33rd International Conference on Multimedia Modeling (MMM 2027)
summary: In video action detection, modeling the temporal dependencies in continuous video streams is crucial. Previous methods based on deep neural networks can perform frame-level video recognition tasks. However, these methods struggle to model dynamic temporal patterns, facing challenges such as redundant frame information, difficulty balancing global and local features, and insufficient fusion of visual and textual features. To address these issues, we propose a video temporal attention module based on the Multi-Scale Latent Temporal Compression Attention, which aggregates continuous temporal sequences into feature representations across diverse temporal scales while efficiently reducing redundancy. We also introduce a Video-Text Cross Attention Fusion module that leverages cross-attention at both latent and standard feature levels, achieving fine-grained fusion between video and textual features to enhance semantic alignment and feature interaction. Experimental results across multiple video recognition benchmarks demonstrate that our proposed methods achieve superior performance compared to existing methods, validating the effectiveness and generalization capability.

AI.title_translation: 用于视频动作检测的多尺度潜在时序压缩注意力和视频-文本交叉注意力融合
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种新的多尺度时序压缩和视文交叉注意力融合方法，显著提升了视频动作检测的准确性和特征对齐能力。
AI.motivation: 现有深度学习方法在视频动作检测中难以建模动态时序模式，面临帧信息冗余、全局与局部特征平衡困难以及视文特征融合不足等挑战。
AI.method: 提出了一种基于多尺度潜在时序压缩注意力的视频时序注意力模块，以及一个在潜在和标准特征级别上利用交叉注意力的视频-文本交叉注意力融合模块。
AI.result: 在多个视频识别基准测试上的实验结果表明，所提出的方法取得了优于现有方法的性能，验证了其有效性和泛化能力。
AI.conclusion: 论文提出的多尺度潜在时序压缩注意力和视频-文本交叉注意力融合机制有效提升了视频动作检测的性能和泛化能力。
AI.translation: 在视频动作检测中，对连续视频流中的时序依赖关系进行建模至关重要。先前基于深度神经网络的方法可以执行帧级视频识别任务。然而，这些方法难以对动态时序模式进行建模，面临着帧信息冗余、难以平衡全局与局部特征以及视觉与文本特征融合不足等挑战。为了解决这些问题，我们提出了一种基于多尺度潜在时序压缩注意力的视频时序注意力模块，该模块将连续的时序序列聚合为跨不同时序尺度的特征表示，同时有效地减少冗余。我们还引入了一个视频-文本交叉注意力融合模块，利用潜在特征和标准特征级别的交叉注意力，实现视频与文本特征之间的细粒度融合，以增强语义对齐和特征交互。多个视频识别基准测试的实验结果表明，与现有方法相比，我们提出的方法取得了优异的性能，验证了其有效性和泛化能力。
AI.summary: 本文针对视频动作检测中时序依赖建模和多模态融合的不足，提出多尺度潜在时序压缩注意力和视频-文本交叉注意力融合方法，有效消除了时序冗余并实现了视文特征的精细化融合。
AI.keywords: 视频动作检测, 时序建模, 注意力机制, 视文融合, 多尺度压缩
AI.comments: 该论文针对视频动作检测中的时序建模与视文融合难题，创新性地提出了多尺度潜在时序压缩注意力和视频-文本交叉注意力融合模块，有效解决了冗余帧和特征对齐不佳的问题，在多个基准测试上展现出优越的性能。

title: ROCOCO: Robust Outline Completion of Occluded Curvilinear Objects
summary: We propose a learning-based generative model for completing curvilinear features under occlusion by environmental obstacles. To this end, we adopt a flow matching-based approach that supports the inpainting of occluded regions with the appropriate curvilinear features. To eliminate the reliance on privileged information about the occlusion a priori, we also train a UNet-based mask prediction model, which can identify regions for inpainting given only the occluded observation. The components of our approach are validated via experiments using procedurally-generated test cases, and the complete pipeline is validated using large public datasets for curvilinear objects. Against off-the-shelf inpainting baselines, ROCOCO is the strongest method by a wide margin when no occlusion mask is given, and is competitive with mask-supervised inpainting when one is, achieving best on full-image error and second only to LaMa on the occluded region, while using a completer of $7.7$M parameters against LaMa's $51$M and Stable Diffusion's $860$M.

AI.title_translation: ROCOCO：遮挡曲线对象鲁棒的大纲补全
AI.tldr: ROCOCO是一种轻量级（7.7M参数）且高效的生成模型，无需预先知道遮挡信息即可精准补全被遮挡的曲线对象。
AI.motivation: 为了解决在环境障碍物遮挡下准确补全曲线特征的问题，同时消除对先验遮挡特权信息的依赖。
AI.method: 采用基于流匹配的生成模型来进行被遮挡区域的曲线特征修复，并训练了一个基于UNet的掩码预测模型，用于在仅有遮挡观测的情况下自主识别需要修复的区域。
AI.result: 在没有给定遮挡掩码时，ROCOCO以很大优势成为最强的方法；在给定掩码时，其表现与掩码监督修复方法竞争激烈，在全图误差上达到最佳，在遮挡区域仅次于LaMa，而其参数量仅为7.7M（相比之下LaMa为51M，Stable Diffusion为860M）。
AI.conclusion: ROCOCO是一个高效且鲁棒的学习型生成模型，能够在无需先验遮挡信息的情况下准确补全被环境障碍物遮挡的曲线对象，兼具出色的性能与极低的参数量。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一种基于学习的生成模型，用于在环境障碍物遮挡下补全曲线特征。为此，我们采用了一种基于流匹配的方法，支持用适当的曲线特征对遮挡区域进行修复。为了消除对先验遮挡特权信息的依赖，我们还训练了一个基于UNet的掩码预测模型，该模型仅根据遮挡观测就能识别出需要修复的区域。我们通过使用程序生成测试案例的实验对方法的各个组件进行了验证，并使用用于曲线对象的大型公共数据集对完整管道进行了验证。与现成的修复基线相比，在没有给定遮挡掩码时，ROCOCO以巨大优势成为最强的方法；在给定遮挡掩码时，它与掩码监督修复方法具有竞争力，在全图误差上达到最佳，在遮挡区域仅次于LaMa，而其补全器的参数量为7.7M，相比之下LaMa为51M，Stable Diffusion为860M。
AI.summary: ROCOCO是一种用于补全被环境障碍物遮挡的曲线特征的鲁棒学习型生成模型。该方法结合了基于流匹配的生成模型和用于识别修复区域的UNet掩码预测模型，无需先验遮挡信息。实验表明，ROCOCO在参数量极小的情况下，实现了优于或竞争于现有主流图像修复基线的性能。
AI.keywords: 曲线对象补全, 流匹配, 掩码预测, 遮挡处理, 生成模型
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种名为ROCOCO的鲁棒大纲补全模型，通过结合基于流匹配的生成模型和UNet掩码预测模型，无需预先提供遮挡信息即可高效补全被遮挡的曲线特征。其创新之处在于参数量极小（仅7.7M）的同时，性能显著优于传统基线，甚至在无遮挡掩码的情况下大幅超越现有方法，具有很高的实用价值和效率优势。

title: Correlated Failures of AI Approval Monitors
summary: Before an AI agent takes a consequential action, such as paying, messaging or changing code, several monitors check it. Their verdicts are combined by aggregating scores or by counting approvals, whatever inputs the monitors share. Monitors that share a base model or a poisoned input, however, may fail together. We borrow the fail-prone systems of distributed computing: lists of monitor sets that may fail together. A rule is safe if it executes no bad action and live if it blocks no good one. We measured twelve small open-weights monitors on payment approval under two pre-registered protocols. Without pre-registration, we also measured three closed frontier models (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon) and the open DeepSeek-V3.2. Every reliable fooling of a monitor into approving a fraud came through an evidence source and reached only that source's readers. Fooling it into blocking a correct payment depended on injection resistance, a monitor's refusal to follow instructions planted in its data. Small models and DeepSeek obeyed such notes. The three closed models ignored them in all but one case, and Opus also resisted persuasion tailored to it. On new data, a rule that counts sources instead of votes blocked 0.9% of correct payments, against 7.4% for the best counting rule, at equal safety. The pre-registered worst-case test failed. One attack left the approvers on a single source, so no rule over the twelve language-model monitors survives every measured attack. Adding a rule engine, which cannot be persuaded, restored the condition for a safe and live rule on the measured attacks. Diversify the inputs, harden the monitors, count sources, not votes.

AI.title_translation: AI审批监控器的相关失效
AI.tldr: AI审批监控器容易因为共享输入或基础模型而发生相关失效，研究表明必须通过多样化输入、加固模型以及计算独立源而非简单投票来保障安全。
AI.motivation: AIAgent在执行重要操作前通常由多个监控器共同审批，但由于共享基础模型或受到污染的输入，这些监控器可能会同时失效，因此需要研究如何应对AI审批监控的相关失效问题。
AI.method: 借鉴分布式计算中的失效系统理论，对12个小型开源模型和4个前沿闭源模型在支付审批任务上进行了预注册与非预注册协议的测试。
AI.result: 实验发现欺骗一个监控器往往通过特定的证据源影响其读者，小模型容易受提示词注入攻击而闭源模型较为抗拒；简单的投票规则表现不佳，而结合不能被说服的规则引擎则能够恢复安全性和活性。
AI.conclusion: 通过对12个小型开源模型及多个前沿闭源模型的测试，论文指出仅依赖大模型投票存在安全隐患，必须通过多样化输入、加固模型以及计算独立源而非简单投票来确保AI审批的安全性。
AI.translation: 在AI智能体采取诸如支付、发消息或修改代码等重要行动之前，会有几个监控器对其进行检查。它们的裁决通过聚合分数或计算批准次数（无论监控器共享什么输入）来进行组合。然而，共享基础模型或受污染输入的监控器可能会同时失效。我们借用了分布式计算中易错系统的概念：即可能共同失效的监控器集合列表。如果一个规则不执行任何坏动作且不阻止任何好动作，则是安全且活性的。我们在两个预注册协议下，对12个小型开源监控器进行了支付批准的测量。在没有预注册的情况下，我们还测量了三个闭源前沿模型（Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6 Astra、Gemini 4 Argon）以及开源的DeepSeek-V3.2。每一次成功欺骗监控器批准欺诈的行为都通过一个证据源发生，并且只触及该源的读者。将其欺骗为阻止正确支付则取决于注入抵抗力，即监控器拒绝遵循植入其数据中的指令的能力。小模型和DeepSeek服从了此类便签。三个闭源模型在除一种情况外的所有情况下都忽略了它们，Opus还抵御了针对它的说服。在新数据上，计算源而不是投票的规则在保持相同安全性的情况下，仅阻止了0.9%的正确支付，而最佳投票规则这一比例为7.4%。预注册的最坏情况测试失败了。一次攻击将审批者留在了单个源上，因此没有一个规则能够在所有测量的攻击中幸存下来。添加一个无法被说服的规则引擎，恢复了在测量攻击下安全且活性规则的条件。结论是：使输入多样化，加固监控器，计算源，而不是投票。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了AI审批监控器在面对共享输入或基础模型时的相关失效问题，借鉴分布式计算理论评估了多种模型的审批性能，并提出通过多样化输入、加固监控器以及计算独立源（而非简单投票）来提升AI动作审批的安全与活性。
AI.keywords: AI审批监控, 相关失效, 分布式计算, 提示词注入, 安全性与活性
AI.comments: 该论文将分布式计算中的失效系统理论引入AI审批监控领域，揭示了共享基础模型或输入源带来的相关失效风险，对AI安全治理具有重要的实践意义。

title: Resuming Vision-Language Inference across Onboard Interruptions
summary:
Executing vision-language models (VLMs) aboard low-Earth orbit satellites enables flexible processing of observation data without first downlinking it to the ground. On commercial off-the-shelf payloads, however, a request may span multiple execution windows: power and thermal constraints, fault-triggered reboots, and competing payload demands can interrupt inference before it completes. Each shutdown discards volatile activations and KV caches, forcing an unprotected request to repeat work after restart.
  We present OrbitWeaver, a framework that preserves VLM inference progress across onboard interruptions through coordinated checkpointing and recovery. Its phase-aware checkpointing selects recovery boundaries according to the state lifetimes and computational characteristics of vision encoding, language-model prefill, and decoding, balancing storage traffic against recomputation. Its dependency-aware dynamic recovery schedules restoration from partially completed states across the layer and token-chunk dimensions. By overlapping checkpoint and weight reads with recomputation, it reduces restart latency; the recovery planner computes an optimal execution order under its scheduling model within 100 ms.
  Experiments on satellite payload hardware using on-orbit telemetry traces show up to a 4.07-fold end-to-end speedup and a 3.56-fold reduction in SSD write volume over the evaluated baselines. A 72-hour deployment on two low-Earth orbit satellites demonstrates that OrbitWeaver retains inference progress and resumes execution across repeated bus-enforced shutdowns.

AI.title_translation: 在星载中断恢复跨任务的视觉语言模型推理
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为OrbitWeaver的框架，通过协调检查点和恢复机制，解决了低轨卫星上视觉语言模型推理因电源、热量或故障中断而丢失进度的问题，大幅提升了推理效率和鲁棒性。
AI.motivation: 在低轨卫星上执行视觉语言模型（VLM）时，功率与热限制、故障重启以及竞争性有效负载需求等常会导致推理在完成前被中断，传统的无保护请求在重启后需要重复计算，丢弃了易失性激活和KV缓存，因此需要一种能够在中断间恢复VLM推理进度的机制。
AI.method: 提出OrbitWeaver框架，包含阶段感知检查点机制（根据不同计算阶段选择恢复边界以平衡存储流量与重计算）和依赖感知动态恢复调度（在层和Token块维度调度部分完成状态的恢复，并重叠读写与重计算以降低延迟）。
AI.result: 在卫星载荷硬件和在轨遥测轨迹上的实验表明，相比评估的基线，实现了高达4.07倍的端到端加速以及3.56倍的SSD写入量减少；在两颗低轨卫星上进行72小时的部署证明了其有效性。
AI.conclusion: OrbitWeaver能够有效地在低轨卫星的多次总线强制关机下保持VLM推理进度并恢复执行，相比基线方法实现了显著的端到端加速和SSD写入量减少。
AI.translation:
在低轨卫星上执行视觉语言模型（VLMs）可以在无需先下传到地面的情况下灵活处理观测数据。然而，在商用现货载荷上，一个请求可能跨越多个执行窗口：功率和热约束、故障触发的重启以及竞争的有效负载需求可能会在推理完成前中断它。每次关机都会丢弃易失性激活和KV缓存，迫使未受保护的请求在重启后重复工作。
我们提出了OrbitWeaver，这是一个通过协调检查点和恢复来跨星载中断保留VLM推理进度的框架。其阶段感知检查点根据视觉编码、语言模型预填充和解码的状态生命周期与计算特征选择恢复边界，平衡了存储流量与重计算。其依赖感知动态恢复调度从层和Token块维度的部分完成状态中调度恢复。通过将检查点和权重读取与重计算重叠，它降低了重启延迟；恢复规划器在其调度模型下可在100毫秒内计算出最优执行顺序。
在卫星载荷硬件上使用在轨遥测轨迹进行的实验表明，与评估的基线相比，实现了高达4.07倍的端到端加速和3.56倍的SSD写入量减少。在两颗低轨卫星上进行的72小时部署证明，OrbitWeaver能够保留推理进度并在重复的总线强制关机中恢复执行。
AI.summary: 本文针对低轨卫星边缘计算中视觉语言模型推理易受电源、热量和故障中断影响的问题，提出了OrbitWeaver框架。该框架通过阶段感知的检查点机制和依赖感知的动态恢复调度，实现了在中断后高效恢复VLM推理进度，显著减少了重计算并降低了存储写入量与重启延迟。
AI.keywords: 视觉语言模型, 低轨卫星, 检查点与恢复, 推理中断, 动态调度
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地解决了低轨卫星上视觉语言模型（VLM）推理在面对电源限制、故障重启等中断时的进度保持问题。通过提出阶段感知的检查点机制和依赖感知的动态恢复调度，显著降低了重启延迟和存储开销，在卫星硬件和在轨遥测数据上表现出优异的加速效果和存储缩减，具有很高的实用价值。

title: Optimal Labeling Schemes for $Γ$-Free Matrices
summary:
We study labeling schemes for $p \times q$ $Γ$-free binary matrices, which do not contain a submatrix of the form $Γ= \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. We give a labeling scheme that uses $O(\log^2 N)$-bit labels for rows and columns, where $N=p+q$, such that any matrix entry can be determined from the corresponding two labels in constant time in the word RAM model. The worst-case label size matches the counting lower bound up to constant factors. We also show that the entrywise least $Γ$-free supermatrix of an arbitrary $p\times q$ binary matrix, together with its labels, can be constructed in $O(pq)$ time.
  Our construction represents a $Γ$-free matrix by a sequence of rooted forests, where each column corresponds to a node and the $1$-entries of each row form a root path in its corresponding forest.
  For $n$-vertex strongly chordal and chordal bipartite graphs, our result gives asymptotically optimal $O(\log^2 n)$-bit adjacency labeling schemes with constant-time queries. These results answer both representation questions posed by Spinrad in 1995.

AI.title_translation: $\Gamma$-free 矩阵的最优标记方案
AI.tldr: 本文提出了 $\Gamma$-free 矩阵的最优标记方案，实现了 $O(\log^2 N)$ 位标签和常数时间的元素查询，解决了 Spinrad 1995 年提出的长期公开问题。
AI.motivation: 研究 $p \times q$ $\Gamma$-free 二元矩阵的标记方案，旨在改进矩阵表示并解决 Spinrad 在 1995 年提出的关于弦图和弦二分图表示的问题。
AI.method: 通过将 $\Gamma$-free 矩阵表示为一系列有根森林的序列，其中每一列对应一个节点，每行的 1-条目在其对应的森林中形成根路径。
AI.result: 设计了一种使用 $O(\log^2 N)$ 位标签的方案，能在词 RAM 模型中以常数时间确定矩阵元素，最坏情况下的标签大小与计数下界相匹配，且可在 $O(pq)$ 时间内构造超矩阵及标签。
AI.conclusion: 本文给出了 $\Gamma$-free 矩阵的最优标记方案，并成功解决了图论中的两个长期未决的表示问题。
AI.translation:
我们研究了 $p \times q$ $\Gamma$-free 二元矩阵的标记方案，这类矩阵不包含形如 $\Gamma= \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ 的子矩阵。我们提出了一种标记方案，为行和列使用 $O(\log^2 N)$ 位的标签（其中 $N=p+q$），使得在词 RAM 模型中，可以通过对应的两个标签在常数时间内确定任何矩阵元素。最坏情况下的标签大小在常数因子上与计数下界相匹配。我们还表明，任意 $p \times q$ 二元矩阵的逐元素最小 $\Gamma$-free 超矩阵与其标签可以在 $O(pq)$ 时间内构造出来。
我们的构造将 $\Gamma$-free 矩阵表示为一个有根森林序列，其中每一列对应一个节点，每行的 1-条目在其对应的森林中形成一条根路径。
对于 $n$ 个顶点的强弦图和弦二分图，我们的结果给出了渐近最优的 $O(\log^2 n)$ 位邻接标记方案以及常数时间的查询。这些结果回答了 Spinrad 在 1995 年提出的两个表示问题。
AI.summary: 本文针对 $p \times q$ $\Gamma$-free 二元矩阵提出了一种最优的标记方案，使用 $O(\log^2 N)$ 位标签实现了常数时间的矩阵元素查询，并解决了 Spinrad 于 1995 年提出的图论表示问题。
AI.keywords: 标记方案, $\Gamma$-free 矩阵, 弦二分图, 强弦图, 邻接查询
AI.comments: 该论文解决了 Spinrad 在 1995 年提出的关于强弦图和弦二分图的邻接标记方案的两个表示问题，理论意义重大，且其最坏情况下的标记大小在常数因子上与计数下界相匹配。

title: CloudIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Root Cause Analysis and Mitigation of Cloud Incidents
summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) and mitigation prediction are essential for incident management, enabling the identification of underlying causes of failures and ensuring the reliability of complex cloud-based systems. With rising incident volume and system complexity, incident reports have become a valuable resource for these tasks. Recent studies have shown promising results using Large Language Models (LLMs) to predict root causes and mitigation actions from textual descriptions in incident reports. Despite these advances, further progress is hindered by the lack of publicly available datasets; existing work relies on private data, which limits transparency, reproducibility, and generalization. To address this gap, we introduce CloudIR-Bench, the first publicly available benchmark providing a dataset and evaluation framework for incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction. Curated from incident reports across five leading cloud-based systems, CloudIR-Bench captures a diverse range of real-world production scenarios representing authentic failures and engineers' reasoning. We also release an open-source evaluation framework that includes eight recent LLM-based approaches. Our comprehensive evaluation includes zero-shot and in-context learning experiments, along with a qualitative analysis to identify where and why LLMs fail. Benchmarking results reveal the capabilities and limitations of existing LLMs in this domain. The benchmark, including the dataset, framework and supplementary materials, is available at https://github.com/hoangtnm/CloudIR-Bench.

AI.title_translation: CloudIR-Bench：一个用于云事件根本原因分析与缓解的基准测试
AI.tldr: 推出了首个用于云事件根本原因分析与缓解预测的公开基准测试CloudIR-Bench，填补了该领域缺乏标准化数据集的空白。
AI.motivation: 尽管大语言模型在云事件的根本原因分析（RCA）和缓解预测中展现出潜力，但由于缺乏公开数据集，现有研究依赖私有数据，阻碍了透明度、可重复性和泛化能力。
AI.method: 构建了CloudIR-Bench基准测试，涵盖来自五个领先云系统的数据集，并开源了包含八种基于LLM的方法及零样本、上下文学习实验和定性分析的评估框架。
AI.result: 通过全面评估揭示了现有大模型在云事件RCA和缓解预测领域的具体能力与局限性。
AI.conclusion: CloudIR-Bench为云事件报告的RCA和缓解预测提供了一个全面的公开数据集和评估框架，有助于未来大模型在云运维领域的深入研究与应用。
AI.translation: 根本原因分析（RCA）和缓解预测对于事件管理至关重要，它能够确定故障的根本原因并确保复杂云系统的可靠性。随着事件数量和系统复杂性的增加，事件报告已成为这些任务的重要资源。最近的研究表明，使用大语言模型（LLM）从事件报告的文本描述中预测根本原因和缓解行动取得了有前景的结果。尽管取得了这些进展，但缺乏公开可用的数据集阻碍了进一步的发展；现有工作依赖于私有数据，这限制了透明度、可复现性和泛化能力。为了填补这一空白，我们推出了 CloudIR-Bench，这是第一个公开可用的基准测试，为基于事件报告的RCA和缓解预测提供了一个数据集和评估框架。CloudIR-Bench从五个领先的云系统事件报告中筛选而来，捕捉了代表真实故障和工程师推理的各种真实生产场景。我们还发布了一个开源评估框架，其中包括八种最新的基于LLM的方法。我们的综合评估包括零样本和上下文学习实验，以及定性分析，以确定LLM在何处以及为何失败。基准测试结果揭示了现有LLM在该领域的强大功能和局限性。该基准测试，包括数据集、框架和补充材料，可在https://github.com/hoangtnm/CloudIR-Bench获取。
AI.summary: CloudIR-Bench是首个用于云事件报告根本原因分析和缓解预测的公开基准测试，包含来自五个领先云系统的数据集及开源评估框架，旨在解决该领域缺乏公开数据集、难以进行透明评估的问题。
AI.keywords: 云事件管理, 根本原因分析, 大语言模型, 基准测试, 缓解预测
AI.comments: 该论文填补了云服务领域缺乏公开、标准化事件报告数据集的空白，通过构建CloudIR-Bench推动了基于大语言模型的根本原因分析（RCA）和缓解策略预测研究，具有很高的实用价值和开源贡献。

title: A Decade of Learning-Based Control: From Theoretic Foundations to Practical Deployment
summary: Motivated by ten years of Learning-Based Control Invited Sessions at the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC), this tutorial paper reviews key advances at the intersection of machine learning and control. We focus on methods that combine the flexibility of machine learning techniques with the structure and theoretical foundations of control to design autonomous systems that are capable, reliable, and safe. We first introduce core notions for establishing stability and safety guarantees, then review approaches that learn dynamics models to improve control under uncertainty, and finally discuss data-driven methods that directly synthesize or learn policies, including reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and Bayesian optimization. We further discuss representative applications and open challenges. The goal is to provide an accessible entry point to the field and to support continued progress toward reliable learning-based control in real-world systems. To support learning and practical exploration, we share implementations and illustrative examples along with our discussion, together with additional resources on our website: https://learning-based-control.github.io/tutorial/.

AI.title_translation: 学习型控制十年：从理论基础到实际部署
AI.tldr: 本文综述了过去十年学习型控制领域的关键进展，结合机器学习与控制理论，探讨了稳定安全性保证、动态建模、策略学习及实际应用。
AI.motivation: 为了总结过去十年在IEEE决策与控制会议（CDC）上“学习型控制特邀分会”的成果，回顾机器学习与控制交叉领域的关键进展，为设计能够胜任、可靠且安全的自主系统提供易于理解的入门途径和资源。
AI.method: 本文是一篇教程型综述论文，首先引入建立稳定性和安全保证的核心概念，接着回顾学习动态模型以改善不确定性下控制的方法，最后讨论直接合成或学习策略的数据驱动方法（如强化学习、模仿学习和贝叶斯优化），并辅以实际应用和开源实现。
AI.result: 梳理了建立稳定性和安全性保证的核心概念、学习动态模型的方法以及直接策略学习方法，并提供了代表性应用、开放性挑战及开源实现示例。
AI.conclusion: 学习型控制在结合机器学习灵活性与控制理论严格保证方面取得了显著进展，未来需要在真实世界的可靠部署和开放挑战上继续努力。
AI.translation: 受IEEE决策与控制会议（CDC）上十年学习型控制特邀分会的启发，这篇教程论文回顾了机器学习与控制交叉领域的关键进展。我们重点关注将机器学习技术的灵活性与控制理论的结构和理论基础相结合的方法，以设计能够胜任、可靠且安全的自主系统。我们首先引入建立稳定性和安全保证的核心概念，接着回顾了学习动态模型以改善不确定性下控制的方法，最后讨论了直接合成或学习策略的数据驱动方法，包括强化学习、模仿学习和贝叶斯优化。我们进一步讨论了代表性的应用和开放性挑战。其目标是为该领域提供一个易于接近的入门点，并支持在真实世界系统中对可靠学习型控制的持续进展。为了支持学习和实际探索，我们在讨论的同时分享了实现和说明性示例，以及我们网站上的其他资源：https://learning-based-control.github.io/tutorial/。
AI.summary: 本文是一篇关于学习型控制十年进展的教程综述，探讨了如何结合机器学习的灵活性与控制理论的结构及基础，以设计安全、可靠的自主系统，涵盖稳定性保证、动态建模、策略学习、应用场景及开源资源。
AI.keywords: 学习型控制, 机器学习, 控制理论, 稳定性与安全性, 强化学习
AI.comments: 本文是回顾学习型控制（Learning-Based Control）过去十年发展的重要教程类论文，结合了机器学习的灵活性与控制理论的安全性保证，对未来现实世界的自主系统部署具有重要指导意义。

title: LTEM: LLM-Friendly Table-Enhanced Markdown for Table Understanding and Generation
comments: Accepted to the EMNLP 2026 Main Conference
summary: Tables in real-world documents, including scientific papers, financial reports, and statistical summaries, frequently use merged cells, multi-level headers, and sectioned layouts. Yet the lightweight formats LLMs handle best (Markdown, CSV) cannot express these structures, while expressive formats (HTML, LaTeX) impose excessive token cost and parsing complexity. To enable systematic analysis of this trade-off, we introduce a taxonomy decomposing table structure into six atomic features (F1-F6) and corresponding complexity levels (L1-L6), and construct STB (Synthetic Table Benchmark), a controlled benchmark with 1,089 tables systematically distributed across complexity levels. Using this framework, we propose LTEM (LLM-friendly Table-Enhanced Markdown), a formally specified, minimal extension of Markdown that explicitly encodes spans and hierarchical headers. Experiments across five state-of-the-art LLMs show that LTEM achieves accuracy comparable to HTML, offers a favorable accuracy-token trade-off relative to HTML and LaTeX, and produces substantially fewer invalid responses than LaTeX; for table generation, LTEM is comparable to MultiMarkdown though HTML is best. We release our taxonomy, benchmark, and format specification to support future research on LLM-table interaction.
