title: Policy Central: Detecting Conflicts, Redundancy, and Similarity in Deployed Police Policy
summary: Policy Central is a deployed system that helps police departments find relationships between sections of their written policy: whether two sections conflict, are redundant, are merely similar, or are different. We describe the system and compare two architectures. Retrieve-Judge, a retrieve-then-classify pipeline, runs as a cheap library-wide health signal; Screen-Confirm, a screen-then-confirm cascade, is a selective audit of the documents a reviewer chooses, checking them exhaustively against one another. On a 302-pair benchmark drawn from one department's ~84 real policy documents, given each pair Screen-Confirm reaches 0.795 aggregate recall and 0.885 on Conflict, so current models judge well. Finding the pair is the hard part: Retrieve-Judge's composed recall falls to 0.457, and Screen-Confirm recovers 0.472 (0.615 on Conflict). Today these pairs are found by reading the whole library, nearly 20,000 sections, checked against one another and re-checked after every revision. A scan that returns half of them in minutes, at low cost, and can be re-run on demand changes the economics of policy review even before recall improves.

title: ChronoSynth: Constraint-Aware Question Synthesis over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
summary: Knowledge graph question generation (KGQG) generates natural-language questions from structured graph evidence and a target answer. When the input graph is temporal, a valid question must also preserve the answer field, time condition, reference event, and temporal order that determine the answer set. Existing KGQG methods and prompting baselines can produce fluent questions that alter these conditions, causing temporal semantic drift. This paper studies temporal KGQG as a constraint-preserving graph-to-question problem and proposes ChronoSynth, a memory-augmented and constraint-aware generation framework. ChronoSynth first constructs a Temporal Intent State to make the intended question semantics explicit. It then retrieves compatible typed question patterns from an indexed pattern memory, adapts them to the input graph, and validates the generated question. Validation feedback guides revisions when a supported inconsistency is detected. Experiments on CRONQUESTIONS and MultiTQ demonstrate state-of-the-art generation performance, with ablations supporting the contributions of its components.

title: Reader--Writer Coupling in Transformer MLPs
summary: A transformer MLP gives each hidden channel two roles: a reader that decides when the channel responds, and a writer that decides what it adds back to the residual stream. Read as a key--value memory, the layer can be measured one factor set at a time: the pairing of readers to writers is carried only by their shared index, invisible to any quantity computed from one factor set alone. Yet training couples the two factors through their joint update, so we ask what reading them together shows. The block supplies the joint instrument: the MLP writes back into the very stream it reads, so the exact Jacobian of its update is square, and its agreement with its own transpose resolves into reader--writer terms whose inner products give each channel, read as a couple, a signed pairing coordinate. Ranked by this coordinate, each block we measure has a small core of strongly coupled channels; where initialization gives either sign equally, the core is nearly all opposed: each writer points against the direction its reader responds to. This opposed core recurs from the smallest models trained from scratch to released checkpoints; its sign is in place within a few percent of training and holds while the coupling grows. Read as couples, most channels return their contribution against the reader that fired it, and the readers of later blocks take it up; few show in the logits. Training holds the couples in place: flipping the opposed writers moves the output toward common tokens, and a writer permuted onto another reader regrows to fit that reader while the reader stays.

title: Uncensored Is Not Unbiased: Abliteration Removes Refusals but Not Script-Dependent Bias About Taiwan
comments: 33 pages, 3 figures, 18 tables. Code, data and an interactive project page: https://daaab.github.io/uncensored-not-unbiased/
summary: "Abliterated" ("uncensored") builds of open-weight language models remove the activation direction that mediates refusal, and are popular partly on the assumption that a model that no longer refuses is also free of political censorship. We test this on two matched pairs of 2-bit models: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, each against a community abliteration. Each model judged 22 statement pairs (on the Republic of China (Taiwan), 1989 Tiananmen, control countries) in Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese (a character-level conversion) and English, and answered 27 open questions per script. Script mattered far more than abliteration: the original Bolt scored +0.58 on Index S (-1: People's Republic of China (PRC) position; +1: ROC position) in Traditional Chinese, +0.57 in English and +0.05 in Simplified Chinese, and affirmed "Taiwan is part of the PRC" with probability 0.91 in Simplified but 0.06 in Traditional characters; abliteration changed its scores by at most 0.06, mostly by raising "yes" on both sides. In Qwen, abliteration removed every refusal on 1989 and raised scores by 0.21 to 0.34, yet the abliterated Qwen still affirmed that Taiwan is part of the PRC in all three scripts. Naming the state the Republic of China (Taiwan) raised every model's score by 0.10 to 0.33 but left the script gap. Control pairs showed no script gap; each abliteration changed only its declared tensors. In 740,000 web documents, Simplified text on Taiwan contained PRC-framing terms 3.7 times as often as Traditional text. A script direction could not be steered away; a contrastive stance direction raised scores in every script, and its negation lowered them. A four-sentence system prompt raised the abliterated Qwen to +0.93 to +0.97. Keyword scoring rules failed the models closest to the ROC position mostly for attributing or denying the PRC claim. Uncensored is not unbiased.

title: MASAR: Multi-stage Attack Surface Analysis and Reasoning Framework for Telecom Networks
summary: The increasing complexity of modern telecommunications networks introduces security challenges that require systematic threat analysis. However, a gap remains between architectural threat modeling frameworks, such as Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege (STRIDE), and operational knowledge bases, such as the MITRE Five-G Hierarchy of Threats (FiGHT). This gap limits the ability to connect architectural weaknesses with specific protocol behaviors and attack sequences. This paper presents Multi-stage Attack Surface Analysis and Reasoning (MASAR), a formal framework that bridges this gap through three layers: strategic threat mapping, logical attack path decomposition using directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and operational synthesis of tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). MASAR is evaluated using a 5G-ready IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) architecture, examining two signaling attack scenarios: early media billing bypass through Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) signaling and subscriber information disclosure and topology discovery through the Diameter Cx interface. MiniZinc constraint models are used to analyze the reachability of unsafe protocol states. The analysis demonstrates how MASAR connects architectural threats with specific protocol behaviors and supports security controls that account for network states in telecommunications systems.

title: Decodability Is Not Controllability: Local and Anisotropic Speaker Control in Continuous-Latent TTS
summary: High linear decodability does not entail causal controllability in continuous-latent text-to-speech (TTS). In VoxCPM2, position-matched probes and equal-norm interventions across 30 speakers and 60 directed dyads expose this separation: reference-audio states at the final residual acoustic language model layer (RALM L7) retain 0.970 probe accuracy, yet aligned edits yield 0/60 target-dominant dyads. Edits at early reference-audio positions produce the opposite pattern. At L0, pair-aligned updates increase target similarity by 0.326 and achieve target dominance in all 60 dyads, against at most 1/60 under any equal-norm direction or position control. Independent speaker encoders, retrieval against held-out speaker prototypes, and double-blind listening confirm that the shifted voice is heard as the intended target. Cross-architecture interventions in dots.tts distinguish backbone leverage from direct acoustic control: backbone edits displace the source without target attraction, while x-vector ablation reduces source similarity from 0.849 to 0.006. These findings identify two requirements for training-free speaker control: geometric specificity and a computational route that carries the intended speaker condition into acoustic synthesis.

title: Benchmarking and Error Analysis of Deep Search and Deep Research LLM Agents
comments: Proceedings of the 1st ICML Workshop on Failure Modes in Agentic AI (FAGEN), Seoul, South Korea, 2026
summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) evolve into autonomous Deep Search and Deep Research Agents capable of executing long-horizon, multi-step tasks, evaluating their reliability becomes increasingly critical. However, existing evaluation paradigms predominantly focus on final task outcomes, leaving a significant gap in understanding the intermediate execution traces, where agents are highly susceptible to various errors. To address this critical gap, we introduce a comprehensive methodology and analytical framework designed specifically to diagnose errors in intermediate workflows. Building upon this framework, we establish a structured taxonomy that categorizes these vulnerabilities into two primary dimensions: System-Level Errors and Task-Level Errors. Through a systematic examination of step-by-step execution traces and agent-environment interactions, we reveal how these underlying errors affect overall performance. Finally, through empirical experiments and systematic analysis of the identified error types, we provide actionable design guidelines, aiming to enhance the robustness, reasoning capabilities, and reliability of Deep Search and Deep Research agents.

title: Data Schedules and Learning Rate Schedules Should Be Designed Together
summary: Mid-training (MT) is a training phase in LLM training pipelines that continues pretraining (PT) on smaller datasets of higher value. Taking the PT and MT phases as a whole, training usually starts with only PT data and then transitions completely to MT data. In this work, we view this complete transition from PT to MT data as a special case of a broader class of data mixing schedules that specify how the proportions of PT and MT tokens in each batch change over training. Under fixed total training compute and MT token budgets, we ask: Is this complete transition to MT data optimal for minimizing final MT loss? We show that the answer depends on the learning rate (LR) schedule: one data schedule may outperform another under one LR schedule, but changing only the LR schedule can reverse the outcome. Specifically, when the LR decays throughout continued training, introducing MT data earlier and mixing it with PT data lowers the final MT loss compared with placing all MT data at the end of training, but this result is reversed if we use constant LR. We therefore study how to jointly choose when to introduce MT data and when to decay the LR through ablation studies, and find that it is better to decay the LR only after MT data enters training. Finally, we develop a theoretical model that explains why the optimal data schedule for a fixed MT token budget depends on the LR schedule.

title: B-CARE: Blind Classwise Assessment of Relative Evidence for Stance Error Ranking
summary: Stance classifiers make errors that can be costly to identify under limited human-review budgets. Prioritizing potentially incorrect predictions remains challenging, particularly across heterogeneous base models. We introduce B-CARE (Blind Classwise Assessment of Relative Evidence for Stance Error Ranking), a prediction-blind framework for identifying high-risk stance predictions. Given only a target and text, a fixed LLM verifier assigns ordinal evidence scores to all candidate stance labels without observing the base model's prediction or confidence. B-CARE constructs a comparative risk score by contrasting the strongest alternative-class evidence with the evidence supporting the predicted class. The resulting classwise evidence profile can be reused across multiple base models without training a separate error detector or calibrating risk scores. We evaluate B-CARE on four stance benchmarks and three heterogeneous base LLMs, covering 12 dataset-model settings and 5,206 unique test instances. Evaluation includes error-ranking discrimination (AUROC and AUPRC), selective prediction (E-AURC), and review effectiveness (ErrorCapture at fixed review budgets). B-CARE achieves a mean AUROC of 0.735 and a mean AUPRC of 0.524, capturing 41.06% of errors within the highest-risk 20% of predictions. Although B-CARE does not uniformly outperform strong confidence-based baselines, it provides a reusable, complementary evidence signal for prioritizing potentially incorrect stance predictions across heterogeneous models.

title: Closed-Loop Dual-Reference Guidance for Accent Control in Cross-Lingual Voice Cloning
summary: Zero-shot cross-lingual voice cloning often carries the reference speaker's accent into the target language. We propose closed-loop dual-reference guidance, which pairs the original reference with a reusable native anchor constructed by voice conversion (VC). The references initialize separate language-model (LM) states that guide a shared acoustic trajectory; each completed patch then updates both states, keeping their generated histories aligned with the emitted speech. Anchor construction runs once per speaker, and online synthesis uses a frozen TTS model without per-utterance VC. On 20 held-out French speakers, the fixed setting $λ^{\!*}=0.33$ reduces residual French LID mass by 73\% versus direct cloning, at an ECAPA similarity cost of only $0.042$; relative to anchor-only cloning, it recovers $0.155$. The method achieves the lowest mean WER ($0.009$) and highest mean GOP ($4.750$) among the held-out test arms. In blinded preference tests, native-English listeners favor it over direct cloning on pronunciation naturalness, and over both anchor-only cloning and a TTS$\to$VC cascade on speaker identity. Online RTF is approximately 26\% lower than the cascade's ($0.59$ vs.\ $0.80$), and the same setting reduces Spanish LID mass by 56\% without re-tuning.

title: Don't Stop Long-Context Continual Pre-Training Too Early: An Empirical Scaling Law
summary: Long-context continual pre-training (LCCP) is widely used to improve long-context capability, but how its benefits scale with the number of tokens used for LCCP remains unclear. We investigate this question through modeling, monitoring, and validating the benefits of scaling LCCP. First, we establish an empirical additive power law relating long-context performance to model size and the respective token budgets of short-context pre-training and LCCP. Experiments across five model scales and more than one hundred short- and long-context budget configurations show that the fitted law reproduces the observed trends and extrapolates well to held-out model scales. Second, we introduce \textsc{Constant-Last4}, a training and observation protocol that averages the four most recent consecutive checkpoints from a constant-learning-rate run to enable stable monitoring along a single extensible training trajectory. Under this protocol, the same scaling-law form fits well and accurately predicts the LCCP performance trajectory of a 1.22B-parameter model trained on approximately 100B LCCP tokens. Finally, downstream evaluations along this trajectory show continued improvements in long-context performance, with no clear sign of saturation within the evaluated range. These gains persist after both 128K context extension and supervised fine-tuning, with benefits extending to long-context understanding and agentic tasks. Together, these results argue for continuing to scale LCCP rather than stopping early: its gains are stably observable along an extensible trajectory, quantitatively predictable, and transferable to downstream tasks.

title: GaP-MoE : Explicit Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts via Orthogonal Gradient Accumulation and Projection
summary: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) models improve scalability by routing input tokens to only a subset of expert networks, but they often suffer from representation collapse, in which multiple experts converge toward similar functions and lose their intended diversity. Prior work has addressed this limitation either by improving router architectures or by introducing auxiliary loss terms that implicitly penalize similarity among experts. However, router-based approaches remain vulnerable to routing collapses, and loss-based approaches can conflict with the task's original objective during optimization. In this work, we propose GaP-MoE (Gradient Accumulation and Projection in MoE), which induces expert specialization by directly manipulating expert output gradients rather than modifying the loss function. At each training step, GaP-MoE stochastically selects one of the $TopK$ routed experts as a leader based on normalized routing scores, and projects the gradients of the remaining follower experts onto the orthogonal complement of the subspace spanned by the leader's recent gradients. This removes directional overlap between expert gradients without altering the task loss, allowing specialization to emerge as a direct consequence of the optimization dynamics rather than an externally imposed constraint. We evaluate GaP-MoE in both fine-tuning settings (BERT-based, on GLUE) and from-scratch pretraining settings (GPT-2-based, on WikiText-103, enwik8, and text8), and further confirm its compatibility as a drop-in module for existing SMoE architectures. Experimental results show that GaP-MoE achieves performance comparable to or better than standard SMoE.

title: Payload generalization on feedforward control actions for trajectory tracking in robots with rigid and elastic joints
comments: 18 pages, 17 figures. Accepted for publication in Control Engineering Practice
summary: Industries employ robots for repetitive tasks due to their high precision and performance, typically achieved through feedforward control actions based on an accurate robot description. However, an exact dynamic model can be difficult to obtain, especially for robots with elastic elements or when the payload changes. Learning-based feedforward approaches are promising for trajectory tracking under model uncertainties, but typically face generalization issues when task parameters vary. This paper proposes a novel method to generalize the feedforward control action with respect to payload parameters, independently of the underlying controller. Firstly, the minimal number of example objects needed for payload generalization is derived. Then, an algorithm is proposed to execute the same trajectory with a new payload, given only its parameters, without knowledge of the robot's dynamic model and even in the presence of elastic joints. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated in simulations and experiments on tracking tasks with different robots and controllers. Two sets of experiments are performed: on a standard Franka Emika Panda robot, and on a Franka Emika Panda robot equipped with an elastic wrist.

title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. Whether memory can drive genuine continual learning remains an open question. In this paper, we introduce Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL), arguing that memory should be judged by whether it improves future actions, not merely what it retrieves. MCCL has three main parts. First, a three-axis taxonomy organizes memory by where state is stored (substrates), what form it takes (assets), and how it is managed (policies). This defines a two-loop lifecycle that updates memory state in an inner loop while refining management policies in an outer loop based on task feedback. Second, an evaluation protocol measures retention under interference, adaptation to change, and task transfer to isolate genuine behavioral gains from simple context expansion. Third, a memory scaling framework models how agent performance scales with experience, storage capacity, and compute budgets across non-parametric and parametric memory. Together, these components reframe agent memory from passive lookup to continuous learning, offering a principled route toward self-improving autonomous agents.

AI.title_translation: 面向AI代理的以内存为中心的持续学习
AI.tldr: 本文提出了以内存为中心的持续学习（MCCL）框架，将AI代理的外部内存从被动的检索缓存转变为驱动持续学习和自我改进的核心机制。
AI.motivation: 基于基础模型的自主代理由于固定权重和上下文限制，难以在长期部署中从经验中进行持续学习，而现有的外部内存系统大多仅作为被动检索缓存，无法驱动真正的持续学习。
AI.method: 提出了MCCL框架，包含三个部分：1) 三轴分类法（基质、资产、策略）与内外循环生命周期；2) 评估干涉下的保持力、环境适应和任务迁移的评估协议；3) 建模代理性能随经验、存储容量和计算预算变化的内存扩展框架。
AI.result: 通过将代理内存从被动查找重新构想为持续学习，MCCL提供了一个系统化评估和扩展代理内存的方法，推动了自改进自主代理的发展。
AI.conclusion: MCCL框架通过三轴分类法、严格的评估协议和内存扩展框架，为基于基础模型的自主代理实现自我改进的持续学习提供了一条原则性途径。
AI.translation: 由基础模型驱动的自主代理能够进行推理、规划和使用工具，但其固定的权重和上下文限制阻碍了在长期部署中从经验中进行持续学习。虽然外部内存系统试图弥补这一差距，但它们大多作为被动检索缓存，主要通过能否回忆存储的事实或过去交互来评估。内存能否推动真正的持续学习仍然是一个开放的问题。在本文中，我们引入了以内存为中心的持续学习（MCCL），认为内存的优劣应该以它是否能改善未来的动作来判断，而不仅仅取决于检索到了什么。MCCL包含三个主要部分。首先，三轴分类法根据状态存储位置（基质）、形式（资产）和管理方式（策略）来组织内存。这定义了一个两层循环生命周期，在内循环中更新内存状态，在外循环中根据任务反馈改进管理策略。其次，评估协议测量干涉下的保持力、对变化的适应能力以及任务迁移，以将真正的行为收益与简单的上下文扩展区分开来。第三，内存 scaling 框架建模了代理性能如何在非参数和参数内存中随经验、存储容量和计算预算而扩展。这些组件共同将代理内存从被动查找重新构想为持续学习，为自我改进的自主代理提供了一条有原则的路线。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了内存中心持续学习（MCCL）框架，旨在通过三轴内存分类法、新的评估协议和内存扩展框架，将AI代理的外部内存从被动的检索缓存转变为推动未来行动和持续学习的动态核心。
AI.keywords: 持续学习, 自主代理, 外部内存, 基础模型, 内存管理
AI.comments: 该论文提出了内存中心持续学习（MCCL）框架，将AI代理的外部内存从被动的检索缓存转变为驱动持续学习的核心机制，对解决基础模型代理在长期部署中的持续学习问题具有重要意义。

title: Reading the Mask: Descriptor-Grounded BI-RADS Rationale Generation for Breast MRI Segmentation
summary: Deep learning based models accurately delineate tumours on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), but segmentation masks alone do not provide the rationales or reasoning used by radiologists to assess the lesion suspicion. This limits the explainability as well the clinical integration. We investigate whether clinically relevant descriptors can instead be derived from the segmentation masks and their dynamic contrast-enhancement series. We have used Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) guidelines as a structured framework. Using these guidelines we designed a BI-RADS decision tree with eight quantitative measurements using radiomics, together with the lesion size and component count, that determine the descriptors at eight nodes. Using these descriptors we generate natural-language rationale using a large language model. The model was constrained to express only the derived records from the decision tree. After applying this framework to the expert and automatic masks of each of the 1,506 cases in the MAMA-MIA dataset, we generated a reproducible corpus of 3,012 BI-RADS grounded rationales. We obtained a faithfulness score of 99.98% and a counterfactual accuracy of 99.3%, indicating that the generated rationales faithfully verbalises the measured descriptors and correctly reflects changes in the underlying record. Agreement between the descriptors from expert and automatic masks falls from 0.832 to 0.549 as mask quality falls from Good to Missed. The generated rationales are intended as draft representations for radiologist review and final sign-off rather than autonomous clinical reports.

AI.title_translation: 阅读掩膜：基于描述符的乳腺MRI分割BI-RADS理由生成
AI.tldr: 本研究开发了一个将乳腺MRI分割掩膜转化为基于BI-RADS的结构化自然语言理由的框架，大幅提升了深度学习模型在乳腺肿瘤诊断中的可解释性与临床信任度。
AI.motivation: 深度学习模型虽然能准确勾勒动态对比增强MRI（DCE-MRI）上的肿瘤，但缺乏放射科医生评估病灶可疑度时所依赖的理由或推理过程，从而限制了模型的可解释性以及在临床实践中的整合。
AI.method: 基于乳腺影像报告和数据系统（BI-RADS）指南设计了一个包含8个基于影像组学的定量测量、病灶大小及组件计数的决策树，从分割掩膜和动态对比增强序列中推导临床相关描述符，并利用大语言模型将这些描述符转化为受约束的自然语言理由。
AI.result: 在MAMA-MIA数据集的1506个病例（专家和自动掩膜）上应用该框架后，生成了3012个BI-RADS基础理由语料库。模型达到了99.98%的忠实度得分和99.3%的反事实准确率；随着掩膜质量从“好”下降到“漏检”，专家掩膜与自动掩膜描述符之间的一致性从0.832下降到0.549。
AI.conclusion: 本研究成功开发了一个基于描述符和BI-RADS决策树的自然语言理由生成框架，用于乳腺MRI分割。该框架能够生成高度忠实于底层影像测量特征的临床合理解释，有效提升了深度学习模型在乳腺癌诊断中的可解释性和临床集成潜力。
AI.translation: 基于深度学习的模型能够准确描绘动态对比增强MRI（DCE-MRI）上的肿瘤，但仅凭分割掩膜并不能提供放射科医生用来评估病灶可疑度的理由或推理过程。这限制了模型的可解释性以及临床整合。我们研究了是否可以从分割掩膜及其动态对比增强序列中推导出临床相关的描述符。我们使用乳腺影像报告和数据系统（BI-RADS）指南作为结构化框架。利用这些指南，我们设计了一个BI-RADS决策树，其中包含使用影像组学的八个定量测量值，连同病灶大小和组件计数，共同决定了八个节点的描述符。利用这些描述符，我们使用大语言模型生成了自然语言理由。模型被限制为仅表达从决策树派生的记录。将该框架应用于MAMA-MIA数据集中1,506个病例的专家掩膜和自动掩膜后，我们生成了一个由3,012个基于BI-RADS的理由组成的可复现语料库。我们获得了99.98%的忠实度得分和99.3%的反事实准确率，表明生成的理由忠实地表达了测量的描述符，并正确反映了底层记录的变化。随着掩膜质量从“好”下降到“漏检”，专家掩膜与自动掩膜描述符之间的一致性从0.832下降到0.549。生成的理由旨在作为放射科医生审查和最终签字的草稿表示，而不是自主的临床报告。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种基于描述符的BI-RADS理由生成框架，用于乳腺MRI分割。通过将BI-RADS决策树与大语言模型相结合，该方法能够从分割掩膜中提取定量影像特征并生成忠实、可解释的自然语言临床理由，从而提高深度学习模型的临床可解释性。
AI.keywords: Breast MRI, BI-RADS, Rationale Generation, Segmentation, Large Language Models
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地结合了医学影像分割与大语言模型，利用结构化的BI-RADS决策树将动态对比增强MRI（DCE-MRI）的分割掩膜转化为可解释的自然语言理由，不仅提高了深度学习模型在乳腺MRI分割中的可解释性，还生成了高质量、高忠实度的可复现语料库。局限性在于生成的理由目前仅作为放射科医生的初稿参考，且其描述符的一致性高度依赖于分割掩膜的质量。

title: Seeing through Denoising: Frequency-guided One-step Denoising for Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) is a challenging task due to the extremely small size of targets, low signal-to-noise ratios, and heavy background clutter in infrared imagery. While the progress of deep learning has advanced this field, existing methods primarily adopt discriminative paradigms that directly map images to target masks, overlooking the potential of generative modeling. In this paper, we propose DiffIRSTD, a novel generative framework that reformulates infrared small target detection as a background reconstruction problem. Instead of explicitly predicting target regions, we reinterpret small targets as noise-like signals and leverage a diffusion-based model to recover a clean, target-free background from a perturbed input image. The residual between the reconstructed background and the original image is then exploited to highlight candidate target regions, providing explicit cues for subsequent detection. To address the computational cost typically associated with diffusion sampling, we introduce a one-step denoising strategy that enables efficient background reconstruction while maintaining practical inference speed. Furthermore, we present a frequency-guided perception loss to preserve high-frequency background details and focus more on the reconstruction quality of target regions. More importantly, our DiffIRSTD operates as a plug-and-play framework, compatible with existing IRSTD models without increasing the computational complexity of detectors. Extensive experiments on IRSTD-1K, NUAA-SIRST, and NUDT-SIRST datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method, achieving state-of-the-art performance across three benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: 透过降噪看本质：用于红外小目标检测的频率引导单步降噪法
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于频率引导单步去噪的生成式红外小目标检测框架(DiffIRSTD)，将检测转化为背景重建，实现了SOTA性能。
AI.motivation: 现有深度学习方法多采用直接映射到目标掩码的判别范式，忽视了生成式建模的潜力，且传统扩散采样计算成本高，因此需要一种高效的、基于生成建模的背景重建方案来提升红外弱小目标检测能力。
AI.method: 提出DiffIRSTD生成式框架，将检测转化为背景重建，利用基于扩散模型的一步去噪策略恢复清洁背景，并通过残差提取目标；同时引入频率引导感知损失以保留高-frequency背景细节并聚焦目标区域重建。
AI.result: 在IRSTD-1K、NUAA-SIRST和NUDT-SIRST三个数据集上进行了广泛的实验，结果表明该方法取得了最先进的性能，并作为即插即用框架与现有模型兼容。
AI.conclusion: 提出了一种名为DiffIRSTD的频率引导单步去噪生成框架，有效解决了红外弱小目标检测中背景杂乱和目标微小的问题，在多个数据集上取得了SOTA性能，且具有良好的兼容性。
AI.translation: 由于红外图像中目标极小、信噪比低以及背景杂波严重，红外小目标检测（IRSTD）是一项具有挑战性的任务。尽管深度学习的进展推动了该领域的发展，但现有方法主要采用直接将图像映射到目标掩码的判别范式，忽视了生成式建模的潜力。在本文中，我们提出了DiffIRSTD，一个新颖的生成框架，它将红外小目标检测重新表述为一个背景重建问题。我们没有显式地预测目标区域，而是将小目标重新解释为类似噪声的信号，并利用基于扩散的模型从受扰动的输入图像中恢复干净、无目标的背景。然后利用重建背景与原图像之间的残差来突显候选目标区域，为后续检测提供显式线索。为了解决扩散采样通常带来的计算成本，我们引入了一种单步去噪策略，在保持实际推理速度的同时实现高效的背景重建。此外，我们提出了一种频率引导感知损失，以保留高频背景细节并更多地关注目标区域的重建质量。更重要的是，我们的DiffIRSTD作为一个即插即用框架运行，与现有的IRSTD模型兼容，且不会增加检测器的计算复杂度。在IRSTD-1K、NUAA-SIRST和NUDT-SIRST数据集上的大量实验证明了我们方法的优越性，在三个基准测试中均取得了最先进的性能。
AI.summary: 本文提出了DiffIRSTD，一个用于红外小目标检测的频率引导单步去噪生成框架。该方法将目标检测重构为背景重建问题，利用扩散模型在单步去噪中恢复无目标背景，并通过残差突出目标。实验证明了其在多个基准上的优越性能。
AI.keywords: 红外小目标检测, 扩散模型, 背景重建, 频率引导, 单步去噪
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将红外弱小目标检测转化为背景重建问题，并巧妙地利用去噪扩散模型的思想进行单步去噪，兼顾了生成式模型的优势与高效的推理速度。这种即插即用的设计使其在多个基准数据集上取得了最先进的性能。

title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion
summary: X-ray and neutron scattering are indispensable for structural characterization across condensed-matter physics and materials science. Yet, because scattering experiments generally record intensities without phase information, distinct structures can yield similar scattering patterns, rendering the corresponding inverse problems non-unique. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining complementary measurements, but their integration into machine-learning frameworks remains challenging. Here we introduce a modular framework for probabilistic multi-measurement analysis based on prior-amortized flow matching. Single-observation posterior estimators are trained separately for individual observation types or physical probes and combined only at inference time through a compositional sampler. This late fusion approach allows pretrained single-observation models to be reused without dedicated joint retraining. As a case in point, we consider reflectometry, which provides depth-resolved, nanometer-scale information about thin films and interfaces. Our single-observation demonstrations span X-ray, time-of-flight neutron and polarized neutron reflectometry. In separate co-refinement studies, task-matched estimators enable homogeneous composition across multiple neutron contrasts and heterogeneous multimodal composition of X-ray and neutron measurements. Together, these results establish compositional flow matching as a modular approach to uncertainty-aware inversion and co-refinement, with potential applicability to other scattering problems in which multiple observations constrain a common physical structure while retaining measurement-specific parameters.

AI.title_translation: 用于多模态X射线和中子散射反演的组合神经网络
AI.tldr: 提出了一种基于组合流匹配的模块化神经网络框架，用于无缝整合X射线和中子散射的多模态测量数据以解决结构反演问题。
AI.motivation: X射线和中子散射实验通常记录没有相位信息的强度，导致反问题具有非唯一性。尽管结合互补测量可以减少这种模棱两可性，但将它们集成到机器学习框架中仍然具有挑战性。
AI.method: 引入了一种基于先验摊销流匹配的模块化框架，针对不同观测类型或物理探针单独训练单观测后验估计器，并在推理阶段通过组合采样器进行后期融合（late fusion）。
AI.result: 通过在X射线、飞行时间中子和极化中子反射率测量中的应用展示，该方法能够实现多个中子对比度的同构组合以及X射线和中子测量的异构多模态组合。
AI.conclusion: 基于组合流匹配的多模态散射反演框架能够有效结合X射线和中子散射的互补测量结果，实现考虑不确定性的精确结构表征，而无需重新训练联合模型。
AI.translation: X射线和中子散射对于凝聚态物理和材料科学中的结构表征不可或缺。然而，由于散射实验通常记录没有相位信息的强度，不同的结构可以产生相似的散射图样，从而导致相应的反问题具有非唯一性。这种模糊性可以通过结合互补测量来减少，但将它们整合到机器学习框架中仍然具有挑战性。在这里，我们引入了一种基于先验摊销流匹配的概率多测量分析模块化框架。单观测后验估计器针对各自的观测类型或物理探针进行单独训练，仅在推理时通过组合采样器进行组合。这种后期融合方法允许重复使用预训练的单观测模型，而无需进行专门的联合再训练。作为一个典型例子，我们考虑了反射率测量的应用，它提供了关于薄膜和界面的深度分辨率、纳米级的信息。我们的单观测演示涵盖了X射线、飞行时间中子和极化中子反射率测量的应用。在单独的联合精修研究中，任务匹配的估计器实现了多个中子对比度上的同构组合，以及X射线和中子测量的异构多模态组合。总之，这些结果确立了组合流匹配作为一种用于考虑不确定性的反演和联合精修的模块化方法，并具有在其他多个观测约束共同物理结构同时保留测量特定参数的散射问题中的潜在适用性。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了一种用于多模态X射线和中子散射反演的组合神经网络框架。通过采用基于流匹配的晚期融合方法，该框架能够在推理时将独立训练的单模态模型组合起来，从而在考虑不确定性的前提下有效解决散射测量的反演与联合精修问题。
AI.keywords: 多模态散射, 反演问题, 流匹配, 神经网络, 反射率测量
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地提出了一种基于先验摊销流匹配（prior-amortized flow matching）的模块化框架，通过晚期融合（late fusion）策略在推理阶段组合单模态模型，有效解决了多模态散射反演中的非唯一性和融合难题，具有很高的实用价值和扩展性。

title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
comments: Paper accepted for presentation at IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications 2026
summary: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.
comment: Paper accepted for presentation at IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications 2026

AI.title_translation: 精确共存：面向MIMO-ISAC的角-谱区域约束波形设计
AI.tldr: 提出了一种面向MIMO-ISAC系统的角-谱区域约束波形设计框架，实现与传统系统的精确电磁共存。
AI.motivation: 为了解决MIMO-ISAC系统在拥挤电磁环境中需要与占用特定频段和角扇区的传统系统（如定位传感器、海事雷达网、卫星通信链路）精确共存的问题。
AI.method: 将波形设计问题建模为非凸优化问题，并利用低复杂度的主要化-最小化交替方向乘子法（MM-ADMM）算法进行求解。
AI.result: 仿真结果表明，所提出的框架能够提供精确的传统系统保护，同时维持稳健的雷达感知和多用户通信性能。
AI.conclusion: 所提出的角-谱区域约束波形设计框架能够实现对传统系统的精确保护，同时保持强大的雷达感知和多用户通信性能。
AI.translation: 在本文中，我们为运行在拥挤电磁环境中的多输入多输出集成sensing和通信（MIMO-ISAC）系统开发了一个双功能波形设计框架。在此类环境中，双功能波形必须与占用特定频段和角扇区的传统系统（如局部定位传感器、海事雷达网络和卫星通信链路）共存。为了实现精确共存，我们结合了局部的角-谱区域约束，仅在每个传统系统所占用的角-频率区域内抑制波束成形能量，同时保留这些区域之外可用的空间自由度。由此产生的波形设计问题被建模为一个非凸优化问题，并使用低复杂度的主要化-最小化交替方向乘子法（MM-ADMM）算法进行求解。仿真结果表明，所提出的框架在保持强大的雷达感知和多用户通信性能的同时，提供了精确的传统系统保护。
AI.summary: 本文针对MIMO-ISAC系统提出了一种双功能波形设计框架，通过引入局部的角-谱区域约束，在特定角度和频率区域抑制波束成形能量以保护传统系统，同时保留外部的空间自由度，并采用MM-ADMM算法高效求解非凸优化问题。
AI.keywords: MIMO-ISAC, 波形设计, 频谱共存, 角-谱约束, 主导最小化交替方向乘子法
AI.comments: 该论文针对MIMO-ISAC系统在拥挤电磁环境中的共存问题，创新性地提出了基于角-谱区域约束的波形设计框架，并通过MM-ADMM算法有效解决了非凸优化问题，兼顾了传统系统保护与雷达/通信性能。

title: Probing Spatial and Spectral Grounding in EEG Foundation Models
comments: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: EEG foundation models are advancing at an unprecedented pace, yet their evaluation is driven by downstream accuracy, which reveals little about whether their predictions rely on physiologically interpretable signal structure. We introduce a set of perturbation probes in two grounding axes: spatial grounding in channel identity and topographic locality, and spectral grounding in oscillatory content and waveform morphology. We apply these probes to five published EEG foundation models across motor-imagery and seizure recordings. Our experiments reveal differences in both representational sensitivity and downstream reliance. Electrode identity may be encoded without influencing downstream classification: permuting LaBraM's positional codes heavily displaced its embeddings yet reduced motor-imagery accuracy by only 1.2 points, while spectral details may be discriminable without producing specific responses to simulated clinical markers, as only REVE exceeded a spectral baseline on this task. These dissociations are hidden in common benchmarks, demonstrating how grounding probes can complement performance-based evaluation by revealing what EEG foundation models encode and what their predictions depend on.
