title: Revealing Hidden Failure Modes in Chest X-ray Classification via Spectral Domain Analysis
summary: Deep learning models for chest X-ray anomaly detection remain vulnerable to subtle distributional shifts (e.g., acquisition technique, patient-related factors, and preprocessing). Traditional error analysis often relies on semantic metadata or model embeddings, which can mask low-level signal variations that degrade performance. In this work, we propose a data-centric framework for automated failure mode discovery using spectral analysis. We project images into the frequency domain and extract a compact profile summarizing the distribution of signal energy across frequency bands. By performing unsupervised clustering on these spectral profiles, we demonstrate that model failures are not randomly distributed, but are strongly concentrated within specific spectral clusters. This method effectively isolates "blind spots", enabling the prediction of model reliability and the discovery of performance-degrading data slices without requiring ground-truth failure annotations.

title: S-EDL: Eliciting Self-Evidence from Sequence Likelihoods for Semantic Calibration of LLMs
summary: Calibrating large language models (LLMs) in open-ended generation is uniquely challenging because many distinct token sequences can express the same underlying meaning. Prior calibration techniques target either fixed-set classification confidence or the binary correctness of individual strings, making them inherently ill-suited for the dynamic, multi-string nature of open-ended semantic outcomes. To bridge this gap, we introduce S-EDL, a novel evidential method that natively optimizes LLMs for semantic calibration. By eliciting evidence from the sequence likelihoods of the model itself, S-EDL constructs a differentiable Dirichlet prior over prompt-specific semantic classes. Optimizing the evidential loss under this prior yields a calibration-aware training signal over variable semantic classes, completely bypassing the need for fixed multiple-choice options. Evaluations across four open-ended benchmarks and three models demonstrate that S-EDL substantially reduces semantic calibration error while improving accuracy. By aligning generative likelihoods with semantic correctness, this work establishes a framework for deploying trustworthy LLMs in complex, open-ended applications. Code is available at: https://github.com/sandylaker/s-edl.

title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
summary: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.

title: AT-Differ: Dataset for Audio-Text Difference Captioning
summary: Evaluating audio-text semantic alignment is important in various audio-language tasks. Existing methods mainly quantify audio-text semantic alignment using a single score and cannot explicitly describe how audio and text differ. In this paper, we propose audio-text difference captioning, a task that generates textual descriptions of differences between audio and text. We also construct a new dataset AT-DIFFER containing audio-text pairs with systematically simulated differences and corresponding difference captions. Using AT-DIFFER, we fine-tune an existing multimodal large language model to describe differences between audio and text. The experimental results show that the original model has limited ability to describe such differences, whereas fine-tuning on AT-DIFFER substantially improves this ability.

title: Linear Self-Symmetries of Inverse-Based S-boxes: Generic Rigidity and Applications
summary: Finite-field inversion is a basic nonlinear building block in the design of S-boxes for symmetric cryptography. In inverse-based S-boxes, finite-field inversion is often combined with linear or affine layers that may preserve or destroy algebraic symmetries of the inverse function. We study how often nontrivial linear self-symmetries remain as the outer invertible linear transformation varies over \(GL_n(\mathbb F_2)\). Using the classification of two-sided linear equivalences of inversion, we reduce the problem to semilinear conjugacy and centralizer estimates. We obtain matching upper and lower bounds for the probability that a nontrivial linear self-symmetry remains, and these bounds determine its leading quadratic exponent. This exponent is governed by the smallest prime divisor of the extension degree. Thus the decay rate depends on the arithmetic of the field extension and not only on its dimension. As cryptographic applications, we provide a practical rigidity criterion, prove that the full AES S-box has no nontrivial linear self-symmetry, and illustrate the broader relevance of the framework through ARIA and Vision.

title: Spacetime Splines for Adaptive Robot Motions
summary: Movement primitives commonly represent robot mo- tions through basis functions indexed by time or phase. Inspired by spacetime representations employed in physics, we propose a spline-based formulation in which spatial geometry and temporal progression are represented within a common set of continuous variables. The proposed method jointly estimates a shared Bezier curve, while allowing spatial and temporal model complexity to be adapted independently (e.g., demonstration-specific phase modulation). As use case, we consider an alternating optimization process that simultaneously estimates path intervals observed in partial demonstrations. Simulation experiments demonstrate accurate joint recovery, refinement through modifications in model complexity and continuity, and improved robustness to variance in the demonstration set. Finally, we demonstrate online retiming and synchronization capabilities in a patient-turning task assisted by a robot, evaluated with a physical manikin.

title: Every Part Has Its Role: Part-of-Speech Effects in LLM Post-Training
summary: Large language models are typically trained with next-token prediction (NTP), which rewards predicting specific tokens rather than explicitly accounting for the semantic similarities between different words or expressions. Prior work has addressed this limitation by augmenting training data with minimally varying sentences that replace a target word with conceptually related alternatives, e.g., "The tired coach ran home" $\rightarrow$ {"The tired trainer ran home", "The tired instructor ran home", ...}. Such concept augmentation improves performance, but it remains unclear whether its effectiveness depends on where in the sentence the concept is expressed. We reproduce and extend prior work $\textit{beyond nouns}$ to verbs and adjectives, asking whether the part of speech (POS) carrying the concept signal affects perplexity and downstream performance. We find different patterns across evaluation settings: concept augmentation improves perplexity most consistently on news, independent of the POS used, whereas verbs provide the most reliable downstream gains. Despite these behavioral differences, representational analyses using CKA and linear probing show that the conditions yielding the largest downstream gains are not necessarily those that most alter the model's internal representations. Together, these results suggest that the effectiveness of concept augmentation depends on where and how conceptual information is introduced during training.

title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
comments: 9 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to ICRA 2027; under review
summary: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced.

title: How Do DiTs Denoise? An Aggregator-Predictor View of Attention and MLPs
summary: How do diffusion transformers (DiTs) represent image content and learn rules for reusing it to generalize? We develop an aggregator--predictor view of DiTs as input-adaptive local denoisers, in which context aggregation and patch prediction provide functional roles for interpreting attention and MLPs. We first establish that, for Gaussian Markov random field (GMRF) priors, the global Bayes denoiser can be approximated using only a subset of context patches, with error decaying exponentially in context radius. We further show that patchwise linear denoisers, often invoked to explain diffusion generalization, recover the empirical local denoiser with sufficiently informative aggregation. Within this view, AdaLN-modulated attention naturally parameterizes an input- and noise-dependent aggregator, while the MLP admits a learned key--value representation for tokenwise patch prediction. Our experiments support this view. DiTs trained on real images exhibit noise-dependent denoising contexts resembling those in the analytic GMRF setting, while attention mass exhibits a qualitatively corresponding broadening pattern. In a controlled CelebA64 study, shared-memory patch predictors used in place of DiT MLPs achieve competitive denoising and generative performance. Finally, cross-dataset component transplantation reveals compatibility patterns consistent with the proposed roles of QK in spatial weighting, VO in feature transport, and MLPs in patch prediction. Together, these results provide a component-level account of DiT denoising and motivate architecture-specific fine-tuning and controlled intervention.

title: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.

title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
summary: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.

title: Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents
comments: 29 pages, 5 figures. Source code, raw data, and recorded live demonstrations at https://github.com/pixee/flat-compaction-attacks-oct-2027
summary:
Coding agents that run long enough must compact their context, summarizing the conversation, discarding the original, and carrying the summary forward as memory. We show that in popular open-source coding agents this step is an exploitable trust boundary. Harnesses that flatten the typed conversation into a single plain string, marking each message with a text label such as [User]:, destroy message provenance in code, before the summarizer runs. An attacker who controls anything the agent reads can forge a user turn that survives compaction as a genuine instruction. Across five flattening harnesses (pi, opencode, Cline, Aider, OpenHands) the forged approval launders into the agent's memory 87-100% of the time, up to a ~908,000-token context window; across four role-typed harnesses (Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Continue) the identical attack succeeds 0% of the time. We follow the attack to executed consequences. A laundered standing approval drives real tool-running agents to execute attacker-controlled
  curl | sh in a sandbox, and end to end in the live pi TUI at ~50% against a 0% paired clean arm. The same channel reliably steers an agent's plan away from a file an attacker designates off-limits, which can blind a code review to a planted backdoor. Because the provenance is destroyed deterministically in harness code, no prompt-level defense can restore it; we measure a code-level provenance check that catches 77% of laundering while demoting 2% of legitimate summary content. The defect also has a straightforward fix at the serializer, escaping the role labels before flattening; the role-typed harnesses avoid it entirely by keeping messages role-typed.

title: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
summary: Coding agents can invest substantial effort in repository exploration and testing yet still produce unsuccessful patches. Existing online steering methods review trajectories periodically or invoke an advisor when a monitor detects behavioral problems; frequent reviews are costly, and the absence of anomalous behavior does not mean that an agent is on the right track. We propose PAUSE, a framework for steering coding agents with a single planning intervention. Agents reach their first source-code edit at a median of 60% of trajectory progress, after exploration, bug reproduction, and testing. PAUSE intercepts this edit request before it executes, which requires no learned monitor, no search over checkpoints, and no extra model call (search-free). A separate Planner reads the task and the pre-edit transcript and writes one repair plan; the same agent, the Executor, resumes with this plan, keeping its context and workspace. PAUSE applies online, during a live run, and offline, from a recorded trajectory prefix. We evaluate PAUSE on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual with two Executors and three agent harnesses. With Qwen3-coder as Executor and GPT-5.6 Sol as Planner, online steering improves resolution by 16.8% on Verified in OpenHands and by 14.7% on Multilingual in SWE-agent. In SWE-agent, PAUSE outperforms LivePlan, a rule-triggered advisor, by 3.2% on Verified and 3.7% on Multilingual at similar Planner cost, and is comparable to SICA's periodic overseer at about 11-15% of its Planner cost. Offline, PAUSE recovers 35.4% of eligible failed Verified tasks, and resuming from the recorded prefix uses 33-41% fewer Executor tokens than restarting.

title: Rigorous integration of semilinear parabolic PDEs: forward evolution bounds and projected boundary value problems
summary: In this work, we present a rigorous integrator for initial and boundary value problems for semilinear parabolic PDEs. The method builds on earlier semigroup-based approaches while improving the bounds used in the fixed-point argument and extending the class of problems that can be treated. In particular, it controls the solution operator without requiring backward integration of the variational equation and allows projected boundary value problems to be studied through a simplified construction of an approximate inverse for the linearized operator. To illustrate the scope of the method, we present three applications to the two-dimensional Ohta--Kawasaki equation. For two initial value problems, we prove global existence and obtain explicit enclosures valid for all sufficiently large times around numerical approximations of stripe and spot equilibria. These results use a fixed-point formulation on an unbounded time interval, avoiding the construction of trapping regions. We also rigorously solve a projected boundary value problem with endpoint conditions chosen from linear approximations of the unstable and stable spaces of two saddle equilibria. This provides a step toward the rigorous study of heteroclinic saddle-to-saddle connections.

title: Recovering Plausible Transmission Outage Scenarios
summary: Expansion planning for extreme weather needs outage scenarios that specify which transmission branches fail. However, public outage records often only report customers without power by county, making it unclear how to exploit this information to create outage scenarios. We propose a method to recover sets of outaged branches that most closely match regional load shed data. This gives us sets of plausible outages for a given hazard event. We formulate a bilevel problem with a load shedding DC optimal power flow in the lower level. We relax the binary branch states to differentiate the lower level problem, replace it with its sensitivity matrix, and use gradient descent to update the upper level. We treat the relaxed branch states as probabilities and perform randomized rounding to restore integrality. On three test systems with synthetic outages, the recovered sets reduce the load shed error to $0.02-4.5\%$. On the California Test System with storm data from December 2025, the error falls to $23\%$. These scenarios give expansion planning a reliable source of outage data tied to observed hazards.

title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
summary:
Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts.
  To address this, we propose HAWK, a transfer mechanism that enables rapid KV cache transfer across heterogeneous devices. HAWK establishes a remote direct memory access (RDMA) path for direct cross-device transfers while handling inter-device tensor layout discrepancies as part of the transfer process. In particular, HAWK allocates tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side to match the target tensor layout. Leveraging these buffers, HAWK orchestrates data transfer from a conventional contiguous GPU RDMA buffer to the corresponding NPU buffers, allowing transferred tensors to be consumed directly without additional data rearrangement while maintaining transfer efficiency. We implement and evaluate HAWK on a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, demonstrating performance within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26$\times$ higher power efficiency and 1.72$\times$ higher cost efficiency.

title: Coherent differentiation with a monoid of degrees: derivatives, Taylor expansion, finite differences...
summary: Coherent differentiation has been introduced a few years ago as a refinement of the (categorical semantics of the) differential lambda-calculus and of differential linear logic, compatible with the determinism of computation, and hence in categories where addition of morphisms in the hom-sets is only partially defined. In this setting differentiation is implemented by a kind of ''tangent functor'', with the difference that it maps an object to its object of summable tuples rather to a tangent bundle. In our earlier work, these tuples were pairs in the case of simple differentiation, and families indexed by integers when dealing with Taylor expansion and the Fa{à} di Bruno formula.  We push this idea further, considering now tuples indexed by an arbitrary commutative partial monoid satisfying a nonnegativity condition. The monoid structure on these indices plays a crucial role in the definition of the ''differential'' calculus associated with this ''tangent functor''. In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.

title: Stochastic Nonlinearities Improve Uncertainty Estimation
comments: Accepted to the British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC) 2026. 33 pages, including supplementary material
summary: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important across visual recognition tasks, providing information about the confidence and reliability of model predictions. Many uncertainty estimation methods obtain predictive diversity through mechanisms that can suppress intermediate features, perturb the input, or require substantial additional computation. Stochastic activation functions, where network units randomly select between multiple nonlinearities during a forward pass, have previously been used to improve optimization behavior, mitigate limitations of fixed ReLU activations, and increase output diversity. In this work, we reframe stochastic activation switching as a lightweight mechanism for uncertainty estimation. The proposed method samples between nonlinear activation functions, inducing predictive diversity while keeping intermediate feature pathways active. This enables uncertainty estimation from a single trained model without the training cost of ensembles, task-specific uncertainty heads, or architectural redesign. We evaluate the proposed approach across classification, semantic segmentation, and out-of-distribution detection using convolutional and transformer-based architectures on diverse datasets. Across these settings, stochastic activation switching improves uncertainty quality while preserving competitive primary-task performance, showing that stochastic nonlinearities provide an effective and information-preserving source of predictive variation for visual recognition.

title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
comments: 11 pages (main text), 42 pages (supplementary material), 2 main figures. Submitted to ICLR 2027
summary: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.

title: Characterizing and Defending Utility-Hijacking in Instruction-Tuning Data Selection
comments: An earlier version of this manuscript was submitted for peer review in July 2026
summary: Instruction-data selectors choose which instruction-following records are used for fine-tuning, improving alignment quality, raising training efficiency, and filtering out harmful records. A selector's choices thus directly affect the fine-tuned model's safety, yet despite their widespread use, the security of these selectors remains under-studied. We conduct the first systematic study of adaptive supplier-side attacks against utility-oriented instruction-data selectors and introduce utility-hijacking. Utility-hijacking shapes harmful records to remain compatible with a selector while preserving their malicious payload, causing top-k selection to concentrate rather than filter the poison. Achieving both is non-trivial, because optimizing a record for score tends to wash out its payload, while bluntly preserving the payload makes the record look low-value. Our generate-and-rerank procedure generates, per instruction, many payload-bearing candidates and submits only the highest-scoring survivor. Evaluated across three payloads (over-refusal, false-fact injection, and insecure code), six selectors, and victim models from Qwen2.5-7B to Qwen3-32B, utility-hijacking drives refusal from 0% to 94% and insecure code up to 56/90, while false-fact enrichment intensifies with scoring-model scale from 2.84x to 7.04x. To defend against this attack, we propose CONCERT, a targeted defense needing no content detector or poison labels. It flags suppliers selected far more often than chance allows, then re-selects under the same budget, keeping only records that two dissimilar selectors both rank highly. On a Qwen3-32B victim, CONCERT reverses the poison concentration from 6.67x to 0x (code) and 3.59x to 0.67x (facts), and reduces downstream harm by 100% and 75% respectively, at unchanged capability.

title: DynaCI: Generating GitHub Actions Workflows via Dynamic Analysis
summary: Continuous Integration (CI) is an essential practice that automatically validates code changes through builds and tests. However, configuring CI workflows remains challenging, as modern software often features complex architectures, numerous dependencies, and support for diverse execution environments. Most CI platforms also require workflows to be written in their particular domain-specific languages. As a result, CI workflows are often error-prone and hard to maintain, especially for those unfamiliar with CI semantics. Prior work on automated CI workflow generation require developers to create specifications that describe their intended workflows using natural language, partial workflows, etc. However, in practice, developers may struggle to articulate requirements and may be unaware of available CI features. To address these limitations, we propose DynaCI, a novel approach that uses runtime information from developers' local environments to generate CI workflows. DynaCI (i) traces the developers' local environment to collect runtime information, (ii) constructs an initial workflow by applying runtime-informed heuristics, and (iii) iteratively refines the workflow via LLM-based Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). We evaluate DynaCI on 50 popular Python projects that use GitHub Actions, a popular CI platform, and compare it against the state-of-the-art CI workflow generation approaches: GH-WCOM and LLM4GW. DynaCI outperforms these existing approaches by more than 21.13% in BLEU score and 20.96% in F1 score on average. It also generates workflows without missing functionality in 56% of cases, while requiring fewer manual modifications to repair such exceptions. These results demonstrate that leveraging runtime information substantially improves LLM-based CI workflow generation, and offer a promising direction for broader DevOps configuration automation.

AI.title_translation: DynaCI：通过动态分析生成GitHub Actions工作流
AI.tldr: DynaCI通过追踪本地环境的运行时信息并结合大语言模型RAG，自动化生成高质量的GitHub Actions工作流，显著优于现有方法。
AI.motivation: 配置CI工作流具有挑战性且容易出错，现有自动生成方法依赖开发者提供自然语言规范或部分工作流，但在实际中开发者往往难以准确表达需求或不了解可用的CI特性。
AI.method: (i) 追踪开发者本地环境以收集运行时信息，(ii) 应用基于运行时的启发式方法构建初始工作流，(iii) 通过基于LLM的检索增强生成（RAG）技术迭代细化工作流。
AI.result: 在50个流行的Python项目上，DynaCI的BLEU得分和F1得分平均超过现有先进方法21.13%和20.96%；在56%的情况下生成的工作流无功能缺失，且需要更少的手动修复。
AI.conclusion: 利用本地环境的运行时信息显著提升了基于大语言模型的CI工作流生成质量，为DevOps配置自动化提供了有前景的新方向。
AI.translation: 持续集成（CI）是通过构建和测试自动验证代码变更的核心实践。然而，配置CI workflow仍然具有挑战性，因为现代软件通常具有复杂的架构、众多的依赖项以及对多样化执行环境的支持。大多数CI平台还要求workflow使用其特定的领域特定语言编写。因此，CI workflow往往容易出错且难以维护，特别是对于不熟悉CI语义的人来说。先前关于自动生成CI workflow的工作要求开发人员使用自然语言、部分workflow等创建描述其预期workflow的规范。然而在实践中，开发人员可能难以阐述需求，并且可能不知道可用的CI功能。为了解决这些限制，我们提出了DynaCI，一种利用开发人员本地环境的运行时信息来生成CI workflow的新方法。DynaCI (i) 追踪开发人员的本地环境以收集运行时信息，(ii) 通过应用基于运行时的启发式方法构建初始workflow，以及 (iii) 通过基于大语言模型的检索增强生成（RAG）迭代细化workflow。我们在使用GitHub Actions（一个流行的CI平台）的50个流行Python项目上评估了DynaCI，并将其与最先进的CI workflow生成方法GH-WCOM和LLM4GW进行了比较。在平均BLEU得分和F1得分上，DynaCI分别优于这些现有方法21.13%和20.96%以上。它还在56%的情况下生成了没有功能缺失的workflow，同时需要较少的手动修改来修复此类异常。这些结果表明，利用运行时信息大大改进了基于大语言模型的CI workflow生成，并为更广泛的DevOps配置自动化提供了有前景的方向。
AI.summary: DynaCI提出了一种通过动态分析开发者本地环境来生成GitHub Actions工作流的新方法，它结合了运行时追踪、启发式初始化以及基于大语言模型的RAG迭代优化，在准确性和功能完整性上均显著优于现有技术。
AI.keywords: Continuous Integration, GitHub Actions, Dynamic Analysis, LLM, Retrieval Augmented Generation
AI.comments: DynaCI通过结合本地环境动态追踪与大语言模型RAG，有效解决了传统CI工作流配置复杂、开发者难以精确描述需求痛点，显著提升了工作流生成的准确性与自动化水平。

title: Investigating the Impact of Learner Errors on Social Bias in Large Language Models
summary: Existing social bias benchmarks evaluate large language models mostly on fluent, well-formed English, reflecting native speaker usage and leaving non-native writers unrepresented. To address this gap, we investigate how grammatical errors by non-native writers affect social bias. We develop a controlled framework that injects common learner errors into prompts and apply it to three bias benchmarks covering stereotype alignment and demographic preference across gender, race, and religion. We find that grammatical errors increase bias, and the effect grows with the error rate. Among the four common error types we consider, preposition errors produce the largest and most consistent increase in stereotype alignment. Our analysis suggests that errors increase bias when they are more likely to interfere with comprehension. Finally, fine-tuning on erroneous texts reduces the bias increase caused by grammatical errors. Our findings show that bias evaluations based exclusively on well-formed prompts may underestimate the bias experienced by users whose English contains grammatical errors.

AI.title_translation: 研究学习者错误对大语言模型中社会偏见的影响
AI.tldr: 本文发现非母语者的语法错误会加剧大语言模型的社会偏见，现有评估忽视了这一现象从而低估了非母语用户受到的偏见。
AI.motivation: 现有的社会偏见基准测试主要评估流利、规范的英语，反映了母语使用者的习惯，导致非母语写作者的表现在评估中被忽视，因此需要研究非母语者的语法错误如何影响大语言模型中的社会偏见。
AI.method: 开发了一个受控框架，将常见的学习者语法错误注入提示词中，并应用于三个涵盖性别、种族和宗教的刻板印象对齐和人口偏好的偏见基准测试中；同时测试了在错误文本上微调模型的效果。
AI.result: 语法错误会增加模型的社会偏见，且偏见程度随错误率增加而上升；其中介词错误产生最大且最一致的刻板印象对齐增加；错误在干扰理解时会加剧偏见；在错误文本上微调可以减少由语法错误引起的偏见增加。
AI.conclusion: 基于完美流利英语的偏见评估会低估非母语用户在使用大语言模型时所经历的实际社会偏见，未来的偏见评估和模型微调应将语言多样性和错误纳入考量。
AI.translation: 现有的社会偏见基准主要评估流利、规范的英语，这反映了母语使用者的习惯，使得非母语写作者在评估中没有得到体现。为了填补这一空白，我们研究了非母语写作者的语法错误如何影响社会偏见。我们开发了一个受控框架，将常见的学习者错误注入提示中，并将其应用于涵盖性别、种族和宗教的刻板印象对齐和人口偏好的三个偏见基准中。我们发现语法错误会增加偏见，并且这种影响随着错误率的增加而增大。在我们考虑的四种常见错误类型中，介词错误对刻板印象对齐产生了最大且最一致的增长。我们的分析表明，当错误更有可能干扰理解时，偏见会增加。最后，在错误文本上进行微调可以减少由语法错误引起的偏见增加。我们的研究结果表明，完全基于结构良好提示的偏见评估可能会低估英语包含语法错误的用户所经历的偏见。
AI.summary: 本文研究了非母语者的语法错误对大语言模型社会偏见的影响。研究发现，语法错误会加剧模型的偏见，且偏见随错误率增加而恶化，特别是介词错误影响最大。在错误文本上进行微调可以缓解这一问题。该研究表明，仅基于流利提示词的偏见评估会低估非母语用户面临的偏见。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 社会偏见, 语法错误, 非母语者, 偏见基准测试
AI.comments: 该研究首次系统性地探讨了非母语者的语法错误对大语言模型社会偏见的影响，填补了现有偏见基准测试多关注流利英语的空白，具有重要的现实意义和包容性。

title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
summary:
Haussler's covering lemma (JCTA 1995) gives the sharp $(C/δ)^d$ metric-entropy bound for binary VC classes under normalized $\ell_1$ distance. We prove a sharp global dynamic analogue for bounded real-valued classes in normalized $\ell_p$, for every $1\le p<\infty$. Writing $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$, we obtain a global dynamic cover of size at most $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ for every horizon and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Here a single family of deterministic causal experts, fixed independently of the instance sequence, covers every target on every sequence. For $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, a matching worst-case lower bound $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$ holds already for binary classes on one fixed sequence, even with real-valued experts. The constants are universal, independent of $p$.
  For $p=2$, this resolves the horizon-independent sequential $\ell_2$ covering problem of Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (PTRF 2015) in a stronger global form. For $p=1$, it gives the sharp $(C/δ)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ global dynamic covering bound for binary classes, resolving questions of Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Dagan, Moran, Naor, and Yogev (STOC 2021) and Malliaris and Moran (Trans. AMS 2024). Our proof combines rank-decreasing correction schedules and accurate sampled prefixes with exact continuations after target identification. Shared-parent routing distributes these continuations among eligible prefixes, eliminating the logarithmic overhead.

AI.title_translation: 一个尖锐的动态 Haussler 引理
AI.tldr: 本文证明了有界实值类在规范 $\ell_p$ 距离下的尖锐全局动态 Haussler 引理，解决了多个序贯覆盖与动态覆盖的公开问题。
AI.motivation: 为了寻找二进制VC类在规范 $\ell_1$ 距离下的尖锐度量熵界限的动态全局模拟，并解决 Rakhlin 等人以及 Alon 等人提出的关于序贯覆盖和全局动态覆盖的公开问题。
AI.method: 结合了秩递减修正调度、精确采样的前缀、目标识别后的精确延续，以及通过共享父路由在合格前缀间分配这些延续以消除对数开销的方法。
AI.result: 对于任意 $1\le p<\infty$ 和 $0<\varepsilon<1/2$，得到了大小至多为 $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ 的全局动态覆盖，并且当 $0<\varepsilon<1/4$ 时得到了匹配的最坏情况低界 $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$，通用常数与 $p$ 无关。同时解决了 $p=2$ 和 $p=1$ 时的多个公开问题。
AI.conclusion: 本文证明了关于有界实值函数类在规范 $\ell_p$ 距离下的尖锐全局动态 Haussler 引理，并给出了匹配的最坏情况下面积下界，从而完美解决了多个长期开放的问题。
AI.translation:
Haussler 的覆盖引理（JCTA 1995）给出了二进制 VC 类在规范 $\ell_1$ 距离下的尖锐 $(C/\delta)^d$ 度量熵界限。我们证明了针对规范 $\ell_p$ 中有界实值类的尖锐全局动态模拟，适用于每个 $1\le p<\infty$。令 $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$，对于每个视界和 $0<\varepsilon<1/2$，我们获得了大小至多为 $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ 的全局动态覆盖。这里，一组独立于实例序列固定的确定性因果专家家族，覆盖了每个序列上的每个目标。对于 $0<\varepsilon<1/4$，即使使用实值专家，在一条固定序列上的二进制类也已经成立了匹配的最坏情况低界 $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$。这些常数是通用的，且与 $p$ 无关。
对于 $p=2$，这以更强的全局形式解决了 Rakhlin、Sridharan 和 Tewari（PTRF 2015）提出的与视界无关的序贯 $\ell_2$ 覆盖问题。对于 $p=1$，它给出了二进制类的尖锐 $(C/δ)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ 全局动态覆盖界限，解决了 Alon、Ben-Eliezer、Dagan、Moran、Naor 和 Yogev（STOC 2021）以及 Malliaris 和 Moran（Trans. AMS 2024）的问题。我们的证明结合了秩递减修正调度、精确采样的前缀以及目标识别后的精确延续。共享-父路由将这些延续分配给合格的前缀，消除了对数开销。
AI.summary: 本文证明了有界实值类在规范 $\ell_p$ 距离下的尖锐全局动态 Haussler 引理，给出了大小为 $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ 的全局动态覆盖，并解决了学习理论中的多个公开问题。
AI.keywords: Haussler引理, 度量熵, 动态覆盖, 序贯学习, VC维
AI.comments: 该论文在学习理论和度量熵界限方面取得了重大突破，通过引入秩递减修正调度等新颖技术，解决了多个领域内长期存在的公开问题，具有很高的理论价值。

title: HuMiT: Low-Latency Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation via Compact Reference Tracking
comments: 7 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/
summary: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. Existing motion tracking policies typically require dense reference targets including full joint positions, body-part transformations, and even future frames, which tightly couples the controller to expensive upstream modules. In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames. Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/.
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/

AI.title_translation: HuMiT：基于紧凑参考追踪的低延迟全身人形机器人遥操作
AI.tldr: HuMiT通过使用当前帧的极简稀疏参考目标替代复杂的未来帧和密集关节数据，实现了人形机器人约20ms超低延迟的高保真全身遥操作。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于优化的重定向流程和未来帧调节机制引入了计算延迟，且传统的动作追踪策略需要密集的参考目标（如完整关节位置、身体部位变换和未来帧），导致控制器与昂贵的上游模块紧密耦合，难以实现低延迟的实时全身人形机器人遥操作。
AI.method: 提出了一种统一的追踪策略HuMiT，该策略摆脱了对完整关节位置、密集身体部位变换以及未来帧的依赖，仅需当前帧的根节点高度、根节点速度以及四个稀疏关键点的SE(3)位姿这几个紧凑的参考目标。
AI.result: 实验表明，该策略在不同动作类型下实现了约20毫秒的通信到推理延迟（头显流式传输与策略输出之间）以及65毫秒（中位数）的基于视频的光流延迟，并在Unitree G1人形机器人上成功验证了如接抛球等极速反应动作及协同移动操作能力。
AI.conclusion: HuMiT通过仅依赖当前帧的稀疏紧凑参考目标（根节点状态与四个稀疏关键点SE(3)位姿），成功实现了低延迟、高保真的全身人形机器人实时遥操作，并在Unitree G1上验证了其卓越的反应能力与协同全身操作性能。
AI.translation: 由于基于优化的重定向管线和未来帧条件机制带来的计算延迟，实时的全身人形机器人遥操作依然充满挑战。现有的动作追踪策略通常需要密集的参考目标（包括完整的关节位置、身体部位变换甚至未来帧），这使得控制器与昂贵的上游模块紧密耦合。在这项工作中，我们提出了HuMiT，这是一个建立在统一追踪策略上的全身遥操作系统，该策略仅需一个紧凑的参考目标（由当前帧的根节点高度、根节点速度以及四个稀疏关键点的SE(3)位姿组成），却能实现与依赖更丰富的参考状态（如完整关节位置、密集身体部位变换甚至未来帧）的方法相媲美的追踪保真度。实验表明，我们的策略在不同动作类型下实现了约20毫秒的通信到推理延迟（在头显流传输与策略输出之间测量）以及65毫秒（中位数）的基于视频的光流延迟。我们在Unitree G1人形机器人上验证了该系统，展示了如接住抛球等瞬间反应动作，以及协调的移动操作能力。项目网页：https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/。
AI.summary: 本文提出了HuMiT，这是一个用于低延迟全身人形机器人遥操作的系统。通过引入仅需当前帧稀疏紧凑参考目标的统一追踪策略，该系统在减少对昂贵上游模块和未来帧依赖的同时，实现了与依赖密集参考方法相媲美的追踪保真度，并在Unitree G1机器人上验证了其出色的实时反应与操作性能。
AI.keywords: 人形机器人, 全身遥操作, 动作追踪, 低延迟, 运动重定向
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的紧凑参考动作追踪策略（HuMiT），极大地降低了人形机器人全身遥操作系统的计算延迟与通信负担，在保持高追踪精度的同时实现了毫秒级的超低延迟响应。

title: ViBMR: A Large-Scale Multi-Sequence Brain MRI Dataset and Comprehensive Evaluation for Vietnamese Radiology Report Generation
comments: Accepted at IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)
summary: Automated radiology report generation for multi-sequence brain MRI holds strong promise for alleviating radiologists' workload, yet it remains a demanding problem: brain MRI studies are inherently volumetric, each pulse sequence carries complementary diagnostic information, and annotated data are critically scarce for low-resource clinical languages. Existing brain MRI-report resources are still dominated by English reports, translated clinical text, or datasets adapted from task-specific imaging benchmarks, leaving routine low-resource clinical reporting and heterogeneous multi-sequence MRI protocols insufficiently represented. To bridge this gap, we introduce ViBMR, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale multi-sequence brain MRI dataset paired with routine Vietnamese clinical reports, comprising 3,649 patients and 11,875 MRI series across T1, T2, FLAIR, and contrast-enhanced T1 sequences. Building on ViBMR, we establish a comprehensive evaluation setup for brain MRI report generation, covering representative medical vision-language models, multi-sequence inputs, and feature aggregation strategies. The results provide key insights into dataset characteristics and model behavior, while demonstrating the necessity of native low-resource clinical datasets for reliable Vietnamese-origin brain MRI report generation. Our dataset and baseline models will be released for non-commercial research.
