AI.title_translation: ASPIRE：面向机器人的智能体技能发现
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为ASPIRE的持续学习系统，通过智能体自主探索、代码编写与技能库积累，大幅提升了机器人在各类复杂操作任务中的成功率与泛化能力。
AI.motivation: 传统的机器人编程具有极大挑战性，需要协调多模态感知、处理物理接触动力学、应对环境配置多样性及执行失败，因此需要一个能够自主编写、精炼控制程序并积累可复用技能的持续学习系统。
AI.method: 提出ASPIRE系统，包含三个核心组件：(1) 提供多模态追踪的闭环机器人执行引擎；(2) 持续扩展的可复用技能库；(3) 超越单轨迹精炼的进化搜索程序。
AI.result: 在操作扰动任务上超越先前方法高达77%，Robosuite双手交接任务提升72%，长视距家庭任务提升达32%；在零样本长视距任务泛化上达到31%成功率（先前方法仅4%）；结合Claude Opus 5.5在LIBERO-Pro、Robosuite和BEHAVIOR-1K任务上实现了极高的成功率。
AI.conclusion: ASPIRE能够通过自主探索和迭代精炼，高效发现和演进机器人控制程序及可复用技能库，显著提升机器人在复杂环境下的操作成功率和泛化能力。
AI.translation: 传统的机器人编程非常具有挑战性：它需要协调多模态感知、管理物理接触动力学、处理多样化的环境配置以及应对执行失败。我们介绍了ASPIRE（基于迭代机器人探索的智能体技能编程），这是一个持续学习系统，它在代码即策略范式下自主编写和精炼机器人控制程序，同时将经验沉淀为可复用的技能库。ASPIRE在一个开放式学习循环中运行，包含三个组件：（1）一个公开细粒度多模态追踪的闭环机器人执行引擎，使智能体能够自主诊断故障、综合修复并验证结果；（2）一个持续扩展的技能库，将验证过的修复方案提炼为可复用、可迁移的机器人知识；（3）一个进化搜索程序，生成多样化的程序，系统地对其进行调试，以探索超越单轨迹精炼的方法。在受到扰动的操作任务上，ASPIRE超越先前方法高达77%，在Robosuite的双手交接任务上提升72%，在长视距家庭任务上提升达32%。积累的技能库进一步实现了零样本泛化：在具代表性的未见长视距任务上，ASPIRE实现了31%的成功率，优于先前方法的4%成功率。性能随前沿模型的能力而扩展。借助Claude Opus 5.5，ASPIRE几乎饱和了这些基准，在所有80个LIBERO-Pro任务上取得了99%的平均成功率，并在具代表性的Robosuite和BEHAVIOR-1K任务上取得了100%的成功率。除了仿真之外，在仿真中发现的技能减少了跨具身和机器人API的真实世界机器人编程工作量，而通过与物理机器人进行在线交互获得的技能使ASPIRE能够以逐步提高的效率解决魔方问题。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了ASPIRE（基于迭代机器人探索的智能体技能编程），这是一个持续学习系统，能够在代码即策略范式下自主编写和精炼机器人控制程序，并将经验积累到可复用的技能库中，从而显著提升机器人在复杂和未知环境中的任务执行与泛化能力。
AI.keywords: 机器人技能发现, 代码即策略, 持续学习, 具身智能, 进化搜索
AI.comments: 本文提出了ASPIRE系统，通过代码即策略范式和持续学习，自动发现和提炼机器人操作技能，在多项仿真和真实世界基准测试中展现出卓越的性能和泛化能力。其创新之处在于将大语言模型的代码生成能力与机器人的持续探索、错误诊断和技能库积累有机结合。

title: The Binary Tree Mechanism is Optimal for Differentially Private Continual Counting
summary:
Private continual counting is a fundamental problem in differential privacy: given a binary stream of length $n$, where each $1$ corresponds to the contribution of one individual, the goal is to release all running counts while protecting the privacy of each individual. For fixed privacy parameters, the standard binary tree mechanism achieves expected $\ell_\infty$ error $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ under approximate differential privacy and $O(\log^2 n)$ under pure differential privacy. Whether these dependences on the stream length are necessary has remained a central open problem.
  For fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, we prove a lower bound of $Ω(\log^{3/2} n)$ under approximate DP with sufficiently small fixed $δ>0$, and a lower bound of $Ω(\log^2 n)$ under pure DP. These bounds establish the optimality of the binary tree mechanism in both settings. The bounds hold for arbitrary mechanisms, even when the entire stream is available in advance. Both proofs use the same decomposition and accumulation of residual noise along a tree.
  As a consequence of the approximate-DP bound, we also obtain a largest-possible separation between hereditary discrepancy and private $\ell_\infty$ error for linear queries, showing that the known general upper bound in terms of hereditary discrepancy has the optimal dependence on the number of queries.

AI.title_translation: 二叉树机制对于差分隐私连续计数是最优的
AI.tldr: 该论文证明了二叉树机制在差分隐私连续计数中是渐近最优的，解决了该领域的一个核心开放问题。
AI.motivation: 长期以来，标准二叉树机制在差分隐私连续计数中达到的 $\ell_\infty$ 误差上界（近似DP下 $O(\log^{3/2} n)$，纯DP下 $O(\log^2 n)$）是否为最优一直是一个核心开放问题，该研究旨在解决这一理论空白。
AI.method: 通过在树结构上对残差噪声进行分解与累加，建立了针对任意机制的下界证明（在近似DP下为 $\Omega(\log^{3/2} n)$，在纯DP下为 $\Omega(\log^2 n)$）。
AI.result: 证明了近似DP下的 $\Omega(\log^{3/2} n)$ 下界和纯DP下的 $\Omega(\log^2 n)$ 下界，确立了二叉树机制在两种设置下的最优性，并得出了线性查询下遗传差异与私有 $\ell_\infty$ 误差之间最大可能分离的推论。
AI.conclusion: 二叉树机制在差分隐私连续计数问题中被证明是渐近最优的，分别在近似和纯差分隐私下达到了理论下限。
AI.translation:
私有连续计数是差分隐私中的一个基本问题：给定一个长度为 $n$ 的二进制流，其中每个 $1$ 对应一个个体的贡献，其目标是在保护每个个体隐私的同时发布所有运行计数。对于固定的隐私参数，标准的二叉树机制在近似差分隐私下实现了期望的 $\ell_\infty$ 误差 $O(\log^{3/2} n)$，在纯差分隐私下实现了 $O(\log^2 n)$。这些对流长度的依赖是否必要，一直是一个核心的开放问题。
对于固定的 $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$，我们证明了在具有足够小固定 $\delta>0$ 的近似 DP 下 $\Omega(\log^{3/2} n)$ 的下界，以及在纯 DP 下 $\Omega(\log^2 n)$ 的下界。这些界限确立了二叉树机制在这两种设置下的最优性。这些界限适用于任意机制，甚至在整个流提前可用时也成立。两个证明都使用了沿树的残差噪声的相同分解和累积。
作为近似 DP 界限的结果，我们还获得了线性查询的遗传差异与私有 $\ell_\infty$ 误差之间最大可能的分离，表明关于遗传差异的已知一般上界对查询数量具有最优的依赖性。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了差分隐私下的连续计数问题，通过证明下界，首次确立了标准二叉树机制在纯差分隐私和近似差分隐私下均具有渐近最优性。
AI.keywords: 差分隐私, 连续计数, 二叉树机制, 最优性, 下界证明
AI.comments: 该论文解决了差分隐私连续计数领域长期存在的开放性问题，通过证明下限完美匹配了标准二叉树机制的误差界，证明了二叉树机制在近似和纯差分隐私下的最优性，具有极高的理论价值。

title: On the algebraic analysis of runtime distribution of probabilistic programs
summary: We present an algebraic method for analyzing probabilistic programs with counters and discrete states, Generalized Constant Probability (GCP) programs. We define the operational semantics of GCP in terms of the runs of a type of probabilistic pushdown automata (pPDAs). We characterize the resulting (sub-)probability generating function (pgf) $Δ(z)$ as an algebraic function, representable via the roots of a kernel polynomial associated with the program. Next, we provide algorithms that, leveraging this information, compute under mild algebraic conditions the dominant singularities and the exact radius of convergence of $Δ(z)$, leading to an exact asymptotic expansion and to exponential bounds for its coefficients. Our approach is sound for GCP programs and complete for the single-state subclass.

AI.title_translation: 概率程序运行时分布的代数分析研究
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于代数方法的框架，用于分析概率程序的运行时分布，并能计算出精确的渐近展开式和指数界。
AI.motivation: 为了解决分析带有计数器和离散状态的概率程序的运行时分布的问题，提供一种严谨且系统化的代数分析方法。
AI.method: 定义了GCP程序的操作语义（基于概率下推自动机），将概率生成函数表征为代数函数，并设计算法计算其主奇异点、收敛半径、渐近展开和指数界。
AI.result: 将（次）概率生成函数表征为可通过核多项式根表示的代数函数，并在温和的代数条件下开发了计算主奇异点和收敛半径的算法，得出精确的渐近展开和指数界。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功建立了一种分析GCP程序运行时分布的代数框架，不仅能够表征概率生成函数，还能有效计算其主奇异点、收敛半径及渐近展开。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一种用于分析具有计数器和离散状态的概率程序——广义常概率（GCP）程序的代数方法。我们根据一类概率下推自动机（pPDAs）的运行定义了GCP的操作语义。我们将所得的（次）概率生成函数（pgf）$\Delta(z)$表征为一个代数函数，该函数可通过与程序相关联的核多项式的根来表示。接着，我们提供了相关算法，在温和的代数条件下利用这些信息计算 $\Delta(z)$ 的主奇异点和精确收敛半径，从而得出其系数的精确渐近展开式和指数界。我们的方法对于GCP程序是可靠的，对于单状态子类是完备的。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种针对具有计数器和离散状态的概率程序（GCP程序）的代数分析方法。通过将语义建模为概率下推自动机并利用概率生成函数，该方法能够精确计算程序的渐近展开和运行时分布的指数界。
AI.keywords: 概率程序, 运行时分布, 代数方法, 概率下推自动机, 生成函数
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的代数方法来分析带计数器和离散状态的概率程序（GCP程序），通过将概率下推自动机与概率生成函数相结合，能够精确计算渐近展开和指数界，对概率程序的运行时分布研究具有重要意义。

title: Learning When to Automate: Queue Control in Human-AI Service Systems
summary: We study a human-AI service system in which tasks arrive sequentially and are processed through a two-stage architecture: an automated chatbot followed, when necessary, by a human agent. We consider $T$ sequentially arriving tasks, each belonging to one of $K$ heterogeneous types. For each task the decision maker chooses how many resources to allocate to the chatbot, whose type-dependent success probabilities are initially unknown. Tasks not resolved by the chatbot enter type-dependent human-service queues, where they are processed by a human agent with unknown service rates. This model captures a central tradeoff in hybrid service systems: relying more on automation reduces human congestion but increases chatbot costs, while insufficient automation may overload the human agent. We propose the UCB-DPP policy, which combines Upper Confidence Bounds with Drift-Plus-Penalty control to learn the unknown parameters of the system while making queue-aware decisions. We prove that UCB-DPP achieves regret $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(K\sqrt{T})$ and guarantees mean-rate stability of the human-service queues. Simulations on synthetic instances show that the proposed policy outperforms natural baselines.

AI.title_translation: 学习何时自动化：人机服务系统中的队列控制
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为UCB-DPP的策略，用于解决人机服务系统中未知参数学习与队列稳定性的权衡问题，实现了低遗憾界和队列稳定性。
AI.motivation: 研究人机协同服务系统中如何平衡自动化与人类服务：过度依赖自动化会增加成本，而自动化不足则会导致人类代理过载，同时系统的聊天机器人成功率和人类服务速率初始时是未知的，需要进行学习。
AI.method: 提出了UCB-DPP策略，将上置信界（Upper Confidence Bounds）与漂移加惩罚（Drift-Plus-Penalty）控制相结合，以在做出队列感知决策的同时学习系统的未知参数。
AI.result: 证明了UCB-DPP策略实现了 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(K\sqrt{T})$ 的遗憾界（regret），并保证了人类服务队列的均值速率稳定性；合成实例仿真表明该策略优于自然基线方法。
AI.conclusion: 通过提出的UCB-DPP策略，该研究成功实现了人机服务系统中未知参数的高效学习与队列稳定，达到了 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(K\sqrt{T})$ 的遗憾界，仿真实验也证明了其优越性。
AI.translation: 我们研究了一个人机服务系统，其中任务按顺序到达并通过两阶段架构进行处理：首先是自动化聊天机器人，必要时由人工代理跟进。我们考虑 $T$ 个顺序到达的任务，每个任务属于 $K$ 个异构类型之一。对于每个任务，决策者选择分配多少资源给聊天机器人，其类型依赖的成功概率最初是未知的。未被聊天机器人解决的任务进入类型依赖的人工服务队列，由具有未知服务速率的人工代理处理。该模型捕捉了混合服务系统中一个核心权衡：更多地依赖自动化可以减少人工拥挤但增加聊天机器人成本，而自动化不足可能会使人工代理过载。我们提出了 UCB-DPP 政策，它将上置信界（Upper Confidence Bounds）与漂移加惩罚（Drift-Plus-Penalty）控制结合起来，在做出队列感知决策的同时学习系统的未知参数。我们证明了 UCB-DPP 实现了 $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(K\sqrt{T})$ 的遗憾界，并保证了人工服务队列的均值速率稳定性。对合成实例的仿真表明，所提出的策略优于自然基线。
AI.summary: 本文研究了包含聊天机器人和人工代理的两阶段人机服务系统中的任务自动化决策问题。针对聊天机器人成功率和人类服务速率未知的情况，作者提出了UCB-DPP策略，在动态学习未知参数的同时进行队列感知的资源分配。理论分析证明了该策略能够达到次线性的遗憾界并保证队列稳定，仿真结果验证了其有效性。
AI.keywords: 人机服务系统, 队列控制, 强化学习, 遗憾界, 自动化分配
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的UCB-DPP策略，结合了上置信界（UCB）和漂移加惩罚（Drift-Plus-Penalty）控制，解决了人机协同服务系统中未知参数学习与队列稳定性的核心权衡问题，具有很强的理论和实际应用价值。

title: When Does Tool Use Increase the Expressive Power of Finite-Precision Recurrent Models?
summary: Modern sequence models are increasingly deployed as agents that interleave token generation with calls to external tools. We study when such tool access increases computational expressivity. We model any fixed finite-precision recurrent sequence model, including finite-precision state-space models (SSMs) with $B$ bits of internal state, as a deterministic finite-state controller interacting with an oracle through a finite command/observation interface, and establish a separation between the two regimes analyzed. First, every finite-state bounded-interface tool with memory set $M$ can be internalized at a cost of at most $\lceil\log_2|M|\rceil+O(1)$ recurrent bits, so the combined system remains finite-state. Second, a single unbounded tape with only local $\mathtt{read}$/$\mathtt{write}$/$\mathtt{move}$ commands suffices for Turing completeness: every single-tape Turing machine with state set $Q$ and tape alphabet $Γ$ is simulated by a controller with $O(\log|Q|+\log|Γ|)$ recurrent bits, and $\mathrm{EQ}_n$ requires $2^n$ states without tools but one constant-size controller with the tape. Third, this construction is realized exactly by a one-layer finite-precision \emph{selective} affine SSM with binary one-hot states, $\{0,1\}$ transition matrices, and zero biases. Under explicitly stated resource conventions, $O(\log B)$ recurrent bits suffice for tape-assisted simulation of any $B$-state Turing machine, whereas directly realizing an arbitrary $B$-state transition map in one exact affine update without external memory requires total recurrent dimension exactly $B-1$. Fixed description size, occupied tape cells, and interaction cost are reported separately from recurrent memory. Our results concern exact expressivity under deterministic semantics, not learnability or empirical performance.

AI.title_translation: 工具使用何时能增加有限精度循环模型的表达能力？
AI.tldr: 本文从理论上证明了外部工具的使用如何将有限精度的循环序列模型（如状态空间模型）从有限状态提升至图灵完备，并分析了所需的内存和资源代价。
AI.motivation: 现代序列模型越来越多地与外部工具交互，但工具访问究竟在何种条件下以及如何增加计算表达能力，目前缺乏严格的理论研究。
AI.method: 将固定有限精度的循环序列模型建模为与外部预言机交互的确定性有限状态控制器，通过分析有界工具内存与无界纸带指令，研究其等价性和模拟能力，并用选择性仿射SSM进行了具体实现。
AI.result: 研究发现：1. 具有内存大小 $M$ 的有限状态有界接口工具可被内部化，增加至多 $\lceil\log_2|M|\rceil+O(1)$ 个循环比特；2. 具有局部读/写/移动命令的单一无界纸带可实现图灵完备性，控制器仅需 $O(\log|Q|+\log|Γ|)$ 个循环比特；3. 这一构造可通过一层有限精度选择性仿射SSM精确实现，相比直接实现需要更少的循环维度。
AI.conclusion: 论文证明了有界工具可以被模型内部化，而无界纸带（图灵机）则能将有限精度的循环模型提升至图灵完备，且具有极高的资源效率（对数级的内部状态需求）。
AI.translation: 现代序列模型越来越多地被部署为代理，将token生成与外部工具调用交织在一起。我们研究了这种工具访问何时能增加计算表达能力。我们将任何固定的有限精度循环序列模型（包括具有 $B$ 位内部状态的有限精度状态空间模型 SSM）建模为与通过有限命令/观测接口与预言机交互的确定性有限状态控制器，并在分析的两种机制之间建立了分离。首先，每个具有内存集 $M$ 的有限状态有界接口工具都可以以内化成本至多 $\lceil\log_2|M|\rceil+O(1)$ 个循环比特的代价实现，因此组合系统仍然是有限状态的。其次，仅具有局部 $\mathtt{read}$/$\mathtt{write}$/$\mathtt{move}$ 命令的单个无界纸带就足以实现图灵完备性：具有状态集 $Q$ 和纸带字母表 $\Gamma$ 的每个单带图灵机都可以由具有 $O(\log|Q|+\log|\Gamma|)$ 个循环比特的控制器模拟，并且 $\mathrm{EQ}_n$ 在没有工具的情况下需要 $2^n$ 个状态，但在有纸带的情况下只需要一个常数大小的控制器。第三，该构造由具有二进制独热状态、$\{0,1\}$ 转移矩阵和零偏置的一层有限精度“选择性”仿射SSM精确实现。在显式陈述的资源约定下，$O(\log B)$ 个循环比特足以对任何 $B$ 状态图灵机进行纸带辅助模拟，而在一个精确的仿射更新中直接实现任意 $B$ 状态转移映射需要正好 $B-1$ 的总循环维度。固定描述大小、占用的纸带单元和交互成本与循环内存分开报告。我们的结果涉及确定性语义下的精确表达能力，而不是可学习性或经验性能。
AI.summary: 本文研究了外部工具访问对具有有限内部状态的循环序列模型（如状态空间模型）计算表达能力的影响。研究表明，有界工具可以被模型以对数级比特的代价内部化，而配备无界纸带则能赋予模型图灵完备性，且只需极少的循环状态即可模拟复杂的图灵机。
AI.keywords: 工具使用, 表达能力, 循环模型, 状态空间模型, 图灵完备
AI.comments: 该论文从理论计算机科学的角度，严格分析了工具使用对有限精度循环序列模型（如状态空间模型SSM）计算表达能力的影响，区分了有界工具与无界工具（图灵机）的不同效果。这为理解大模型与外部工具交互的本质提供了重要的理论基础。

title: Hilti-Trimble-Oxford Dataset: 360 Visual-Inertial Benchmark with Floor Plan Priors for SLAM and Localization
summary: Automated progress monitoring on construction sites is an active area of research and development. Robot and human-carried mapping systems have been developed to build 3D maps of building and infrastructure projects. While LiDAR-based mapping systems achieve high accuracy, the cost of LiDAR can be prohibitive. Consumer-grade cameras with wide field of view ("360 cameras") combined with embedded inertial measurement units (IMUs) provide a cost-effective alternative. To support change detection and progress monitoring, highly accurate visual simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) and floor plan localization systems are required. In this paper, we present a high-quality dataset collected at an active construction site, which captures realistic challenges such as variable lighting conditions, moving workers, fast motions, and repetitive structures. The dataset offers thirty visual-inertial sequences recorded across ten floors over an eight-month period of the construction project. Ground truth trajectories are collected using a high quality LiDAR-inertial SLAM system rigidly attached to the 360 camera. Additionally, we report the results of an open research challenge evaluating the best visual SLAM and localization systems from around the world. The Challenge attracted substantially higher participation in SLAM, with 62 teams compared to 22 in floor plan localization, which suggests that this task receives less attention from researchers and motivates further exploration through proposed dataset and challenge, available at: https://hilti-trimble-challenge.com/dataset-2026.

AI.title_translation: Hilti-Trimble-Oxford数据集：用于SLAM和定位的带有楼层平面图先验的360度视觉惯性基准
AI.tldr: 本文推出了一个包含楼层平面图先验的360度视觉惯性建筑工地数据集与挑战赛，旨在推动SLAM和室内定位技术的发展。
AI.motivation: 虽然基于LiDAR的系统精度高但成本过高，而消费级360度相机结合IMU是经济高效的替代方案，但缺乏针对建筑工地复杂环境（如可变光照、移动工人、重复结构等）的高质量基准数据集来支持高精度的视觉SLAM和楼层平面图定位系统。
AI.method: 使用刚性连接360度相机和高精度LiDAR惯性SLAM系统的设备，在活跃的建筑工地收集了跨越十个楼层、历时八个月的30个视觉惯性序列，并举办了开放式研究挑战赛进行评估。
AI.result: 成功收集了30个跨度8个月的序列，并通过开放挑战赛吸引了大量研究团队参与（SLAM组62支队伍，楼层平面图定位组22支队伍），证明了该数据集对推动相关领域研究的有效性。
AI.conclusion: 通过发布Hilti-Trimble-Oxford数据集及开放式研究挑战赛，本文填补了建筑工地环境下360视觉惯性SLAM和楼层平面图定位基准的空白，并指出楼层平面图定位任务相对较少受到关注，亟需进一步研究。
AI.translation: 建筑工地上的自动化进度监测是一个活跃的研究与开发领域。人们已经开发出机器人和人工携带的测绘系统来构建建筑和基础设施项目的3D地图。虽然基于LiDAR的测绘系统能达到高精度，但LiDAR的成本可能会令人望而却步。具有宽视场角的消费级相机（“360度相机”）与嵌入式惯性测量单元（IMU）相结合，提供了一种经济高效的替代方案。为了支持变更检测和进度监测，需要高度精确的视觉同时定位与建图（SLAM）以及楼层平面图定位系统。在本文中，我们提出了一个在活跃建筑工地收集的高质量数据集，捕捉了现实世界的挑战，如可变的光照条件、移动的工人、快速运动和重复的结构。该数据集提供了在一个建筑项目八个月期间跨越十个楼层记录的三十个视觉惯性序列。真实轨迹是使用刚性附着在360度相机上的高质量LiDAR惯性SLAM系统采集的。此外，我们报告了一项开放研究挑战赛的结果，该挑战赛评估了来自世界各地的最佳视觉SLAM和定位系统。该挑战赛在SLAM方面吸引了极高的参与度，有62支队伍参加，而楼层平面图定位只有22支队伍，这表明该任务受到的研究人员关注较少，并通过所提出的数据集和挑战赛激发进一步的探索。
AI.summary: 本文推出了Hilti-Trimble-Oxford数据集，这是一个在活跃建筑工地采集的、包含楼层平面图先验的360度视觉惯性基准数据集，旨在支持SLAM和精细化定位研究，并总结了相关开放挑战赛的结果。
AI.keywords: 360相机, 视觉惯性SLAM, 建筑进度监测, 楼层平面图定位, 数据集
AI.comments: 该论文提供了一个具有挑战性的真实建筑工地360度视觉惯性数据集，结合了楼层平面图先验，对于推动SLAM和室内定位技术在建筑自动化监测中的应用具有重要价值。

title: Trees from Marginals: Autoregressive drafting with factorized priors
summary: Speculative decoding greatly increases the interactivity of autoregressive language models by trading off computation for extra tokens generated in a single forward pass. Factorized draft models are especially efficient because they predict future-token marginals in parallel, but their independence assumption causes acceptance rates to degrade sharply as the speculative budget grows. We analyze this limitation and introduce Weaver, a lightweight autoregressive adapter that constructs proposal trees from the top-K marginals of a factorized drafter. Weaver restores conditional dependencies between proposed tokens while avoiding a full-vocabulary projection. To support fast verification for models with Gated Delta Net layers, we derive a rollback-free tree-verification algorithm and implement optimized CUDA kernels in SGLang. By combining these model and systems contributions we achieve a 4.08-fold speedup over autoregressive decoding, and outperform a highly optimized DFlash baseline by 16.3%.

AI.title_translation: 基于边缘概率的树结构：带因式分解先验的自回归起草
AI.tldr: 提出Weaver适配器和无回溯树验证算法，通过从因式分解草稿模型的边缘概率构建提议树恢复条件依赖，大幅提升了语言模型的推测解码速度。
AI.motivation: 因式分解草稿模型能够高效并行预测未来Token的边缘概率，但由于其独立性假设，当推测预算增长时，接受率会急剧下降。为了克服这一局限性，本研究旨在恢复预测Token之间的条件依赖关系，同时避免全词表投影。
AI.method: 引入Weaver轻量级自回归适配器，从因式分解草稿模型的Top-K边缘概率构建提议树以恢复条件依赖；为带有Gated Delta Net层的模型推导了无回溯的树验证算法，并在SGLang中实现了优化的CUDA内核。
AI.result: 实现了4.08倍的自回归解码加速，并且比高度优化的DFlash基线性能提升了16.3%。
AI.conclusion: Weaver成功解决了因式分解草稿模型在较大推测预算下接受率下降的问题，配合针对Gated Delta Net层设计的无回溯树验证算法和优化CUDA内核，实现了显著的解码加速。
AI.translation: 推测解码通过权衡计算资源以在单次前向传递中生成额外的Token，极大地提高了自回归语言模型的交互性。因式分解的草稿模型特别高效，因为它们并行预测未来Token的边缘概率，但它们的独立性假设导致接受率随着推测预算的增长而急剧下降。我们分析了这一局限性，并介绍了Weaver，这是一个轻量级的自回归适配器，它从因式分解草稿模型的Top-K边缘概率构建提议树。Weaver恢复了所提议Token之间的条件依赖关系，同时避免了全词表投影。为了支持对带有Gated Delta Net层模型的快速验证，我们推导了一种无回溯的树验证算法，并在SGLang中实现了优化的CUDA内核。通过结合这些模型和系统的贡献，我们实现了比自回归解码快4.08倍的加速，并且性能超越了高度优化的DFlash基线16.3%。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了Weaver，一种用于自回归草稿的轻量级自回归适配器，能够从因式分解草稿模型的边缘概率中构建提议树，恢复条件依赖。结合无回溯树验证算法和优化CUDA内核，该方法显著提升了语言模型的推测解码速度和性能。
AI.keywords: 推测解码, 自回归语言模型, 树状提案, 因式分解先验, CUDA内核优化
AI.comments: 该论文巧妙地结合了因式分解草稿模型的并行优势与自回归模型的条件依赖恢复，通过引入Weaver适配器和优化的树验证算法，在保持高效的同时显著提升了推测解码的接受率和整体加速比。

title: Evaluating Grid Resilience in the Era of Ever-Increasing Data Centers
comments: 8 pages, 2 figures, accepted for Dynamic Data Driven Applications Systems (DDDAS) 6th International Conference
summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence workloads is increasing the scale and concentration of data center demand, creating new concerns for power system resilience under disruptive events. This paper extends a validated multi-time-step DC optimal power flow framework to evaluate the impact of aggregated data center demand on contingency-induced unserved energy. Using an IEEE 30-bus system with flexible resources, we replace a conventional load at a contingency-exposed bus with an energy-matched constant data center load and examine two capacity-growth levels under generator derating, transmission line derating, and coupled derating. The results show that data center capacity growth substantially increases both system-level and data-center-bus unserved energy under transmission-constrained contingencies. Under coupled derating, the high-growth case increases total unserved energy from 3.203 MWh in the energy-matched case to 22.891 MWh. A supplementary energy-matched coincident-demand case further increases total unserved energy by 34.4%, indicating that temporally concentrated data center demand can amplify resilience impacts even without increasing total energy consumption.
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, accepted for Dynamic Data Driven Applications Systems (DDDAS) 6th International Conference

AI.title_translation: 评估日益增长的数据中心时代下的电网韧性
AI.tldr: 本文研究发现，数据中心的爆发式增长和空间集中会严重威胁电网在突发故障下的韧性，大幅增加未供应能量。
AI.motivation: 人工智能工作负载的快速增长导致数据中心规模和需求高度集中，引发了人们对破坏性事件下电力系统韧性的新担忧。
AI.method: 扩展了一个经过验证的多时段直流最优潮流框架，在IEEE 30节点系统上将常规负荷替换为能量匹配的恒定数据中心负荷，并在发电机降额、输电线路降额及耦合降额三种情况下评估了两级容量增长的影响。
AI.result: 在输电受限的故障下，数据中心容量增长大幅增加了系统级和数据中心节点未供应能量。耦合降额时，高增长情况下的总未供应能量从3.203 MWh激增至22.891 MWh；而巧合负荷情况进一步使总未供应能量增加了34.4%。
AI.conclusion: 数据中心的大规模接入和集中式增长显著降低了电力系统在突发故障下的韧性，特别是当面临输电线路受限和巧合负荷叠加时，未供应能量（UE）会急剧增加。
AI.translation: 人工智能工作负载的迅速增长正在增加数据中心需求的规模和集中度，这引发了人们对破坏性事件下电力系统韧性的新担忧。本文扩展了一个经过验证的多时段直流最优潮流框架，以评估聚集的数据中心需求对偶发事件引发的未供应能量的影响。利用带有灵活资源的IEEE 30节点系统，我们将易受偶发事件影响的节点上的传统负荷替换为能量匹配的恒定数据中心负荷，并考察了发电机降额、输电线路降额以及耦合降额情况下的两个容量增长水平。结果表明，数据中心容量的增长大幅增加了输电受限偶发事件下系统级和数据中心节点的未供应能量。在耦合降额下，高增长情况使总未供应能量从能量匹配情况下的3.203 MWh增加到22.891 MWh。补充的能量匹配巧合需求情况进一步使总未供应能量增加了34.4%，这表明即使在不增加总能耗的情况下，时间上集中数据中心需求也会放大对韧性的影响。
AI.summary: 本文利用扩展的直流最优潮流框架，研究了快速增长的数据中心需求对电力系统在故障情况下韧性的影响，发现数据中心的集中和容量增长会显著加剧系统未供应能量。
AI.keywords: 数据中心, 电网韧性, 最优潮流, 突发事件, 未供应能量
AI.comments: 该论文抓住了当前人工智能与数据中心爆发式增长对电网带来的现实挑战，通过扩展直流最优潮流框架，量化评估了数据中心负荷对电力系统韧性的负面影响，具有重要的现实指导意义和前瞻性。

title: On the Assadi Liu Tarjan Auction Algorithm for Bipartite Matching: Simplification, Alternative Analysis, and Hard Instance
comments: ESA 2026 (track S). Fixed bug in proofs in Section 3, fixed typos
summary: Assadi, Liu, and Tarjan [SOSA'21] gave an auction algorithm that outputs a $(1-ε)$-approximation to Maximum Matching in bipartite graphs. Their algorithm computes a sequence of $O(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ maximal matchings in subgraphs of the input graph and can be implemented in the multi-pass streaming setting with $O(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ passes in a straightforward manner, which constitutes the state-of-the-art pass/approximation trade-off result in the multi-pass streaming setting. Their analysis uses tools from combinatorial auctions and, at its heart, relies on a clever potential function argument. Their proof, however, provides only limited insight into the inner workings of the algorithm. In this paper, we revisit the ALT-algorithm and present the following contributions. Simplification: The ALT-algorithm is built upon a freezing mechanism where vertices on one side of the bipartition that have already been rematched $Θ(\frac{1}ε)$ times over the course of the algorithm remain matched to their current partner forever. We show that this mechanism is in fact unnecessary, i.e., no special treatment of such vertices is needed. Alternative Analysis: We give an alternative analysis of the algorithm that is based on augmenting paths. Our analysis allows for a reinterpretation as one that follows the traditional approach of searching for and eliminating augmenting paths. Our analysis also copes with the removal of the freezing mechanism in a natural way, whereas the analysis of Assadi et al. strictly depends on its use. Hard Instance: We provide the first hard instance on which the algorithm requires $Ω(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ iterations/maximal matching computations. The instance is a simple path graph, where we exhibit a cyclic behaviour that prevents fast progress.
comment: ESA 2026 (track S). Fixed bug in proofs in Section 3, fixed typos

AI.title_translation: 论用于二分图匹配的Assadi-Liu-Tarjan拍卖算法：简化、替代分析与困难实例
AI.tldr: 本文对二分图最大匹配的ALT拍卖算法进行了简化，去除了冗余的冻结机制，给出了基于增广路径的新分析，并首次构造了算法的困难实例。
AI.motivation: 尽管Assadi、Liu和Tarjan提出的拍卖算法实现了多遍流模型下最大匹配的最佳权衡，但其原有的基于组合拍卖和势能函数的分析方法复杂且难以提供深入的直观理解。因此，本文旨在简化该算法、提供更直观的分析，并探索其运行下界。
AI.method: 通过理论分析，证明了原算法中“冻结”机制的不必要性，采用基于增广路径的替代分析方法，并构造了特定的路径图作为困难实例来分析算法的最坏情况性能。
AI.result: 证明了“冻结”机制可以被完全移除而无需特殊处理；给出了基于增广路径的替代分析；并首次构造了证明该算法需要 $Ω(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ 次迭代的困难实例。
AI.conclusion: 本文通过简化算法、提供替代分析以及构造困难实例，加深了对ALT二分图匹配拍卖算法的理解。
AI.translation: Assadi、Liu和Tarjan [SOSA'21] 提出了一种拍卖算法，该算法能够输出二分图最大匹配的 $(1-ε)$ 近似解。他们的算法在输入图的子图中计算了一系列 $O(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ 个极大匹配，并且可以通过 $O(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ 趟扫描在多遍流模型中直接实现，这构成了多遍流模型中当前最先进的趟数/近似度权衡结果。他们的分析使用了组合拍卖的工具，其核心依赖于一个巧妙的势能函数论证。然而，他们的证明对算法的内部运作机制提供的洞察有限。在本文中，我们重新审视了ALT算法并做出了以下贡献。简化：ALT算法建立在一种“冻结”机制之上，即在一边中在算法过程中已经被重新匹配 $Θ(\frac{1}ε)$ 次的顶点将永远与当前的伙伴保持匹配。我们证明这种机制实际上是不必要的，即不需要对这些顶点进行特殊处理。替代分析：我们给出了一种基于增广路径的算法替代分析。我们的分析允许将其重新解释为遵循寻找和消除增广路径的传统方法。我们的分析也能自然地处理移除冻结机制的情况，而Assadi等人的分析则严格依赖于该机制的使用。困难实例：我们提供了第一个困难实例，在该实例上算法需要 $Ω(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ 次迭代/极大匹配计算。该实例是一个简单的路径图，我们在其中展示了一种阻止快速进展的循环行为。
AI.summary: 本文重新研究了Assadi、Liu和Tarjan提出的二分图最大匹配拍卖算法（ALT算法）。主要贡献包括：1. 简化了算法，证明了复杂的“冻结”机制是不必要的；2. 提出了基于增广路径的替代分析方法，使算法原理更加直观；3. 首次构造了需要 $Ω(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ 次迭代的困难实例，展示了算法在特定情况下的循环行为。
AI.keywords: 二分图最大匹配, 拍卖算法, 流模型, 增广路径, 近似算法
AI.comments: 本文重新审视了ALT拍卖算法，不仅成功去除了复杂的“冻结”机制，还通过增广路径提供了更加直观的分析方法，并首次给出了该算法的困难实例，展现了极高的理论价值。

title: Triggering Stealthy Feature Map Backdoors via Physical Fault Injection in Embedded Neural Networks
summary: Fault injection (FI) attacks on embedded neural network (NN) implementations primarily focus on inducing misclassification by corrupting weights or intermediate computations, overlooking their interaction with algorithmic adversarial threats. In this work, we present a cross-level attack that bridges implementation-level physical faults to algorithm-level adversarial attacks. By characterizing fault-induced data perturbations during NN inference, we connect FI with backdoor learning, enabling system-level attacks that jointly exploit implementation- and algorithm-level vulnerabilities. Specifically, we propose a precise fault-injection method that reliably manipulates targeted register values to tractable states during execution. Leveraging this level of FI precision, we propose a novel end-to-end feature map-level backdoor attack, where physically induced intermediate perturbations serve as stealthy triggers. Unlike conventional input-based backdoors, our trigger is activated only under physical faults, causing the NN to exhibit adversarial behavior that compromises system integrity while remaining benign during normal operation. We demonstrate that such physically triggered backdoors can be mounted on embedded NN platforms and remain effective against existing backdoor defenses that typically assume input-space triggers. We showcase the attack practicality using electromagnetic FI on convolutional neural networks implemented on ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller, which is a common platform for constrained embedded applications. Our results highlight a novel attack vector at the intersection of hardware and algorithmic levels, stressing the need for defenses across abstraction levels.

title: Conditional Optimal Bridge for Riemannian Activation Steering
summary: Activation steering offers a lightweight alternative to fine-tuning for controlling large language models at inference time. Many existing steering methods implicitly optimize a log-density-ratio objective between desired and undesired activation distributions without a principled derivation. Methods with fixed steering directions can also degrade out-of-distribution (OOD) performance. We introduce Conditional Optimal Bridge for Riemannian Activation Steering (\textsc{Cobras}), which casts steering as a Schrödinger Bridge on the residual-stream hypersphere. This formulation yields a principled derivation of the log-density-ratio steering objective from a well-posed optimization problem. We construct a query-adaptive steering field that recovers log-density-ratio steering as a limiting case. The fitted transport also provides a support score for controlling OOD interventions. Across four models, \textsc{Cobras} outperforms prior steering methods in nearly all model--task settings spanning helpfulness, truthfulness, and detoxification, while largely preserving OOD performance. The code is available \href{https://github.com/arshandalili/cobras}{here}.

title: Flout at Your Own Risk: LLMs Struggle with Pragmatic Cooperativity Under Epistemic Asymmetry
summary: Fruitful collaborations require effective communication of privately-held information. The increasing use of LLMs as "collaborators" raises questions about the extent to which they exhibit these pragmatic capabilities. In this paper, we perform a novel investigation into the pragmatic reasoning capabilities of LLMs in a multiparty collaborative task under partial information conditions. We first formalize a notion of collaborative epistemic asymmetry and prove that fully actionable instructions in this context requires adherence to Grice's cooperative principle. We then empirically assess various LLMs' abilities to act cooperatively as both speakers and listeners, including both prompting and post-training strategies. Our results show that while LLMs exhibit certain pragmatic capabilities in collaborative settings, they still face challenges in pragmatic communication with incomplete information, and that Grice's maxims predict distinct failure modes.

title: Exploring Post-Training Alignment of Small Language Models for Biomedical Data-to-Text Generation: A Case Study of Medication Leaflet
summary: Translating structured biomedical information into accurate, patient-friendly narratives remains a challenging biomedical data-to-text (D2T) task. While small language models (SLMs) are attractive for healthcare applications because of their lower computational cost, easier deployment, and improved data governance, the impact of post-training alignment on biomedical D2T generation has not been systematically studied. In this work, we compare four alignment methods: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), odds ratio preference optimization (ORPO), and group relative policy optimization (GRPO), using Qwen-2.5 models for medication leaflet generation. We further introduce FDALeaflets, a dataset derived from OpenFDA drug labels, to evaluate cross-regulatory generalization in a zero-shot setting. Selected aligned SLMs outperform GPT-5 on several reference-based metrics, whereas GPT-5 achieves better hallucination and adequacy scores on FDALeaflets under LLM-as-judge evaluation. Among RL-free alignment methods, ORPO achieves the best in-domain semantic performance, reaching a semantic textual similarity (STS) score of 0.9752. GRPO achieves the highest FDALeaflets STS (0.9407), exceeding GPT-5 (0.9295). These findings show that post-training alignment is a key factor in improving both semantic fidelity and generalization for biomedical D2T generation, while clinical safety and patient readability require human verification.

title: MARS: Multi-hop Adaptive Retrieval and SPARQL Generation for KGQA
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning performance, but their tendency to hallucinate limits their reliability in knowledge-intensive tasks requiring up-to-date and grounded information. Combining knowledge graphs (KGs) with LLMs facilitates the use of explicit symbolic knowledge that can be continuously updated without costly fine-tuning, while benefiting from rapidly advancing LLM reasoning. We propose MARS, a scalable knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) approach that requires no model fine-tuning. Rather than relying on open-ended agentic exploration, MARS performs a structured retrieval procedure that links question entities to the KG and iteratively retrieves relevant next-hop information. At each step, MARS decides whether to continue graph traversal or to generate the final SPARQL query, allowing the model to adapt the retrieval depth to the question while keeping the overall pipeline more predictable than fully agentic approaches. We evaluate MARS on three established KGQA benchmarks across several LLMs and settings, including multilingual evaluation, and provide insights through ablation studies and error analysis. Our approach achieves competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art methods while remaining efficient and scalable. The evaluation results, code and resources are publicly available: https://github.com/dice-group/mars-kgqa.

title: DFAH-Bench: What Agreement Leaves Unmeasured in Financial Agents
comments: 28 pages, 6 figures; supersedes v3; incorporates the AI4F and SLM-Agents workshop material
summary: When a financial agent repeats its decision, how much does that tell us about the actions behind it? DFAH-Bench examines this question through replay experiments, a controlled test of omitted tool calls, and banking tasks with authorization checks. Across 570 eligible prospective replay episodes, decisions agreed at rates of 94-95%, while tool paths, including inputs and results, agreed at 45-52%; one condition fell one group short of the planned minimum. In a separate 48-execution diagnostic, deleting the same calls from repeated records left agreement perfect. In banking probes, repeated authorization decisions sometimes conflicted with constructed rule labels. The $τ$-Knowledge banking study scheduled 1,080 episodes, with 1,033 known outcomes. Structural checks alone completed more primary tasks than either model-based gate-and-recovery bundle. Input limits and recovery behavior materially shape these results. The typed-choice bundle had lower mean episode cost than the generative bundle on complete task pairs, but fewer successes across the primary schedule under every assignment of unknown outcomes. Missing outcomes prevented the planned confirmatory tests, so the banking comparisons are descriptive. Together, the findings show that agreement alone cannot establish reliability: it can conceal changes in execution, systematic omissions, and unsupported decisions. Evaluation therefore needs to connect what the agent did, the evidence and rules governing its action, and whether it completed the task.

title: Action-Conditioned World Model for Goal Plane Guidance in Robotic Neck Ultrasound
summary: Ultrasound examinations typically follow specific scanning protocols that require navigating through an ordered sequence of anatomical landmarks and target imaging planes. We present a local action-conditioned world model framework for goal plane probe guidance in robotic ultrasound. Autonomous ultrasound tasks often require large numbers of probe-motion trajectories for training, but collecting high-quality demonstrations is labor-intensive and explicit simulators are difficult to build because ultrasound appearance depends on contact, tissue deformation, and view-dependent acoustic artifacts. We address this problem with a two-stage model-based learning pipeline. First, a latent conditional diffusion world model predicts future ultrasound observations from recent context frames, probe motions and temporal offset. Second, a goal-conditioned temporal transformer predicts ordered probe motions and is fine-tuned using rewards from the frozen world model. Experiments on the self-collected dataset show that the world model preserves action-dependent anatomical structure on target-directed scans. In real-world closed loop experiments, the framework achieves success rates of 70.0\% for carotid guidance and 65.0\% for thyroid guidance. These results demonstrate the potential of learned ultrasound dynamics for training goal-directed robotic probe navigation within protocol-constrained organ specific tasks.

title: SIREN (Luring LLMs onto the Rocks): PAIR-Driven Preference Manipulation in Web-RAG Recommenders
summary: This paper investigates the adversarial manipulation of the ranked recommendations produced by web-augmented large language models (LLMs). When an LLM answers a recommendation query by retrieving and reading live webpages, it acts as a recommender, and each retrieved page becomes a potential attack surface. Prior work has examined fabricated products, retrieval poisoning, and rank promotion. However, these studies do not compare how different edits to an already retrieved page change the model's final ranking while the surrounding source set remains unchanged. To address this gap, we propose SIREN, an automated attacker--judge method that adapts the PAIR jailbreaking loop to competitive rank manipulation, with the goal of moving a chosen entity to rank~1 in an LLM-generated recommendation. SIREN retrieves and captures webpages using Anthropic's web tools, then iteratively edits a retrieved source using an interpretable taxonomy of 23 content-poisoning techniques. The custom-RAG replay platform keeps the same sources in the same order, so changes in the model's ranking can be linked to changes in the supplied content rather than to differences in retrieval. Across two production Claude models, SIREN reaches rank~1 in 62 of 124 technique trials nested within eight query--model contexts. The payloads that reached rank~1 were then tested in fresh sessions, where they reproduced the result with a mean success rate of 0.805. Across the evaluated settings, declarative ranking claims and seeded lists were generally more effective than directive-form injections, although the strength of this difference depended on the target model. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first controlled studies of competitive rank manipulation in production LLMs where the supplied source context is kept fixed.

title: DeepLook: Uncertainty-Guided Branching with Lookahead Confidence for Efficient Reasoning
summary: Test-time scaling improves large language model reasoning, but spends compute uniformly along a reasoning trace, even in stretches that are already stable. Motivated by the observation that reasoning failures show an early onset of uncertainty, we introduce DeepLook, a training-free decoding framework that monitors segment-level confidence, branches only at uncertainty bottlenecks, and ranks candidate continuations by Average Lookahead Confidence (ALC)---their mean confidence over fixed-horizon rollouts---before completing and voting over a pruned subset. On four competition mathematics benchmarks across four open models, DeepLook matches or exceeds the accuracy of DeepConf-low in 12 of 16 settings while generating 87.3% fewer tokens, showing that a model's own confidence is informative enough to decide where extra decoding compute is worth spending. On knowledge-intensive GPQA-Diamond the accuracy advantage disappears even though the token saving does not: coherent hallucinations also receive high ALC, so internal confidence localizes instability, not falsehood. Code is available at https://github.com/txyang1/deeplook.

title: The Best Programming Language for Tokenmaxxing: An Investigation of Coding Agent Behavior Across Programming Languages
summary: Although coding agents are now very effective in a variety of programming languages, this paper first shows that the cost (in tokens) can very significantly by programming language. We evaluate five recent models on programming problems in Python, Java, Rust, and OCaml. We carefully control for problem difficulty, and show that there can be stark variation in token consumption that is consistent across models. To understand why, we analyze both the structure and content of agent trajectories. First, we re-execute every intermediate solution and abstract each trajectory as a sequence of test-outcome vectors, then label the work between successive solutions. This reveals agents repeatedly producing noncompiling solutions in unfamiliar languages and revising solutions that already pass. Second, we analyze trajectory text, finding that agents plan solutions in code comments, distrust the provided tests in favor of inputs they invent, and sidestep unfamiliar target languages by prototyping in Python. Our results show that by-language token efficiency is a metric that should be considered when benchmarking and developing multilingual agents, and, for the tokenmaxxer, a guide to the most expensive language to work in.

title: Inverse RL Helps Align AI by Imitating Humans
summary: Language model alignment aims to make model behavior reflect desirable properties such as helpfulness, safety, and instruction following. Existing methods draw supervision from expert demonstrations, preference judgments, or verifiable outcomes. Demonstrations typically guide supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while preference judgments and verifiers provide rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). This raises a question: can the demonstrations alone be used to derive an explicit, interpretable reward useful in a post-training pipeline? Motivated by inverse reinforcement learning, we introduce Projected Alignment Reward Estimated from Demonstrations (PARED). PARED learns an explicit reward from expert demonstrations over a small set of response-level features, using a lightweight discriminator that separates demonstrations from the policy's own samples in this feature space. Experiments with inference-time reranking and adversarial on-policy RL show improvements both when starting from a base model without an SFT stage and when further optimizing an SFT-trained model. Additionally, we demonstrate that PARED can be used for contextual alignment, in which a single policy learns to adapt its responses to the preferences of different audiences.

title: Goal Retrieval versus Action-Value Ordering: Contrastive Critics under Best-of-$K$ Selection
summary: Goal-conditioned action generators can produce many plausible actions. Best-of-\(K\) selection then uses a critic to rank those actions for the current state and goal. Standard contrastive critics are trained and evaluated on a different ranking: distinguishing future goals from unrelated negatives for a fixed state--action pair. The unnormalized contrastive score is monotone in behavior-policy value at the population optimum. Cosine-normalized scores lack this guarantee, and finite trained networks may fail to recover the correct ordering. We audit the resulting gap using shared state--goal queries and frozen candidate pools, so critics differ only in their action ordering. Raw and cosine critics reach retrieval AUCs of \(0.96\)--\(1.00\) across eight OGBench tasks. Their progress ordering on navigation tasks is much weaker and sometimes inverted. In the exact-value controlled problem, all three contrastive selectors have higher mean regret than random selection. Their regret can increase with \(K\). TD-Q stays close to the pool oracle. PointMaze is the only task with a reliable learned value reference. TD-Q gives substantially better fixed-query ordering there, though the differences in executed return are smaller and vary by task. Matched controls suggest that graded value supervision accounts for most of the improvement. Changing score bounds or model capacity alone has much less effect. High retrieval performance does not establish whether a critic ranks actions correctly for best-of-\(K\) selection. That requires a separate action-ordering evaluation before deployment.

title: Green Cell-Free Massive MIMO for ISAC: Joint Cloud, Fronthaul and Radio Resource Allocation
summary: In this paper, we develop a cross-layer end-to-end (E2E) resource orchestration framework for green cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with distributed multi-target detection. We propose a distributed sensing approach in which receive access points (RX-APs) compute local test statistics, which are aggregated at the cloud using weights based on sensing interference and channel quality. We derive the local maximum a posteriori ratio test (MAPRT) detectors under fully informed and partially informed operation, representing different levels of transmit-signal information at the RX-APs. We further characterize their processing and fronthaul requirements and derive a network power model incorporating radio transmission, AP and cloud processing, and fronthaul infrastructure. We formulate a mixed-integer non-convex problem that jointly optimizes transmit powers, AP modes, user equipment (UE) and sensing-area associations, RX-AP assignments, and active fronthaul and cloud resources subject to communication, sensing, power, processing-capacity, and fronthaul constraints. A two-stage iterative algorithm based on Big-M reformulation, convex- concave programming, penalty-based relaxation, and structured discrete recovery is developed. Numerical results show that the proposed E2E framework reduces total power by up to 50% compared with transmit-power-only optimization and by approximately 11-17% compared with joint radio optimization under full coordination, while maintaining detection probabilities above 0:95.

title: What Transfers from Text to Vision? Capability Scaling Laws and Transfer Dynamics for VLMs
summary: Choosing the right large language model (LLM) backbone is the most consequential decision when building a vision-language model (VLM), yet it remains fundamentally unprincipled: compute-based scaling laws fail to generalize across model families, and no framework exists for directly predicting VLM performance before training begins. We propose the Capability-Driven Multimodal Scaling Law, the first cross-family framework that predicts VLM benchmark accuracy from directly observable textual capability. Given a low-dimensional capability score $S$ extracted from LLM textual benchmarks via PCA, we model VLM performance as a function of $S$, with a per-backbone transfer rate and an absorption rate that quantifies data-scaling efficiency. To fit and validate the framework, we train over 150 VLMs on 34 LLMs spanning 7 model families under a strictly controlled recipe. Evaluations on more than 200 textual and 50 multimodal benchmarks show that the law accurately extrapolates transfer rate from models up to 8B parameters to 72B-scale backbones, predicts full VLM training trajectories with high fidelity, and generalizes to entirely held-out model families. Beyond the scaling law, our analysis surfaces actionable insights: certain textual benchmarks negatively correlate with multimodal performance, exposing latent benchmark-gaming behavior; base LLMs outperform instruction-tuned counterparts as VLM backbones due to higher absorption rates and lower data-scaling decay; and different model families occupy distinct positions in the transfer--absorption space. The framework turns backbone selection from costly empirical sweeps into a principled, quantitative decision. Code and data are available at https://github.com/wangq-dev/CDMScaling.

title: Group Perspective Matters: Regulating Debate Relationships Can Mitigate Blind Conformity in Multi-Agent Debate
summary: Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) improves the reasoning performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) through multi-round interaction. However, LLMs in MAD are highly susceptible to blind conformity. Existing individual evaluation methods, typically based on confidence or perplexity, fail to reflect the correctness of reasoning and may even exacerbate blind conformity. To address this, we shift the perspective from individual evaluation to group interaction. We define mutual referencing among LLMs as \textbf{Debate Relationships} and recognize that regulating these relationships is the key to mitigating blind conformity. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for \textbf{D}ynamically r\textbf{E}gulating deb\textbf{A}te \textbf{R}elationships (DEAR) from the group perspective. At first, DEAR quantifies consensus and divergence as \textit{group evidence} to capture the debate state. Then, DEAR operates through three stages: 1) What: perceiving group consultation tendency and uncertainty; 2) Who: introducing a Selection RL-Agent to dynamically select reference peers; and 3) How: adopting a Behavior RL-Agent to adaptively adjust generation behaviors. Notably, we formulate the execution of the two RL-Agents as a sequential decision-making process, jointly optimizing via multi-agent reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DEAR achieves superior performance while significantly reducing token consumption.

title: Analytical Prediction of Equilibrium Existence in Current-Limited Grid-Forming Inverters
comments: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
summary: As converter-interfaced units become dominant in power systems, understanding nonlinear stability phenomena involving discrete switching events becomes essential for secure operation. The limited overcurrent capability of grid-forming (GFM) inverters makes current limiting essential during large disturbances. Activation of a circular current limiter (CCL) can cause the operating equilibrium to disappear under certain circumstances. This paper develops an analytical framework to predict the grid-voltage boundaries for CCL activation and determine whether the operating equilibrium persists or disappears after activation. For CCL-based GFM inverters with frozen anti-windup, closed-form expressions for the activation boundaries are derived while accounting for the filter capacitor. A criterion is established to determine whether a saturated (i.e., current-limited) stable equilibrium point (satSEP) persists following limiter activation. A continuation method is also developed to trace equilibria across normal-control and current-limited operation. Power-angle analysis and dynamic-model continuation in single-inverter and modified 9-bus systems validate these predictions. Time-domain simulations further confirm the results. The results show that CCL activation can either cause immediate loss of the stable equilibrium or allow stable current-limited operation to continue until the equilibrium is lost as operating conditions change further.

title: Large Language Models Can Explain Experts Better Than Experts Themselves
comments: Main text (29 pages) with Supplementary Information appended (29 pages). Supersedes v1
summary: Capturing tacit knowledge, or the "know-how" embedded in individual experiences and contexts, is a central challenge that limits the preservation and transfer of valuable expertise. Traditional methods rely on experts' ability to articulate their own reasoning, even though much of tacit knowledge is difficult to verbalize. Here, we show that Large Language Models (LLMs) can uncover tacit knowledge from expert behavior and support knowledge transfer from experts to novices. We first identify prompting strategies that improve LLMs' ability to externalize tacit knowledge (i.e., transform tacit into explicit knowledge), and then evaluate the downstream utility of the resulting LLM-externalized tacit knowledge. Our analysis reveals that LLM-externalized tacit knowledge incorporating expert behavior improves decision quality and helps reduce the expert-novice score gap, outperforming knowledge articulated by human experts. We further show that LLMs meaningfully learn and extract knowledge from expert behavior rather than simply mimicking expert responses, and that these findings generalize across different LLMs and information retrieval methods. These findings reaffirm Polanyi's Paradox---that "we can know more than we can tell"---and suggest that LLMs can help overcome human experts' articulation bottleneck that has long challenged tacit knowledge externalization.

title: ANTMAN: An Efficient and Interpretable RTL-Level Run-Time Detection Framework for Stealthy Branch Predictor Attacks on BOOM
summary: Runtime detection of microarchitectural side channel attacks remains significantly underexplored in RISCV compared with x86 and ARM ISAs, posing a serious threat to critical applications. State-of-the-art branch predictor attacks bypass traditional data and instruction caches by directly exploiting the state of internal history tables, making them inherently stealthy. Recent research has explored offline detection of microarchitectural attacks on RISC-V; however, efficient runtime detection of microarchitectural attacks on RISC-V hardware remains significantly unaddressed. State-of-the-art hardware-based runtime detection solutions leverage hardware performance counters (HPCs) but suffer from a restricted set of counter registers and tradeoffs between detection accuracy, detection speed, and sampling granularity, making them impractical for stealthy attacks. Moreover, sampling HPCs after distinct intervals leaves intermediate relationships between different microarchitectural blocks unobserved. Additionally, proprietary x86 and ARM ISAs constrain researchers from modifying processor microarchitectural designs. To address these limitations, we propose the first secure-by-design, highly interpretable, non-intrusive, RTL-level runtime detection solution for stealthy branch predictor attacks on BOOM RISC-V, evaluated under both simplified Next-Line Predictor (NLP) and complex TAGE predictor configurations. The attack detection relies on association rules extracted offline and embedded in hardware as a non-intrusive rule monitor that enables runtime detection. The proposed approach achieves excellent detection speed, terminates execution before secret disclosure, and produces zero false positives while remaining flexible for detecting previously unseen variants within the same family of branch predictor attacks.

title: SeFoRA: Sketch-Aggregated Federated Low-Rank Adaptation with Heterogeneous Client Ranks
summary: We consider federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning of foundation models, e.g., LLMs and LVMs, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA; ~Hu et al.\ 2022). Combining LoRA with federated learning introduces challenges absent from either setting alone: clients may use different LoRA ranks, making their factor matrices dimension-incompatible, and factor-wise averaging suffers from a bilinear mismatch. We propose SeFoRA, a sketch-aggregated federated LoRA algorithm in which each client transmits a linear sketch of its local $Δ\mathbf{W}$ updates, enabling direct aggregation at the federator. As a result, SeFoRA overcomes the rank heterogeneity challenge and alleviates the bilinear mismatch. We establish convergence to a neighborhood of a first-order stationary point at rate $\\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$. Extensive numerical experiments on language and vision models showcase the performance of our algorithm compared to existing methods.

title: Small-Scale Experiments: Are We There Yet?
summary: Scaling laws promised cost-effective experiments; six years later, they have yet to fully deliver. Instead, researchers have found them unreliable at small scales (starting at 4M parameters) and concluded that sizable models cannot be avoided. We show this is not the case: the confounding factor is hyperparameters. Small models are highly sensitive, but hyperparameter sensitivity fades with scale. This small-scale sensitivity makes scaling laws easy to miss because they only emerge on the fully tuned frontier, and reaching that frontier requires an extensive search far beyond what most ever run. By ablating the basic scaling law recipe, we show well-tuned hyperparameters matter more than any other ingredient. Further, we reveal why those hyperparameters become easier to find: as scale increases, the hyperparameter loss surface becomes lower dimensional. Nevertheless while scaling laws exist in small models, extrapolation hits statistical limitations. A holistic approach is required. Synthesizing our insights with the recent literature, we develop a new methodology for model-centric research and demonstrate it on a question that once took the field years to settle: where to place normalization layers in the transformer architecture. From small-scale experiments, we recover the large scale result: pre-normalization works better as models grow in size. With the right tools and a better understanding, small-scale experiments can deliver on scaling laws' long-awaited promise.

title: CTBench: Evaluating Troubleshooting Capabilities of AI Agents in Realistic Telecom Network Operations
summary: While autonomous agents show promise for network operations, existing telecom troubleshooting evaluations fail to capture the partial observability and heterogeneity of real-world telecom environments. We introduce CTBench, a public benchmark evaluating agent troubleshooting capabilities in root cause analysis (RCA) and path restoration. Constructed by domain experts, CTBench features rich metadata and golden evidence trajectories, utilizing metrics that assess both final accuracy and diagnostic reasoning. Our evaluation of state-of-the-art agents reveals that while they excel at path endpoint identification, they severely underperform in RCA. Crucially, even when agents produce correct answers, they frequently fail to gather the requisite diagnostic evidence demanded in operational practice. Finally, we demonstrate that increased computational expenditure does not guarantee improved diagnostic competence, highlighting critical gaps in current agent capabilities.

title: Multiobjective Preexpectation Reasoning for Probabilistic Programs
summary: Probabilistic programs with nondeterminism model planning problems in which a strategy typically resolves the nondeterminism to meet a specification. We study the multiobjective setting, meeting several specifications at once along a Pareto front, and provide a deductive, program-level account of strategy synthesis. Its core is a multiobjective preexpectation transformer mapping a tuple of postexpectations to the set of simultaneously achievable values, an element of the convex Hoare powerdomain. It conservatively extends weakest preexpectations and lifts standard loop rules. We develop rules to synthesize witnessing strategies as mixed determinizations that solve nondeterminism probabilistically. We prove the transformer and synthesis rules sound against an operational Markov decision process (MDP) semantics, without requiring a finite state space: our approach can be seen as a symbolic approach - at program level - for multiobjective optimization over infinite MDPs. We demonstrate our machinery using two case studies.

summary: Restricted assignment minimizes makespan, the busiest machine's load, when each job has one size and a set of allowed machines. Its tightest studied relaxation is the configuration linear program, which fractionally gives each machine whole job sets that fit. Its integrality gap, the worst-case ratio of integral optimum to relaxation value, is open in general. On two-weight graph balancing (sizes 1 and 2, each job allowed on at most two machines) the gap is known: Jansen, Land, and Maack (2016) give both bounds. Their Table 1 instance attains 3/2, and their Corollary 11 bound of 2-s/b for sizes s < b matches it at {1,2}. We ask how small such an instance, a witness, can be. We give a six-job witness I* on the complete graph on four machines: unit jobs form a cycle through all four, and two weight-2 jobs take the remaining edges. I* has integral optimum 3 against relaxation value 2, one job fewer than the smallest earlier witness of this class. We prove I* minimum and unique at its size, on any number of machines: no instance with at most five jobs reaches gap 3/2, and at six jobs I* is the only witness, up to relabeling machines and adding unusable machines. At seven jobs uniqueness fails: we classify all thirteen witnesses, including the Jansen-Land-Maack instance. Eight jobs give 154, nine 1,662. At least four machines are necessary. Kartak et al. (2015) classified the extremal non-round-up instances of the same relaxation in one-dimensional cutting stock for small demand; the Discussion relates them. Recognizing witnesses at relaxation value 2, shared by all ours, is coNP-complete, so no min-max characterization with polynomially checkable conditions exists unless NP = coNP. Every feasibility decision behind the exhaustive claims was made twice, in floating-point and exact rational arithmetic, with identical results. We accept the pipeline's negatives only after it rediscovers I*.

title: Toward Safe LLM Agents: A Survey of Specification, Verification, and Enforcement
comments: 37 pages, 2 figures, 11 tables. Revised version under review at ACM Computing Surveys. Data deposit: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23376335. PRISMA 2020 checklist included as an ancillary file
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents take irreversible real-world actions, yet no system gives formally grounded, task-level safety guarantees for their plans. In a PRISMA 2020 systematic review, we searched six databases (20-29 May 2026) for work on LLM agent specification, verification, and enforcement published in 2022-2026. We narratively synthesized 38 studies, assessed risk of bias per study, and graded evidence certainty with GRADE. Three authors independently screened a repeated search to validate the single-reviewer screening (agreement: Fleiss' $κ= 0.81$). First, specification is the bottleneck: on one benchmark, only 24.8-34.2% of LLM translations from natural language into Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) are semantically correct. Second, runtime monitoring is the most mature enforcement strategy; it reduced unsafe actions by 65.37% in one household-agent study, but its guarantees cover only single steps or short horizons. Third, in one $τ$-Bench study of transactional tool-use agents, blocking 94% of unsafe actions still left fewer than 5% of tasks completed both safely and correctly in most settings, because agents found other unsafe routes (the verifier tax). Fourth, no approach simultaneously achieves soundness, completeness, scalability, semantic grounding, and utility preservation. For seven of the nine principal claims, GRADE gives the lowest certainty rating (Very Low), meaning further studies are likely to produce substantially different figures; each rests on one or two studies in narrow domains. Two of the open problems we rank highest are translating requirements into formal specifications that keep their meaning and enforcing safety over whole plans rather than single actions. We contribute a three-level taxonomy and an agenda of ten open problems.

title: Learning reshapes power-law anisotropy in internal representations
summary: Power-law anisotropy in internal representations has been observed across a wide range of biological and artificial neural systems, from state-of-the-art language models to the mouse cerebral cortex. This anisotropy is a key geometric property of high-dimensional information processing and underlies a variety of theoretical analyses. However, the mechanism by which it emerges from input structure and task-driven learning has remained unclear. Here, we characterize this formation process by exactly solving the learning dynamics of a wide two-layer linear neural network in a teacher--student setting with power-law input and teacher structures. We show that, in the feature-learning regime, the local power-law exponent of the internal-representation spectrum evolves nonmonotonically over the course of training and exhibits up to four distinct asymptotic regimes across modes and training times. By contrast, in the lazy regime, the exponent remains essentially unchanged. We further demonstrate numerically that similar exponent dynamics arise in more realistic nonlinear networks. Together, these results suggest a general mechanism by which the dynamic interaction between input statistics and task structure gives rise to power-law internal representations.

title: Dorsal Hand Images for Immersive (XR) and Privacy-preserving Age Assurance and Child Safety
comments: v2: Revised data availability statement; dataset will not be shared. No changes to results
summary: Ensuring that Extended Reality (XR) environments are age-appropriate is an important regulatory and safety challenge. However, current age assurance operates only at registration and cannot verify the age of the active user during a session. Face-based approaches, the dominant solution in social media and adult platforms, are impractical in XR, because they require removing the headset and taking a self-captured image, often on a mobile app. This both breaks immersion and introduces the privacy risk of sharing face pictures with third parties, which leaves XR platforms without a viable path to continuous, in-session and privacy-preserving age assurance. We propose the dorsal part of the hand as an alternative to the face, by exploiting the egocentric cameras that XR headsets inherently and naturally use to capture gesture interactions. To evaluate this, we collect an age- and sex-stratified, ethnodiverse dataset of 436 participants spanning the minor--adult boundary, captured under unconstrained lighting and orientation conditions. To characterise what is achievable with off-the-shelf methods at the minor--adult boundary, we evaluate standard neural network architectures for age assurance at the legally critical 18-year threshold. Analysis confirms performance is robust to skin-tone variation. On this dataset, the challenge-31 operating point achieves zero minor admission, making the system a viable first-stage filter for age assurance. These findings position dorsal hand morphometrics as an effective and more privacy-preserving biometric modality for in-session age assurance in XR.

title: On the Role of Citations in Preference Data
summary: Many NLP tasks require systems to provide attribution in their outputs--i.e. citations to grounding sources. Attribution serves as a bulwark against model hallucination and as a means for users to verify the credibility of model outputs. Yet, it is unclear how humans and LLMs evaluate citations when comparing outputs, a process central to reward modeling and modern LLM post-training. This paper studies the role of citations in the preferences of human judges and four open-source LLMs within the context of scientific question answering, leveraging mixed effects models to investigate the influence of citations on pairwise judgments. Among our key findings are (1) that humans prefer more diverse citations but fewer overall, and (2) that LLMs show some citation-related preferences compared to humans, despite lacking access to the sources, but these preferences depend on the data and specific models. We further discuss the implications of our findings for preference data collection.

title: Language Models Give Group-Linked Fields the Wrong Weight
summary: Large language models are increasingly used to judge people, and their answers can depend on inputs correlated with a protected attribute such as race, even when that attribute is never shown. Interpreting this reliance requires knowing how much predictive information those inputs add, but audits often report only whether a decision changes. We introduce an evidence-referenced audit that compares proxy reliance with two references, the known outcome rule and a Bayesian linear regression fitted to the same labeled examples, while measuring ranking accuracy separately. We apply it to four models in a simulated patient-ranking task with known field weights. We find four results. First, at zero predictive value, the models still relied on fields that carried no information, while the same-example learner did not. Second, as proxies became predictive, reliance grew far less than the reference. Third, display format mattered. Ordered labels drew more reliance than arbitrary labels, a direction that held in all four models. Fourth, ranking accuracy did not consistently track these changes in reliance. Based on these findings, we argue that decision changes and accuracy cannot show whether proxy reliance is warranted by the evidence. Audits should report reliance against an explicit predictive reference, alongside accuracy. Ordered fields whose values move with group membership, such as scores or income bands, are a useful starting point. Together, these results make it possible to measure how far reliance departs from the evidence, rather than infer it from observed choices alone.

title: Hierarchical Exponential-Gaussian Mixtures for Watch-Time Distribution Prediction
comments: 16 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables, accepted at IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM 2026)
summary: Accurate watch-time (WT) prediction is an important requirement for short-video recommendations. Yet WT distributions are near-zero-inflated, long-tailed and multimodal. The recent Exponential-Gaussian Mixture Network (EGMN) models the full conditional WT distribution rather than a single point estimate and achieves state-of-the-art performance. Our large-scale reproduction study reveals that EGMN is vulnerable to variance collapse, component redundancy, and inactive components. We propose a Hierarchical Exponential-Gaussian Mixture (HEGM) model that addresses these failure modes through a hierarchical skip-watch decomposition, structured initialization, removal of the forced Gaussian shift and entropy regularizer and optional KL-based variance regularization for over-parameterized mixtures. Across large-scale industrial and public datasets, under a fixed-backbone head-replacement protocol, HEGM improves ranking accuracy and threshold-event prediction over reproducible lightweight baselines, while maintaining competitive point-estimation accuracy and substantially improving mixture stability and interpretability. A 1.5-month production A/B test confirms statistically significant engagement lifts. Our code and models are publicly released at https://github.com/rw404/HEGM.

title: From Atomic to Agentic: Towards Interpretable Evaluation of LLMs' Agentic Mathematical Capabilities
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are evolving from performing end-to-end mathematical reasoning to integrating agentic intelligence. However, most existing math benchmarks evaluate only final answers. This outcome-oriented evaluation provides limited diagnostic value for identifying process-level failures or rigorous logic, failing to guide the transformation of LLMs into robust agents. To bridge this gap, we present a process-level benchmark designed to evaluate the inherent agentic mathematical reasoning abilities of LLMs. Our framework aligns problem-solving agentic behaviors with a structured taxonomy of reusable mathematical atomic capabilities. We design a comprehensive suite of planning, action, and feedback tasks across both textual and multimodal contexts, supported by an automated pipeline that synthesizes high-quality trajectories and produces fine-grained annotations via controlled LLM rewriting. Experiments reveal that models with similar end-to-end accuracy can exhibit markedly different agentic capability profiles. This demonstrates that process-level evaluation is crucial for interpreting the true potential of LLMs and guiding the development of next-generation mathematical agents.

title: Euclidean Fourier Neural Operators
summary: Fourier neural operators (FNOs) provide an efficient framework for learning mappings between function spaces as they are, by construction, independent of the grid resolution at which they are trained and evaluated. However, FNOs are not independent of the periodic domain they are applied to: their discrete spectral weights are indexed by integer Fourier mode numbers, which correspond to physical wavevectors. When applied to a different domain, the same trained weights act at different wavevectors, and the FNO silently represents a different operator. This makes FNOs unsuitable for tasks where transfer across domains is crucial. We propose Euclidean Fourier neural operators~(EFNOs) as a domain-independent alternative to FNOs. By parameterizing the spectral kernel as a continuous function of the physical wavevector, the EFNO can learn operators that act consistently across periodic domains of varying shape and size. We evaluate the EFNO on a simple heat equation and on a practically relevant materials science task of learning exchange-correlation potentials across different crystal structures, and demonstrate that the EFNO is able to generalize to unseen grid sizes and domains.

title: CPR for LLMs: Critical-Point Routing against Catastrophic Forgetting in Domain Adaptation
summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is the de facto standard for adapting large language models (LLMs) to target domains, but it often degrades the model's general capabilities, a phenomenon known as catastrophic forgetting. Existing approaches typically modify the SFT loss to mitigate forgetting, but they inevitably operate along a domain-generality trade-off. In this work, we step outside this trade-off by decoupling the two capabilities at the model level: we keep the original base model for general capability, and selectively invoke the SFT expert only when domain-specific knowledge is required. Specifically, we propose CPR (Critical-Point Routing), a token-level routing framework between a base model and its expert derivative, based on critical tokens where the base model fails but the expert succeeds. We train a lightweight hierarchical router that estimates the expert-call probability per token, and pair it with a tailored inference procedure that combines momentum smoothing and threshold gating. Across diverse model-domain configurations, CPR achieves state-of-the-art across all settings, surpassing SFT expert by 1.4-5.5% in domain performance while recovering its general-capability drop from 3.4-14.5% to at most 0.5%, with minimal overhead from invoking the expert on only one-third of tokens.

title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Know Physics? Contamination, Units, and the Deterministic Limit
comments: 5 pages (4 figures, 1 table), plus appendix. Accepted at the Representations for the Physical Sciences Workshop @ NeurIPS 2026
summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) learn to fill in tables the way language models fill in text --- and tables are arguably the format in which most physical measurement arrives. Did they learn any physics in the process? They are Bayesian by construction, so the question is what their prior contains. We probe it directly, evaluating four of them ($\texttt{TabPFN-3}$, $\texttt{TabICLv2}$, $\texttt{TabDPT}$ and $\texttt{Real-TabPFN-2.5}$) against six baselines on datasets sampled from 316 physical equations, in and out of domain. TFMs dominate, out of the box and after tuning. But they struggle to represent noiseless deterministic mechanisms in their uncertainty, and show no sign of exploiting physical units: they interpolate physics without yet being able to act as physical models.

title: Carbon-aware Resource Management for Latency-Sensitive Cloud Computing Environments: A Taxonomy and Future Directions
summary: The proliferation of cloud-based latency-sensitive workloads, such as autonomous driving, real-time healthcare services, industrial automation, immersive interactive services, and intelligent AI-based applications requires infrastructures tuned to meet stringent latency constraints. Today, these workloads are reshaping the cloud from a general-purpose computing platform into a diverse ecosystem of workload-specific cloud environments. As demand for latency-sensitive workloads grows, cloud providers must scale their infrastructures accordingly, adversely increasing the carbon footprint and challenging net-zero goals. However, the strict performance requirements and rigid deployment patterns used to satisfy latency Service Level Objectives (SLOs) constrains conventional carbon optimization. Therefore, novel carbon-aware techniques are needed to exploit application-specific opportunities for reducing both operational and embodied carbon footprints while preserving latency guarantees. This survey examines carbon-aware resource management for latency-sensitive cloud computing environments. We introduce a holistic taxonomy that organizes existing techniques by carbon management objective, workload management mechanism, control architecture, system tier, latency requirements, and deployment stage. Then, we use this taxonomy to classify and critically analyze existing approaches, revealing the interactions and trade-offs between latency guarantees and operational and embodied carbon reduction. Finally, we identify limitations in the literature and present a structured research agenda for the design of sustainable latency-sensitive cloud systems.

title: The 11/6 supremum of the Wang-Sitters rounding scheme for graph balancing
comments: 43 pages, 9 figures. v3: the beta < 1/2 seven-machine witness is certified in exact rational arithmetic; the strict-rule endpoint at beta = 1/2 is argued in full; the computational status cites the companion's NP-hardness of best-matching selection for a supplied fractional solution; smaller corrections. Companion to arXiv:2609.10004. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/SKX86
summary: Wang and Sitters' 11/6-approximation for graph balancing (each job allowed on at most two machines) is not one algorithm but a set of permitted executions. Step 1 may return any feasible solution of the fractional relaxation. Step 3 may match remaining jobs to the rounding's slots in many ways. We determine exactly what that latitude permits: ratios arbitrarily close to 11/6, none reaching it, so 11/6 is the least constant bounding every permitted run. We then determine the worst-case guarantee, against the optimum itself, as a function of the big-job threshold beta, the fractional share at or above which Step 2 assigns a job. On Wang and Sitters' own range 1/2 < beta < 1 the guarantee is exactly max{3/2 + beta/2, 5/2 - beta}. We extend the same eligibility rule to 0 < beta <= 1/2, outside the range they state. There a big job's two shares can both reach the threshold, so Step 2 acquires a third choice. We determine it too: exactly 3/2 + (1-beta)floor(1/beta), hence unbounded as beta falls. The worst-case ratio is therefore known at every threshold in (0,1), and attained at none. Consequently 2/3 is the unique optimal threshold, and the guarantee jumps at one half and again at every threshold 1/k below it, rather than degrading smoothly. A companion note examines changes that leave the constant unchanged.

title: Interface-Induced Trajectory Censoring
comments: 39 pages, 14 pages main text. Code, data, and pre-registrations: https://github.com/nebula-1999/Interface-Induced-Trajectory-Censoring
summary:
Agent evaluations report a tool-call rate read off the serving stack. That number can be zero while the model is emitting well-formed calls: the interface censors the trajectory before anything downstream sees it.
  On BFCL v4's own data, executor and scorer, holding weights, cases, decoding and seeds fixed and changing only the serving adapter, the same model scores 0.00 or 0.96 / 0.19. A 2x2 over chat template and parser locates the effect exactly: both main effects are exactly zero and all of it sits in the interaction -- no component is defective, and repairing one side of the contract buys precisely nothing. On tau-bench's 115 interactive retail tasks the same swap moves server-parsed calls from 0 to 636 and tasks reaching any tool execution from 0 to 103. Our probe reproduces the funnel across a 21x scale range of Qwen2.5-Coder: the server parses 0/100 at every size while well-formed emitted calls rise to 80/100 at 32B (~72 after calibration against an adjudicated gold standard). Under a matched envelope, across a comparable scale span, the silent fraction stays at 0-2, a prediction committed to the repository before the run. Llama-3.1-8B's 23% rate of calling the task function itself as a tool falls to 0 under one strict:true flag.
  The mismatch reaches inside the training loop, and its consequence is scale-dependent: in verl's AgentLoop at 7B, 45 of 115 generations carry a complete call; 0 are accepted, 0 execute, 0 return an observation. At 1.5B the same zero is over-determined, so we report the two scales separately. At evaluation time, repairing the adapter restores the mechanism but not a significant outcome gain: parsing 0->84, rescues 0->9, pass rate 53->62 (n.s.). We release a 98-line preflight check that catches every silent failure here. The observed tool-call rate is not a property of the model alone; it is a property of the model-interface stack that measures it.
